issues.title: A list index known only at run time fails the query when it is negative, for a list read from a property or indexed by a parameter, and answers the element as text
issues.block: ### A list index known only at run time fails the query when it is negative, for a list read from a property or indexed by a parameter, and answers the element as text Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: List indexing does not correctly handle negative indexes supplied through runtime data or parameters. Valid queries can fail, and nonnegative reads from stored lists can return text instead of the original value type. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 47) Found by: the frozen W54 prediction L2 missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-PAIRS.md)); narrowed by [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) item 2 (a WITH-held literal list answers correctly); [cypher_fns](models/cypher_fns/NOTES.md) `theorem_row_negative_index_fails` and `theorem_param_negative_index_fails` with neighbors `theorem_with_literal_row_index_follows_rule`, `theorem_literal_index_follows_rule`, `theorem_row_nonnegative_index_follows_rule` and `theorem_ivglistget_is_rule`; controls `row-index-through-ivglistget`, `with-literal-elem-unwrapped`, `with-literal-elem-untyped`, `literal-negative-unwrapped`, `ivglistget-no-wrap`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([iteration-47 observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-observed2-20261117T015618Z.json) `I_row_*`, `I_param_neg`, `I_with_list_neg`; iteration 50: [fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `idx_*`, [binding](results/cypher_fns/20261117T033050Z-binding/receipt.json) `index___`, 63 cases over three list sources). Over a stored `n.l = [1, 2, 3]`, `UNWIND [-1] AS i RETURN n.l[i]` (and -3, -4) fails with `-149 ... JSON_ARRAYGET ... `; `WITH n.l AS l UNWIND [-1] AS i RETURN l[i]` fails `` in `JSON_VALUE`; `n.l[$i]` fails "Incorrect number of parameters" for every value; `WITH [1, 2, 3] AS l RETURN l[$i]` with `$i = -1` fails ``. A non-negative run-time index into a list from a property answers text: `UNWIND [0] AS i RETURN n.l[i]` answers `'1'` where `n.l[0]` answers 1. Passing neighbors: a WITH-held literal list read by a row index follows the rule with the element's type (`WITH [1, 2, 3] AS l UNWIND [-1] AS i RETURN l[i]` answers the integer 3, review item 2); every literal index; `CypherFn_IVGLISTGET('[1,2,3]', '-1')` answers 3. Expected: openCypher (TCK `List1`): a negative index counts from the end, an index past either end is null, and the element keeps its type. The translator already wraps a literal negative index (4.6.0 R267) and a row index into a WITH-held literal list (R308, `CY_LIST_ELEM`). Observed: `_expr_subscript` decides by the list's source and the index's syntax (`translator.py:23509-23656`). A property read takes `JSON_ARRAYGET(l, CAST(i AS INTEGER))`; another WITH column takes `JSON_VALUE(l, '$.' || i)`; a parameter index is inlined into `JSON_ARRAYGET` for a WITH column and left as a marker IRIS refuses on a property read. `Graph_KG.JSON_ARRAYGET` and `JSON_VALUE` are `%Get(i)` (`schema.py:2179-2184`), which raises `` below 0 and answers text. Only a row index into a WITH-held literal list reaches `CY_LIST_ELEM` (`_is_row_list_elem`, `translator.py:7681-7732`). Consequence: a query that indexes a stored list with a computed or unwound negative index, or any list with a negative parameter, returns nothing and an error; with a non-negative index into a stored list the value comes back as a string. Medium. Repair proposal (not implemented): emit `CY_LIST_ELEM` (typed, wraps negatives) for every run-time index, whatever the list's source, and compute a parameter index in Python as R311 does for literals. Preserve: literal indexes, the WITH-literal path, null past either end, and a null index giving null (today it does not: [bug-cyp-126](#bug-cyp-126)). Writers and readers affected: the `RETURN`/`WITH` columns that read an element, and `CY_LIST_ELEM`'s callers. Distinguishing case: `MATCH (n) UNWIND [-1] AS i RETURN n.l[i]` answers 3 while `WITH [1, 2, 3] AS l UNWIND [-1] AS i RETURN l[i]` still answers 3. The control `row-index-through-ivglistget` checks the repaired rule in the model only. Governing statement: [query.functions.list_index](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.list_index). Iteration 55: a list parameter indexed by a parameter, `RETURN $l[$s]` with `l = [1, 2, 3, 4]` and `s = 1`, answers the text `'2'` with IRIS driver 5.4.1 (the index is inlined into `JSON_ARRAYGET`) and fails with 5.3.2 ([5.4.1](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-params-5.4.1-observed-20261117T061233Z.json), [5.3.2](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-params-5.3.2-observed-20261117T061226Z.json) `PA4_index`). Same decision, a new list source; not a new entry.

issues.title: reverse() of a list held in a property, a slice, a subscript or a coalesce reverses its JSON text, and of a WITH column from a property answers the JSON text
issues.block: ### reverse() of a list held in a property, a slice, a subscript or a coalesce reverses its JSON text, and of a WITH column from a property answers the JSON text Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Reversing a stored or computed list can reverse its serialized text instead of its elements. The result is an incorrect value rather than the reversed list the query requested. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 47) Found by: the frozen W54 prediction L1 missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-PAIRS.md)); widened by [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) item 3 (slice, subscript, coalesce, and the Variable case the model mispredicted); [cypher_fns](models/cypher_fns/NOTES.md) `theorem_stored_list_reversed_as_text`, `theorem_unknown_list_variable_answered_as_text`, neighbor `theorem_reverse_neighbors`; controls `property-to-cy-reverse`, `reverse-column-typed`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([iteration-47 observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-observed-20261117T015433Z.json) `L1_list`, `L1_empty`; iteration 50: [fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `rev_*`, [binding](results/cypher_fns/20261117T033050Z-binding/receipt.json) `reverse_*`, eleven argument forms). For a Cypher-written `n.l = [1, 2, 3]`: `reverse(n.l)` and `reverse(coalesce(n.l, []))` answer the string `']3 ,2 ,1['`; `WITH [1, 2, 3] AS l RETURN reverse(l[0..3])` answers `']3,2,1['`; `WITH [[1, 2, 3], [4]] AS l RETURN reverse(l[0])` answers `']3,2,1['`; `WITH n.l AS l RETURN reverse(l)` answers the string `'[3,2,1]'` (reversed, but as text). Passing neighbors: `reverse([1, 2, 3])`, `WITH [1, 2, 3] AS l RETURN reverse(l)`, `reverse(n.l + [])`, `reverse(tail(n.l))` and `reverse(CASE WHEN 1 = 1 THEN [1, 2, 3] END)` answer lists; `reverse(n.str)` of `'gotcha'` answers `'ahctog'`. Expected: openCypher: `reverse()` of a list is the list in reverse order; of a string, the reversed string. Observed: two decisions. `_scalar_string` sends only list literals, comprehensions, list-valued calls (by `_container_kind`), variables and `CASE` to `CY_REVERSE`; a property read, a slice, a subscript or another call goes to SQL `REVERSE()`, which reverses the text (`translator.py:24495-24513`). And `CY_REVERSE`'s JSON answer is decoded into a list only for a column the translator knows to be a list, so a variable from a property comes back as JSON text. Consequence: wrong values for a common list operation on stored data. Medium. Repair proposal (not implemented): send every non-literal argument to `CY_REVERSE`, which already reverses a JSON array or a string by its run-time value, and mark the column for decoding by the value's run-time kind. A stored string that spells a list would then reverse as the list (the documented known issue). Preserve: string arguments and the list forms that work today. Distinguishing case: `WITH n.l AS l RETURN reverse(l)` answers `[3, 2, 1]` and `reverse(n.str)` still `'ahctog'`. Controls `property-to-cy-reverse` and `reverse-column-typed` check the two halves in the model only. Governing statement: [query.functions.reverse](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.reverse).

issues.title: n[k] with a key from UNWIND reads the property named "k", so keys(n) then n[k] answers null for every key
issues.block: ### n[k] with a key from UNWIND reads the property named "k", so keys(n) then n[k] answers null for every key Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: A dynamic property lookup can use the variable's name instead of its value. Iterating over a node's keys can therefore return null or read a different property. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 47) Found by: the frozen W54 prediction L7 missed, then source reading ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-PAIRS.md)); [cypher_fns](models/cypher_fns/NOTES.md) `theorem_row_key_reads_variable_name`, neighbor `theorem_param_key_follows_rule`, control `row-key-by-value`; the WITH-column failure (already in this entry's evidence) gained `theorem_with_column_key_fails` and control `with-key-by-value` in iteration 50 ([review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) m5; [binding](results/cypher_fns/20261117T033050Z-binding/receipt.json) `node_with_key`, [fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `key_from_with_column`). Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-observed2-20261117T015618Z.json) `N_row_key`, `N_with_key`; [idiom](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-observed3-20261117T020020Z.json) `keys_idiom`; [binding](results/cypher_fns/20261117T015955Z-binding/receipt.json) `node_row_key`). A node with `k: 'gotcha'`, `num: 5`: `UNWIND ['num', 'str', 'zz'] AS k RETURN k, n[k]` answers `'gotcha'` on every row; `MATCH (n) UNWIND keys(n) AS k RETURN k, n[k]` answers null for every key; `WITH n, 'str' AS k RETURN n[k]` raises "Non-integer index type for list subscript". Passing neighbor: `n[$k]` with `$k = 'num'` answers 5. Expected: openCypher: `n[k]` is the property whose name is `k`'s value. Observed: for a `Variable` index on a node, `_expr_subscript` binds `context.input_params.get(idx.name, idx.name)`, so a variable that is not a parameter becomes its own name as the key of the `rdf_props` join (`translator.py:23533-23541`). A node carried through `WITH` is a stage column, so `n[k]` takes the scalar branch, where a key known to be a string raises "Non-integer index type for list subscript" (`translator.py:23583-23610`). Consequence: dynamic property reads silently answer another property or null. Medium: wrong values with no error. Repair proposal (not implemented): translate the index expression for a variable that is not a parameter, as for other expressions. Governing statement: [query.functions.dynamic_access](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.dynamic_access).

issues.title: randomUUID() and rand() give one value for every row of a query, and a CREATE that uses one is refused
issues.block: ### randomUUID() and rand() give one value for every row of a query, and a CREATE that uses one is refused Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Random-number and UUID functions return one shared value across a query's rows, and using them in CREATE can fail. Applications cannot rely on them to generate a distinct value for each new node. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 47) Found by: the frozen W54 prediction L12 missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-PAIRS.md)); [cypher_fns](models/cypher_fns/NOTES.md) `theorem_rows_share_one_value` (conditional on the observed IRIS premise), control `per-row-evaluation`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-observed2-20261117T015618Z.json) `R_return`, `R_collect`, `R_create_*`; [CREATE neighbors](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-observed3-20261117T020020Z.json); [binding](results/cypher_fns/20261117T015955Z-binding/receipt.json) `uuid_distinct_over_5`, `rand_distinct_over_5`). `UNWIND [1, 2, 3] AS i RETURN randomUUID(), rand()` answers the same UUID and the same float on all three rows; `UNWIND range(1, 50) AS i WITH randomUUID() AS u RETURN count(DISTINCT u)` answers 1. `CREATE (:X {u: randomUUID()})`, with or without `UNWIND`, fails "nothing written: Cannot write argument in list"; the same `UNWIND ... CREATE` with `u: 'x'` writes three nodes. Other functions inside a `CREATE` map were not checked. Expected: openCypher: each call of `randomUUID()` returns a new UUID and `rand()` a new number. Observed: the translator emits `Graph_KG.NEWID()` and `Graph_KG.RAND()`, calls without a row argument (`translator.py:26919-26924`; `schema.py:2321, 2324`); IRIS 2026.1 evaluates each once per statement. The write refusal was traced in iteration 48: [bug-cyp-119](#bug-cyp-119) (any function the Python constant folder does not work out). Consequence: generated identifiers repeat across rows of a read, and cannot be generated in a `CREATE` at all. Medium. Repair proposal (not implemented): pass a row-dependent argument (or declare the functions non-deterministic) so IRIS evaluates them per row, and accept a function value in a `CREATE` map. Governing statement: [query.functions.random](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.random).

issues.title: A map value read by a key answers numbers and booleans as text
issues.block: ### A map value read by a key answers numbers and booleans as text Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Reading a map entry by key returns numeric and boolean values as text. Subsequent comparisons and arithmetic can therefore operate on the wrong type. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 47) Found by: the frozen W54 prediction L7 missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-PAIRS.md)). No formal contract: probe only, open in Verus. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-observed2-20261117T015618Z.json) `M_rows_types`, `M_literal_key`). `WITH {a: 1, b: 2.5, c: true, d: [1]} AS m UNWIND ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'] AS k RETURN k, m[k]` answers `'1'`, `'2.5'`, `'1'`, `'[1]'`; `m['a']` answers `'1'` and `m.c` answers 1 for `true`. A missing key answers null, as expected. `WITH $m AS m RETURN m[$k]` fails "Incorrect number of parameters". Expected: openCypher: the map's value with its type. Observed: a string or variable key becomes `JSON_VALUE(m, '$.' || key)`, which answers text (`translator.py:23565-23575, 23638-23639`). Related documented issue: a property of a map in a parameter list reads a boolean as 1 (KNOWN_ISSUES). Consequence: comparisons and arithmetic on such values see strings. Low. Governing statement: [query.functions.dynamic_access](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.dynamic_access).

issues.title: head() of a number fails with an error that does not name TypeError
issues.block: ### head() of a number fails with an error that does not name TypeError Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Calling head on a number fails without identifying the problem as a type error. Clients cannot reliably distinguish invalid input from another execution failure. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 47) Found by: the frozen W54 prediction L11 partly missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-PAIRS.md)). No formal contract: probe only. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/cypherfn-observed2-20261117T015618Z.json) `T_head_number_msg`, `T_head_number_literal`). `head(n.num)` of a stored 5, `n.num[0]` and `head(n.str)` fail with `CY_LIST_ELEM failed ... %msg=` (empty); `RETURN head(5)` with `JSON_ARRAYGET failed ... %msg=`. Expected: the 4.6.0 CHANGELOG: a type error on a row fails with IRIS's error text "which contains the openCypher name" (`TypeError`), so a caller can test for it with `in`. Observed: the list element functions raise without a message (`schema.py:2300`, `2179`). Consequence: callers cannot tell a type error from another failure. Low. Governing statement: [query.functions](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions).

issues.title: A negative list-slice bound known only at run time counts as 0
issues.block: ### A negative list-slice bound known only at run time counts as 0 Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: A negative list-slice bound supplied at runtime is treated as zero. Slices calculated from stored data or parameters can silently select the wrong elements. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 48) Found by: the frozen W55 prediction L1 missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-PAIRS.md)); [cypher_exprs](models/cypher_exprs/NOTES.md) `theorem_row_negative_slice_departs` with neighbors `theorem_literal_slice_follows_rule` and `theorem_row_nonnegative_slice_follows_rule`; controls `row-slice-wrapped`, `literal-slice-unwrapped`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed-20261117T021241Z.json) `L1_rows`, `L1_param`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed2-20261117T021350Z.json) `F3_*`; [binding](results/cypher_exprs/20261117T022154Z-binding/receipt.json) `slice_row_*`, `slice_param_*`, `slice_literal_*`). Over a stored `n.l = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`, `UNWIND [[-3, -1]] AS ab RETURN n.l[ab[0]..ab[1]]` answers `[]` (rule `[3, 4]`), `[-3, 5]` answers the whole list (rule `[3, 4, 5]`), `[0, -1]` answers `[]` (rule `[1, 2, 3, 4]`); parameters `n.l[$a..$b]` behave the same, and so does a list the query holds (`WITH [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] AS l`). Passing neighbors: the same bounds written in the query (`n.l[-3..-1]` is `[3, 4]`), and every non-negative run-time bound. Expected: openCypher (TCK `List2` [6], [8]): a negative bound counts from the end; bounds are clamped to the list. Observed: `_expr_slice` wraps a literal negative bound as `GREATEST(0, JSON_ARRAYLENGTH(l) + n)` and passes any other bound as it is into `rn > (start) AND rn <= (end)` (`translator.py:23741-23772`), so a negative run-time start keeps every row and a negative run-time end keeps none. Consequence: a slice computed from data (`l[-k..]`, `l[..-1]` with a parameter) silently answers the wrong elements. Medium. Repair proposal (not implemented): give a run-time bound the same wrap in SQL (`CASE WHEN b < 0 THEN GREATEST(0, len + b) ELSE b END`); preserve literal bounds and null bounds. The control `row-slice-wrapped` checks the repaired rule in the model only (the non-negative neighbor stays verified); see [one run-time path for list positions](design_simplification.md#simp-cyp-101). Governing statement: [query.functions.slice](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.slice).

issues.title: A boolean known only at run time cannot be a CASE WHEN or WHERE condition
issues.block: ### A boolean known only at run time cannot be a CASE WHEN or WHERE condition Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: A boolean obtained from a parameter or computation cannot reliably be used as a WHERE or CASE condition. A valid query can fail instead of filtering or choosing a branch. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 48) Found by: the frozen W55 prediction C4 missed for its `UNWIND` half ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-PAIRS.md)); [cypher_exprs](models/cypher_exprs/NOTES.md) `theorem_row_boolean_condition_fails` (conditional on the observed IRIS premise) with neighbor `theorem_predicate_condition_follows_rule`; controls `row-condition-compared`, `property-condition-raw`, `iris-accepts-scalar-condition`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed-20261117T021241Z.json) `C4_unwind`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed2-20261117T021350Z.json) `F6_*`; [binding](results/cypher_exprs/20261117T022154Z-binding/receipt.json) `cond_*`, `where_RowVar_*`). `UNWIND [true, false] AS f RETURN CASE WHEN f THEN 'y' ELSE 'n' END`, `WITH true AS f RETURN CASE WHEN f ...`, `RETURN CASE WHEN $f ...` and `UNWIND [true, false] AS f WITH f WHERE f RETURN f` each fail at Prepare with SQLCODE -14 "A comparison operator is required here". Passing neighbors: a stored boolean property (`CASE WHEN n.flag`), a literal, `f = true`, `NOT f`, `f AND true` and the simple `CASE f WHEN true`. Expected: openCypher: any boolean expression is a condition; `CASE WHEN b` takes the branch when `b` is true. Observed: `_translate_boolean_expression` turns a literal, a property read, a map access and a comparison into predicates, but returns the SQL of a bare variable or parameter as it is (`translator.py:18688-18716`); IRIS 2026.1 refuses a scalar in a predicate position. The known issue "A boolean property of a map row reads as false in a CASE WHEN" is a neighbor (`input.fixed`), not this shape. Consequence: a query that branches or filters on a computed or passed-in flag fails outright. Medium. Repair proposal (not implemented): compare a bare row or parameter boolean as `= 1` (or route it through `_stored_bool_in`'s JSON-kind test). The control `row-condition-compared` checks the repaired rule in the model only. Governing statement: [query.values.conditions](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values.conditions).

issues.title: A node CREATE whose map value calls a function IVG does not work out in Python is refused
issues.block: ### A node CREATE whose map value calls a function IVG does not work out in Python is refused Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Node creation fails when a property value uses a function the Python translator does not evaluate. Valid writes that generate IDs or calculate values are refused before any data is written. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 48) Found by: the frozen W55 prediction W2 missed (W3 held as the owner predicted) ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-PAIRS.md)); the source reading traced bug-cyp-114's `CREATE` refusal; [cypher_exprs](models/cypher_exprs/NOTES.md) `theorem_unfolded_create_value_refused` with neighbor `theorem_folded_create_value_written`; controls `create-value-translated`, `toupper-not-folded`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed-20261117T021241Z.json) `W2_*`, `W3_*`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed2-20261117T021350Z.json) `F7_*`; [binding](results/cypher_exprs/20261117T022154Z-binding/receipt.json) `create_node_*`, `set_node_*`). `CREATE (:X {id: 'a', v: size('ab')})` fails "execute_cypher failed, nothing written: Cannot write argument in list: unknown list type detected", and so do `abs(-1)`, `toInteger('5')`, `substring('abc', 1)`, `replace('a', 'a', 'b')`, `randomUUID()` and `rand()`, with or without `UNWIND`; no node is written. Passing neighbors: `toUpper('ab')`, `toLower`, `trim`, `coalesce(null, 'x')`, `toString(1)`, `toInteger(2.5)`, `1 + 1` and `toUpper($s)` are stored, and `SET x.v = ` stores the value. Expected: openCypher: a `CREATE` stores each property value its map computes. Observed: `_create_resolve_prop_value` asks `_fold_constant` to work out a function value in Python; the folder handles coalesce, the case and trim functions, `toString`, `toFloat`/`toInteger` of a number and arithmetic, and returns `_NOT_CONSTANT` for anything else, and the function then returns the AST itself (`translator.py:9594-9599`, `9670`), which the node INSERT binds as an argument and the driver refuses. Consequence: a node cannot be created with a generated identifier, a size, an absolute value or a parsed number in one statement; the whole write is refused (nothing partial). Medium. bug-cyp-114 named the `randomUUID()` and `rand()` cases; this is their cause. Repair proposal (not implemented): translate an unfolded value to SQL as `SET` does (control `create-value-translated` checks the repaired rule in the model only); see [one SQL path for computed write values](design_simplification.md#simp-cyp-102). Governing statement: [query.writes.computed_values](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.writes.computed_values).

issues.title: A relationship CREATE between new nodes drops every computed or parameter property value without an error
issues.block: ### A relationship CREATE between new nodes drops every computed or parameter property value without an error Severity: High · Decision: Open Description: Creating a relationship between new nodes silently drops property values supplied through parameters or computed expressions. The command succeeds, but the stored relationship is missing data the caller provided. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 48) Found by: a follow-up to W55's write pairs before the source reading (`F7_rel_fn` in [follow-up 2](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed2-20261117T021350Z.json)), isolated in [follow-up 3](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed3-20261117T021604Z.json); the plain-parameter case by [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) item 5; [cypher_exprs](models/cypher_exprs/NOTES.md) `theorem_inline_rel_expression_dropped` and `theorem_inline_rel_param_dropped` with neighbor `theorem_inline_rel_literal_written`; controls `rel-value-kept`, `rel-param-kept`, `rel-literal-dropped`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed3-20261117T021604Z.json) `toUpper_lit`, `size_lit`, `arith`, `toString_lit`, `uuid`, `param_fn`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed2-20261117T021350Z.json) `F7_rel_*`; iteration 50: [fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `rel_new_param*`, [binding](results/cypher_exprs/20261117T033119Z-binding/receipt.json) `create_rel_*`, `create_rel_matched_*`, `create_node_Param`). `CREATE (:N {id: 'a'})-[:T {v: 1 + 1}]->(:N {id: 'b'})` succeeds and writes both nodes and the relationship, but the relationship has no `v`; the same holds for `toUpper('ab')`, `size('ab')`, `toString(1)`, `randomUUID()`, `toUpper($s)` and a plain parameter: `CREATE (a {id: ...})-[r {k: $k, lit: 1}]->(b {id: ...})` with `$k = 4` stores `keys(r) = ['lit']` and `r.k` null. Passing neighbors: a literal `{v: 'ab'}` and an `UNWIND` literal variable are stored; a node `CREATE` stores `$k`; between matched nodes `$k` and literals are stored, and a computed value is refused with a message naming the property (documented in KNOWN_ISSUES). Expected: openCypher: a `CREATE` stores each property value its map computes or binds; where IVG cannot, it refuses (as it does between matched nodes). Observed: `_create_clause_relationship_entry`, for endpoints known literally, keeps a property value only when it is a Literal or a FOREACH/UNWIND literal variable; any other expression, an `ast.Parameter` included, maps to None, and the next line drops None values as "null props are not stored" (`translator.py:10213-10226`). The multigraph branch receives the same filtered map. Consequence: the write reports success and the property is lost; nothing tells the caller. Drivers send values as parameters, so the ordinary pattern `CREATE (a {id: $a})-[:R {since: $since}]->(b {id: $b})` loses `since`. High (silent data loss on an ordinary `CREATE` pattern). Repair proposal (not implemented): resolve a relationship value as a node value is resolved: bind a parameter as its value, fold or translate a computed value, or refuse naming the property; never drop a non-null value. Preserve: literal and `UNWIND`-literal values, the matched-node refusal until computed values are supported there, and null values not stored. Writers and readers affected: the literal-endpoint fast path and its multigraph branch; every reader of `rdf_edges.qualifiers`. Distinguishing case: `CREATE (:N {id: 'a'})-[:T {k: $k}]->(:N {id: 'b'})` stores `k`. The controls `rel-param-kept` and `rel-value-kept` check the repaired rule in the model only. Governing statement: [query.writes.computed_values](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.writes.computed_values).

issues.title: coalesce over row values, literals or parameters answers numbers and booleans as text
issues.block: ### coalesce over row values, literals or parameters answers numbers and booleans as text Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Coalesce can convert numeric and boolean inputs into text. A fallback value may look correct while later arithmetic or comparisons follow string behavior. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 48) Found by: the frozen W55 prediction C3's literal neighbor missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-PAIRS.md)); [cypher_exprs](models/cypher_exprs/NOTES.md) `theorem_row_coalesce_number_as_text` with neighbor `theorem_node_coalesce_keeps_type`; controls `coalesce-always-typed`, `coalesce-needs-two-props`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed-20261117T021241Z.json) `C3_*`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed2-20261117T021350Z.json) `F5_*`; [binding](results/cypher_exprs/20261117T022154Z-binding/receipt.json) `coalesce_*`). `RETURN coalesce(null, 1)` answers `'1'`, `coalesce(null, 2.5, 'z')` `'2.5'`, `coalesce(null, true, 'z')` `'1'`; `UNWIND [7] AS x RETURN coalesce(x, 'z')` `'7'`; `coalesce($p, 1)` with `$p = 7` `'7'`; `coalesce(n.i, x)` with `x` from `UNWIND` `'7'`. Passing neighbors: `coalesce(n.missing, n.v, 'z')` and `coalesce(n.i, $p)` keep the stored integer. Expected: openCypher (TCK `Conditional1`): `coalesce` returns its first non-null argument unchanged. Observed: `_is_typed_coalesce` reads the winner with its type only when a node property is among node properties, scalar literals and scalar parameters (`translator.py:7620-7642`); otherwise `_scalar_coalesce` CASTs the first argument and later non-string literals to VARCHAR (`translator.py:24455-24472`). Related inherited entry: [bug-cyp-107](#bug-cyp-107) (a relationship property in `coalesce`). Consequence: a defaulted number or flag arrives as a string, and later comparisons or arithmetic on it follow string rules. Low. Governing statement: [query.functions.coalesce](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.coalesce).

issues.title: A list slice whose lower bound is a variable name does not parse
issues.block: ### A list slice whose lower bound is a variable name does not parse Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: A list slice with a variable as its lower bound is rejected by the parser. Callers cannot use that normal parameterization of a slice. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 48) Found by: the W55 probe's own query `n.l[a..3]` failed to parse ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed-20261117T021241Z.json) `L1_rows_scalar`); [cypher_exprs](models/cypher_exprs/NOTES.md) `theorem_identifier_lower_bound_refused` with neighbor `theorem_other_lower_bounds_parse`; control `identifier-lookahead`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed2-20261117T021350Z.json) `F4_*`; [binding](results/cypher_exprs/20261117T022154Z-binding/receipt.json) `parse_*`). `WITH [1, 2, 3] AS l, 1 AS a RETURN l[a..3]` fails "CypherParseError: Expected IDENTIFIER, got FLOAT_LITERAL"; `l[a..b]`, `l[a..]` and `l[a .. 3]` fail "Expected IDENTIFIER, got .". Passing neighbors: `l[1..b]`, `l[$a..3]`, `l[x[0]..3]`. Expected: openCypher: any expression may be a slice bound. Observed: `Parser.parse_primary_expression` reads a `.` after an identifier as a property access and then expects a name (`parser.py:1621-1641`); the postfix loop that serves other bounds looks ahead for `..` and the `.N` float, this branch does not. Consequence: the query is refused (fails loudly); a workaround exists (`l[(a)..3]` was not tested; `l[x[0]..3]` works). Low. Governing statement: [query.functions.slice](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.slice).

issues.title: A negative substring start answers leading characters instead of an error
issues.block: ### A negative substring start answers leading characters instead of an error Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: A negative substring start returns leading characters instead of rejecting the invalid offset. A calculation error can silently produce the wrong text. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 48) Found by: the frozen W55 prediction S2 partly missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-PAIRS.md)); [cypher_exprs](models/cypher_exprs/NOTES.md) `theorem_negative_start_answers_prefix` with neighbor `theorem_inside_substring_follows_rule`; controls `substring-checks-start`, `substring-zero-based`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed-20261117T021241Z.json) `S2_neg_*`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed2-20261117T021350Z.json) `F1_*`, `F2_neg`; [binding](results/cypher_exprs/20261117T022154Z-binding/receipt.json) `substring_*`). `substring('hello', -1, 2)` and `substring(n.s, a, 2)` with `a = -1` from `UNWIND` answer `'h'`, `a = -3` answers `''`; `substring('hello', 1, -1)` fails SQLCODE -400 ``, a fatal IRIS error naming no Cypher error; `left(n.s, -1)` answers null. Literal and run-time arguments behave alike here. Passing neighbors: every start and length inside the string. Expected: the Cypher 9 function reference: a negative start or length raises an error (openCypher's TCK does not pin it). Observed: `_scalar_string` emits `SUBSTRING(s, (start) + 1, len)` with no check (`translator.py:24488-24494`); IRIS takes positions below 1 as the string's start. Consequence: a computed negative offset silently answers a different substring. Low. Governing statement: [query.functions.strings](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.strings).

issues.title: A zero-length left, right or substring answers null instead of the empty string
issues.block: ### A zero-length left, right or substring answers null instead of the empty string Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Requesting a zero-length string segment returns null rather than an empty string. Missing-value tests and fallback expressions can then treat a valid empty result as absent data. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 48) Found by: the frozen W55 prediction S3 partly missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-PAIRS.md)). No formal contract: probe only (open in Verus). Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed-20261117T021241Z.json) `S3_*`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-48/cypherexpr-observed2-20261117T021350Z.json) `F2_*`). `left('hello', 0)`, `right('hello', 0)`, `left(n.s, 0)`, `substring('hello', 2, 0)` and `substring(n.s, 1, 0)` answer null, for literal and run-time arguments; `substring('hello', 0, 0)` answers `''`. Passing neighbors: every length of 1 or more. Expected: openCypher: an empty result is the empty string, not null. Observed: the SQL functions answer IRIS's empty string, which SQL reads as null; not traced further. Consequence: `IS NULL` tests and `coalesce` treat an empty prefix as missing. Low. Governing statement: [query.functions.strings](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.strings).

issues.title: With the driver 5.3.2 an UNWIND of a list parameter fails "Invalid number of parameters"
issues.block: ### With the driver 5.3.2 an UNWIND of a list parameter fails "Invalid number of parameters" Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: With IRIS driver 5.3.2, expanding a list parameter using UNWIND fails with a parameter-count error. Whether that driver version is supported remains unresolved, so the compatibility impact is conditional. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 48) Found by: the first `cypher_exprs` binding run (its `UNWIND $pairs` read answered no rows, [receipt](results/cypher_exprs/20261117T022138Z-binding/receipt.json)); a follow-up after the binding. No formal contract: potential problem, conditional on the driver. Reproduced by: **Partially reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin and its driver `intersystems-irispython` 5.3.2 (the fixture's venv); not run on 5.4.x. `UNWIND $xs AS a RETURN a` with `$xs = [1, 2]` answers ` Invalid number of parameters`, and after a `MATCH` ` Incorrect number of parameters`; the translated SQL reads `JSON_TABLE(?, '$[*]' ...)`. Passing neighbor: `WITH $xs AS l UNWIND l AS a RETURN a` answers `[1], [2]`. Iteration 47's "Incorrect number of parameters" observations for `n.l[$i]` and `m[$k]` ([bug-cyp-111](#bug-cyp-111)) may share this premise. Expected: the README: the TCK passes on Community 2026.1 with drivers 5.4.0 and 5.4.1; `pyproject.toml` accepts `intersystems-iris>=1.0.0`. The iris-sql-quirks guide (item 6) says a `?` inside `JSON_TABLE`'s source is not a parameter. Observed: a potential problem only: whether 5.4.x binds the marker is not established here, and whether 5.3.x is a supported driver is not stated. Consequence: if 5.3.x is supported, the main bulk-load pattern (`UNWIND $rows ...`) fails with it. Low until established. Iteration 50 triage of [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) m2 ([fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `param_list_slice*`, `param_list_index`): `RETURN $l[$s..$e]` and `RETURN $l[$s..]` fail "Incorrect number of parameters", and `RETURN $l[$s]` "Invalid number of parameters", while `RETURN $l[1..3]` (worked out in Python, 4.6.0 R311) and `WITH $l AS l RETURN l[$s..$e]` answer `[2, 3]`. The translated slice reads `JSON_TABLE(?, ...)`, the same marker-in-`JSON_TABLE` shape as above, so this is the same premise, not a new finding. Source reading adds one fault that would remain on any driver: `_expr_slice` adds the null-guard markers to the parameter list after the slice's own markers but writes them first in the SQL (`translator.py:23778-23789`), so with a parameter list the first guard would receive the list's text. Not modeled (`cypher_exprs` has no parameter-list base). Iteration 55 (W60) settles the driver question: **E2E reproduced** on both drivers ([5.3.2](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-params-5.3.2-observed-20261117T061226Z.json), [5.4.1](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-params-5.4.1-observed-20261117T061233Z.json); isolated venv outside the repository; [binding](results/bolt_answers/20261117T062350Z-binding/receipt.json) `F_*`, `C_driver_param`). With intersystems-irispython 5.4.1, `UNWIND $xs AS a RETURN a`, the same after a `MATCH`, and `RETURN $l[$s]` run; with 5.3.2 each fails as above, through `execute_cypher` (the result's error), Bolt and HTTP. The frozen prediction PA3 (fails on both, from driver-drift item 6) missed: item 6 concerns procedure calls inside the source, and 5.4.1 binds a plain marker. The product's own `uv.lock` pins intersystems-irispython **5.3.2** (pyproject accepts any version), so the locked environment reproduces the failure; severity raised to Medium for that reason. `UNWIND $rows ... CREATE` writes on both drivers (another route). The slice with parameter bounds is a separate wrong answer on 5.4.1: [bug-cyp-144](#bug-cyp-144); `$l[$s]` answers its element as text on 5.4.1, as [bug-cyp-111](#bug-cyp-111) records for other run-time indexes. Formal: [bolt_answers](models/bolt_answers/NOTES.md) `theorem_unwind_param_depends_on_driver` (provider premise P-DRV-JT, control `driver-532-binds`). Open question: [query.parameters.drivers](open_questions.md#query.parameters.drivers). Governing statement: [query.conformance](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.conformance).

issues.title: A null list index known only at run time answers the list's first element instead of null
issues.block: ### A null list index known only at run time answers the list's first element instead of null Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: A missing runtime list index can select the first element instead of returning null. The query produces a plausible value even though the index was not supplied. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 50) Found by: [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) item 6 (reviewer probe `p2`); [cypher_fns](models/cypher_fns/NOTES.md) `theorem_null_index_reads_first_element`; controls `null-index-is-null`, `row-index-through-ivglistget`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `idx_null_*`; [binding](results/cypher_fns/20261117T033050Z-binding/receipt.json) `index_*_null`). `WITH [1, 2, 3] AS l UNWIND [null] AS i RETURN l[i]` answers `'1'`; so do `MATCH (n) RETURN n.l[null]`, `n.l[n.nope]`, `UNWIND [null] AS i RETURN n.l[i]`, `WITH n.l AS l UNWIND [null] AS i RETURN l[i]` and `WITH [1, 2, 3] AS l RETURN l[null]`. A null parameter index fails "Incorrect number of parameters". Passing neighbor: the literal list `[1, 2, 3][null]` answers null (folded by the translator). Expected: openCypher (TCK `List1`): a null index gives null. Observed: the run-time paths of `_expr_subscript` hand the null to `JSON_ARRAYGET(l, CAST(NULL AS INTEGER))` or `JSON_VALUE(l, '$.' || CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR))` (`translator.py:23620-23656`). IRIS passes SQL NULL to an ObjectScript function as `""`; `%Get("")` reads position 0, and `'$.' || NULL` is the path `'$.'` whose key `""` also reads position 0 (`schema.py:2179-2184`). `CY_LIST_ELEM` would also read position 0 for `""`. Consequence: a missing index silently selects the first element, so `l[m.idx]` over rows lacking `idx` returns a real-looking value. Medium: wrong value with no error. Repair proposal (not implemented): test the index for null before the lookup (`CASE WHEN i IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE ... END`) on every run-time path, or have the element functions treat `""` as null. Preserve: the literal-list fold and every non-null index. Distinguishing case: `UNWIND [null, 0] AS i RETURN n.l[i]` answers null then 1. The control `null-index-is-null` checks the property path in the model only. Governing statement: [query.functions.list_index](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.list_index).

issues.title: A simple CASE over a property or a row value takes a WHEN of another type when the text matches
issues.block: ### A simple CASE over a property or a row value takes a WHEN of another type when the text matches Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: A simple CASE expression can match values of different types when their text looks the same. Stored or calculated data can select the wrong branch without an error. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 50) Found by: [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) item 7 (reviewer probe `p5`); [cypher_exprs](models/cypher_exprs/NOTES.md) `theorem_simple_case_coerces_across_kinds` with neighbor `theorem_simple_case_same_kind_or_literal_follows_rule`; controls `case-kinds-compared`, `case-literal-kinds-unchecked`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `case_simple_*`, `eq_prop_str_vs_int`; [binding](results/cypher_exprs/20261117T033119Z-binding/receipt.json) `simple_case_*`, nine kind pairs). With `n.s1 = '1'` and `n.i1 = 1`: `CASE n.s1 WHEN 1 THEN 'num' WHEN '1' THEN 'str' END` answers `'num'`; `UNWIND ['1'] AS s RETURN CASE s WHEN 1 ...` answers `'num'`; `CASE n.i1 WHEN '1' THEN 'str' ...` answers `'str'`. Passing neighbors: `n.s1 = 1` is false and `CASE WHEN n.s1 = 1 THEN 'num' ELSE 'other' END` answers `'other'`; `CASE '1' WHEN 1 ...` (literal test) takes the ELSE; same-type WHENs match. Expected: openCypher and [query.values.equality](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values.equality): a simple CASE takes the first WHEN equal to the test, and `'1'` does not equal 1. Observed: `_expr_case` drops a WHEN of another kind only when both kinds are known statically, which `_static_value_kind` knows only for literals; every other WHEN goes to SQL `CASE x WHEN y`, which IRIS evaluates with its own coercion, so a number equals text that spells it (`translator.py:22189-22238`). Consequence: a branch chosen on stored or unwound data can be wrong while the equivalent generic `CASE` is right. Medium: wrong value with no error. Repair proposal (not implemented): translate a simple CASE whose test or WHEN kind is unknown to the generic form through the typed comparison `=` already uses (`CY_JCMP`), keeping the static drop for literals. Preserve: literal simple CASEs, same-type matches, null tests taking the ELSE. Distinguishing case: `CASE n.s1 WHEN 1 THEN 'num' ELSE 'other' END` answers `'other'` while `CASE n.i1 WHEN 1 ...` still answers `'num'`. The control `case-kinds-compared` checks the repaired rule in the model only. Governing statement: [query.values.conditions](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values.conditions).

issues.title: A SET or CREATE of a list literal that holds a property read fails with a raw Python TypeError and writes nothing
issues.block: ### A SET or CREATE of a list literal that holds a property read fails with a raw Python TypeError and writes nothing Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Creating or setting a list that includes a property read can fail with an internal Python error. The otherwise valid write is refused and nothing is stored. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 50) Found by: [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) m3 (reviewer probe `p4`). No formal contract (probe and source reading only). Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `set_list_from_props`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro2-20261117T032546Z.json) `set_list_*`, `create_list_property_elem`, `after_refusal_read`). `MATCH (n) SET n.l1 = [n.a, 1]` and `MATCH (n) CREATE (:X {l: [n.a, 1]})` raise `TypeError: Object of type PropertyReference is not JSON serializable` before any SQL runs; `n.l1` stays null. Passing neighbors: `[x, 1]` from `UNWIND`, `[$x, 1]` and `[1 + 1, 1]` are stored. Expected: openCypher: a list literal's elements are evaluated per row and the list is stored; where IVG cannot, a Cypher error naming the property, as the matched-relationship refusal does. Observed: `_translate_set_value` hands a list literal to `_constant_value` and, when that answers `_NOT_CONSTANT`, `json.dumps` the raw elements, AST nodes included (`translator.py:12638-12642`). Consequence: an ordinary write is refused with an internal error that names no Cypher concept. Medium (refusal of a valid write; nothing partial). Repair proposal (not implemented): build the list in SQL from translated elements (as `SET` translates scalars), or refuse with a `CypherError` naming the property. Preserve: constant lists and row-literal lists. Governing statement: [query.writes.computed_values](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.writes.computed_values).

issues.title: Slicing a null list answers the empty list instead of null
issues.block: ### Slicing a null list answers the empty list instead of null Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Slicing a missing list returns an empty list instead of null. A report can treat absent data as a real list containing no elements. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 50) Found by: [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) m1 (reviewer probe `p4`); [cypher_exprs](models/cypher_exprs/NOTES.md) `theorem_null_list_slice_is_empty`; control `null-list-guard`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `null_list_slice`, `null_list_index`; [binding](results/cypher_exprs/20261117T033119Z-binding/receipt.json) `null_list_slice_*`). `MATCH (n) RETURN n.missing[0..2]` answers `[]` for literal, row and parameter bounds. Passing neighbor: `n.missing[0]` answers null. Expected: openCypher: an operation on null gives null. Observed: `_expr_slice` returns NULL only for an explicit null bound; the list goes into `JSON_TABLE`, which yields no rows for NULL, and the aggregate answers `[]` (`translator.py:23679-23791`). Consequence: a missing list reads as empty, so `size(n.missing[0..2])` is 0 instead of null. Low. Repair proposal (not implemented): add the list to the null guard. Governing statement: [query.functions.slice](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.slice).

issues.title: trim() keeps tabs and line breaks in a query's result, while a node CREATE removes them
issues.block: ### trim() keeps tabs and line breaks in a query's result, while a node CREATE removes them Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Trimming text handles tabs and line breaks differently in query results and node creation. The same expression can therefore produce different text depending on where it is used. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 50) Found by: [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) m4 (reviewer probe `p4`). No formal contract (probe and source reading only). Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `trim_*`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro2-20261117T032546Z.json) `return_trim_*`, `create_trim*`, `set_trim`). `RETURN trim('\t a \n')` answers the string unchanged (size 5), as does `trim(n.s)` and `SET n.t = trim(...)`; `rtrim('a \n')` keeps the line break while `ltrim('\t a')` answers `'a'`; `CREATE (:X {t: trim('\t a \n')})` stores `'a'`. Passing neighbor: `trim(' a ')` answers `'a'`. Expected: Neo4j's Cypher manual: `trim()` removes leading and trailing whitespace; the same expression gives the same value in `RETURN`, `SET` and `CREATE`. Observed: `RETURN` and `SET` translate `trim` to SQL `TRIM` (`translator.py:29537`), which removes spaces only; the node `CREATE` folder works it out with Python's `str.strip` (`translator.py:9456`), which removes all whitespace. Consequence: text with tabs or line breaks is compared or stored differently depending on the clause. Low. Repair proposal (not implemented): trim the same whitespace set on both paths (SQL `$ZSTRIP`-style function or a Python fold limited to spaces), after deciding which set is intended. Governing statement: [query.functions.strings](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.strings).

issues.title: range() with a step known only at run time accepts a fractional step
issues.block: ### range() with a step known only at run time accepts a fractional step Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: A runtime step for range can be fractional even though the operation expects integers. Invalid input produces a sequence of noninteger values instead of an argument error. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 50) Found by: [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) m6 (reviewer probe `p1`). No formal contract: `cypher_fns`'s range model covers integer steps only. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `range_fractional_step_*`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro2-20261117T032546Z.json) `range_*`). `UNWIND [1.5] AS s RETURN range(1, 3, s)` and `range(1, 3, $s)` with 1.5 answer `[1, 2.5]`. Passing neighbors: the literal `range(1, 3, 1.5)` is refused ("must be an integer"); a run-time step of 2 answers `[1, 3, 5]`. Expected: openCypher: `range()` takes integers; the translator already refuses a literal fractional step. Observed: `CypherFn.IVGRANGE` loops with whatever step it receives (`CypherFn.cls:255`), and the translator checks only literal arguments (`translator.py:29114-29122`). Consequence: a fractional run-time step yields non-integer elements instead of an error. Low. Repair proposal (not implemented): raise in `IVGRANGE` for a non-integer argument, as for a step of 0 ([F-C0841](#F-C0841)). Governing statement: [query.functions.range](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.range).

issues.title: A relationship SET from a function of its own property is refused with a message that says such a read is allowed
issues.block: ### A relationship SET from a function of its own property is refused with a message that says such a read is allowed Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Updating a relationship property from a function of its existing value is refused. The error incorrectly says that reading the property's current value is allowed, making the limitation difficult to understand. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 50) Found by: [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) m10 (reviewer probe `p3`). No formal contract (probe only). Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([fresh repro](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) `rel_retype*`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro2-20261117T032546Z.json) `rel_set_*`, `rel_read`). `MATCH ()-[r]->() SET r.age = toInteger(r.age)` and `SET r.n = toString(r.n)` are refused with "a relationship's value can read only its own `age`; a SET of a relationship from another property or another variable is not supported", although the value reads only its own property. Passing neighbor: `SET r.n = r.n + 1` is stored; a relationship's stored `'30'` already reads back as 30 ([relationship text](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values.relationship_text)). Expected: either the SET is stored, or the refusal names the actual limit (a function of the property is not supported). Observed: the relationship `SET` path accepts arithmetic over the relationship's own property only; any function call is refused with the shared message. Consequence: a misleading error; the stored value is unchanged. Low. Repair proposal (not implemented): name the unsupported shape in the message, or translate the function as the node `SET` does. Governing statement: [query.writes.retype](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.writes.retype).

issues.title: With IVG_EDGESCAN=1 every relationship property on a hop from a node named by id reads null
issues.block: ### With IVG_EDGESCAN=1 every relationship property on a hop from a node named by id reads null Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: With the optional edge-scan setting enabled, relationship properties read as null after a hop from a node selected by ID. Filters and returned values can silently change when that setting is used. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 53) Found by: iteration 53 Part B, frozen prediction ME4 (partial: the edges held, the weight missed), after reading `_trp_directed_edge_join` and `_expr_propref_edge_alias`; [sql_procs](models/sql_procs/NOTES.md) `theorem_edgescan_reads_null_property` (for every edge with a stored weight), neighbor `theorem_unweighted_and_named_agree`; control `scan-exposes-weight`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-53/sqlprocs/sqlprocs-observed-20261117T050743Z.json) `edgescan`; [binding](results/sql_procs/20261117T051429Z-binding/receipt.json) `hop_*`). `MATCH (a {id: 'a'})-[r:P]->(b) RETURN b.id, r.weight` answers `b 1.0`, `b 2.0`, `b2 1.0`, `d 10.0` by default and the same targets with `r.weight` null under `IVG_EDGESCAN=1`; `USE GRAPH ''` the same; `USE GRAPH 'g'` (rows plan) is unchanged. `count(r)` agrees (5 and 5). Expected: `IVG_EDGESCAN` chooses a plan, "the plan before 4.3.0" (ADMIN_GUIDE:1248, API_REFERENCE:3215), and CHANGELOG 4.3.0 reports both plans' answers equal; a plan choice must not change what a query answers ([structure.adjacency.scan](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.adjacency.scan)). Observed: the hop joins a `JSON_TABLE` over `MatchEdgesAllGraphs` (or `MatchEdges` for `USE GRAPH ''`) whose columns are `s, p, o_id, w, graph_id`, and `_expr_propref_edge_alias` (`translator.py:22266-22273`) returns the literal `NULL` for every property of such an alias, although the scan carries the weight as `w`. Consequence: with the variable set, any query reading `r.weight` or another relationship property after such a hop, or filtering on one in `WHERE`, answers null or drops rows. The variable is opt-in and off by default. Repair proposal (not implemented): read `r.weight` from the scan's `w` and fall back to the rows plan for any other relationship property (as already done for inline relationship properties). Preserve: the scan's targets and graphs. Distinguishing case: the hop above reads 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 10.0 under both settings (control `scan-exposes-weight` checks the model's direction only). Governing statement: [structure.adjacency.scan](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.adjacency.scan).

issues.title: percentileDisc rounds the rank down: p 0.9 over 10, 20, 30, 40 answers 30, not 40
issues.block: ### percentileDisc rounds the rank down: p 0.9 over 10, 20, 30, 40 answers 30, not 40 Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: The discrete-percentile calculation selects a rank that is too low for many inputs. High-percentile reports over small groups can understate the largest observed values without warning. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 53) Found by: iteration 53 W59 frozen prediction P1b ([PAIRS](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-53/bm25-percentile-PAIRS.md), a miss: nearest rank was predicted); [percentile](models/percentile/NOTES.md) `theorem_disc_top_percentile_misses_max` (for every n ≥ 2 and every p with (n − 1)/n < p < 1), `theorem_disc_never_above_rule`, witness `theorem_disc_rounds_down_p90`; control `disc-nearest-rank`. The iteration-47 checks (median, quartiles) give the same answer under both rules, so they could not see it. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-53/bm25/bm25-percentile-observed-20261117T050649Z.json) `P1b_*:sql`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-53/bm25/followup-observed-20261117T050736Z.json) `unwind_lit_*`, `match_param_0.9`; [binding](results/percentile/20261117T052012Z-binding/receipt.json), 156 cases). `UNWIND [10, 20, 30, 40] AS x RETURN percentileDisc(x, 0.9)` answers 30.0 and `percentileDisc(x, 0.6)` 20.0; `percentileDisc` at 0.95 over 1 to 10 answers 9.0; a stored-value `MATCH` with `$p` = 0.9 and `Percentile_PDISC('[10,20,30,40]', 0.9)` answer the same. p 1/3 over 10, 20, 30, 40 answers 10, because the double 0.333… times 3 is just below 1. Passing neighbors: p 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1 agree with nearest rank; `percentileCont` interpolates correctly (0.9 gives 37.0). Expected: the owner [query.functions.percentile](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.percentile) ("the stored value at the nearest rank", "as Neo4j does"); Neo4j's `percentileDisc` "uses a rounding method and calculates the nearest value to the percentile" (index ceil(p × n) − 1, so 40 at 0.9 and 30 at 0.6). Observed: `IVG.Percentile.PDISC` takes index `((n - 1) * p) \ 1`, the floor of the interpolation position (`iris_src/src/IVG/Percentile.cls:13`), reached from the translator's `Percentile_PDISC(JSON_ARRAYAGG(CAST(x AS DOUBLE)), p)` (`translator.py:28616-28617`). Consequence: the answer is never above the nearest-rank value and is one rank below it for many p (0.6 and 0.9 of four values, though not 0.4); for every p in ((n − 1)/n, 1) it is the second-largest value instead of the largest, so high percentiles (p90, p95, p99 of latencies or scores) of small groups are understated. No error is raised. Repair proposal (not implemented): index `ceil(p × n) − 1` clamped to [0, n − 1] (Neo4j). Preserve: p 0 and 1, the median and quartile answers already observed, null for no values, NumberOutOfRange. Writers: none; readers: every Cypher `percentileDisc` and SQL `Percentile_PDISC`. The control `disc-nearest-rank` checks the repaired index in the model only; the repair was not run on the product.

issues.title: A grouping key and count(DISTINCT) treat a stored number and the string spelling it as one value, while RETURN DISTINCT keeps them apart
issues.block: ### A grouping key and count(DISTINCT) treat a stored number and the string spelling it as one value, while RETURN DISTINCT keeps them apart Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Grouping and distinct counts can merge a stored number with text containing the same digits. Reports undercount distinct values and disagree with RETURN DISTINCT on the same data. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 54) Found by: iteration 54 W59 frozen predictions AG1 and AG2 ([PAIRS](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-PAIRS.md), both missed); [cypher_clauses](models/cypher_clauses/NOTES.md) `theorem_sql_group_merges_number_and_its_text` (every spelling), `theorem_sql_group_and_distinct_disagree_on_marked_text` (exactly the pairs with equal text and different storage marks); control `group-by-typed`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-observed-20261117T053516Z.json) `AG1_api`, `AG1_twin`, `AG1_api_distinct`, `AG2_*`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-observed2-20261117T053826Z.json) `G_*`; [binding](results/cypher_clauses/20261117T060402Z-binding/receipt.json) `A_*`, 112 cases). Over nodes written by `create_node` with `k` = 1, 1, `'1'` and 1.5, `MATCH (n:G) RETURN n.k AS k, count(*) AS c` answers `[1, 3], [1.5, 1]`; `RETURN DISTINCT n.k` answers 1, `'1'` and 1.5. The Cypher-written twin answers the same. `count(DISTINCT n.k)` over 1, `'1'`, 1.0, `'1.0'`, true, `'true'`, `'01'` answers 4 where `RETURN DISTINCT` and `collect(DISTINCT n.k)` list 6 values (true and `'true'` are one stored value, the documented collision). Over a literal list, `UNWIND [1, '1'] AS k` gives one group, one `DISTINCT` row and count 1; `UNWIND [1, true]`, `[[1], '[1]']` give one group but two `DISTINCT` rows. Passing neighbors: two integers, two strings, an integer and a list, `'1'` and `'x'`. Expected: [query.aggregation](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.aggregation) ("`DISTINCT` removes repeated equal values") with [equality](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values.equality) ("an integer literal on a node matches only a stored number of that value: the string "1" ... do[es] not equal 1"); openCypher groups and counts distinct by equivalence, so 1 and `'1'` are two groups. Observed: `translate_return_clause` selects a stored property through `CY_TYPED` (`translator.py:30676`) but adds the plain `sql`, the stored text, to `GROUP BY` (30777, "GROUP BY below keeps the plain `sql`"); `_expr_aggregation` writes `COUNT(DISTINCT arg)` over the plain argument (24431). IRIS compares the text, and the row's `CY_TYPED` value is whichever member IRIS picks. Consequence: a report grouped by a property that holds numbers on some nodes and their spelling on others (an earlier release's Python numbers, imported text) counts them as one group under the number's type, and `count(DISTINCT)` undercounts, with no error. `RETURN DISTINCT` on the same data disagrees with both. Repair proposal (not implemented): group and count distinct by the `CY_TYPED` value the column already selects. Preserve: single-kind keys, the null group, the documented boolean/list text collision, graph-and-id node distinctness. Readers: every grouped RETURN or WITH and `count(DISTINCT)`. The control `group-by-typed` checks the direction in the model only.

issues.title: The SQL path and the native executor group the same stored values differently
issues.block: ### The SQL path and the native executor group the same stored values differently Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: The SQL and native executors group some stored values differently. A change in query routing can alter a report's groups and counts even when the underlying data is unchanged. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 54) Found by: iteration 54 W59 follow-up (the native executor's answer beside the SQL path's for AG1's shape); [cypher_clauses](models/cypher_clauses/NOTES.md) `theorem_paths_disagree_exactly_on_marked_text` (for every pair of stored values), `theorem_native_group_follows_rule`; control `native-text-key`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-observed2-20261117T053826Z.json) `G_api_group`, `NV_group_api`; [binding](results/cypher_clauses/20261117T060402Z-binding/receipt.json) `A_Int1_Str1_native_group`, `A_Int2_Str2_native_group`). `MATCH (n:G) RETURN n.k AS k, count(*) AS c` over 1, `'1'`, 1.0, `'1.0'`, true, `'true'`, `'01'` answers 4 groups on the SQL path (`[1, 3]`, …) and 6 on the native executor (`['1', 1]`, `[1, 1]`, `[1.0, 1]`, …). The native executor accepts this shape by default, so the answer depends on which path the planner picks. Expected: [query.native.equal-answers](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.native.equal-answers): the native executor gives the SQL path's answer. The native grouping is the one that follows openCypher here (1 and 1.0 aside; see the [open question](open_questions.md#query.aggregation.keys.numbers)). Observed: `Graph.KG.Cypher.Exec.GroupOf` finds a group by the keys' `$List` from `KeyValues` ("a number stays a number"; `Exec.cls:1349-1380`, 1742), while the SQL path groups by text ([bug-cyp-135](#bug-cyp-135)). The shadow-mode TCK runs could not see it: their data are Cypher literals of one kind per key. Consequence: the same grouped query answers different groups and counts on the two paths, and changes answer when the planner's choice changes (an `OPTIONAL MATCH`, a parameter `LIMIT` or a native gate sends it to SQL). Repairing [bug-cyp-135](#bug-cyp-135) removes the disagreement.

issues.title: Arithmetic over two property aggregates answers a rounded integer: sum(n.v) + sum(n.f) of 3 and 3.5 answers 6
issues.block: ### Arithmetic over two property aggregates answers a rounded integer: sum(n.v) + sum(n.f) of 3 and 3.5 answers 6 Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Arithmetic combining aggregates over stored properties can discard fractional values. Totals, differences and ratios can be rounded to an integer without an error. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 54) Found by: iteration 54 W59, after the first observation (`AG4_mixed_props`, `AG7_api_sum`; not among the frozen predictions, whose sums were single aggregates); [cypher_clauses](models/cypher_clauses/NOTES.md) `theorem_sum_of_property_sums_is_int_column`, `theorem_int_column_loses_any_half` (every total with a half), witness `theorem_probe_totals`; controls `prop-default-unknown`, `int-read-exact`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-observed-20261117T053516Z.json) `AG4_mixed_props`, `AG7_api_sum`, `AG7_twin_sum`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-observed2-20261117T053826Z.json) `AR_*`; [binding](results/cypher_clauses/20261117T060402Z-binding/receipt.json) `B_*`). With `v` 1, 2 and `f` 2.5, 1.0 written by `create_node`, `RETURN sum(n.v) + sum(n.f)` answers 6 (6.5), in either order; over 1 and 1.5 it answers 2 (2.5) and over 1 and 0.5 answers 2 (1.5): Python's half-to-even round. `sum(r.w) + sum(r.weight)` over relationship values 1 and 2.5 answers 4, for API- and Cypher-written relationships. `min(n.f) * 2` answers the integer 2 for 2.0. Passing neighbors: `sum(n.f)` alone (3.5), `sum(n.v) + 0.5`, `count(*) + 0.5`, `avg(n.v) + 1`, `RETURN 3 + 3.5`. Expected: [query.aggregation](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.aggregation) ("with typed numeric inputs, it stays an integer when every contributor is an integer and a float when one is a float") and openCypher arithmetic (3 + 3.5 = 6.5). Observed: `_numeric_static_type` types `sum`/`min`/`max` by `_arith_operand_type` of the argument, which defaults a bare property to `'int'` (`translator.py:22088-22089`, 22151-22152); `+` of two `'int'` operands is `'int'` (22110-22116), so the column joins `int_expr_aliases` (30742-30743) and `_int_expr_value` answers `int(round(v))` (`_engine/query.py:1237`). A bare `sum(n.f)` takes the typed-sum path instead. Consequence: totals, ratios and differences of aggregated stored values lose their fraction silently (financial or score reports combining two sums). No error is raised. Repair proposal (not implemented): give an aggregate of a stored property no static type (as a bare sum has none) and read the column through `CY_TYPED`, or type it from the stored values. Preserve: integer results of integer contributors, `count()`, integer division. Readers: every RETURN or WITH column of arithmetic over aggregates. The control `prop-default-unknown` checks the direction in the model only.

issues.title: A UNION answers stored property values as their storage text: 1 as "\x01N1", 2.5 as "\x01D2.5", a list as JSON text
issues.block: ### A UNION answers stored property values as their storage text: 1 as "\x01N1", 2.5 as "\x01D2.5", a list as JSON text Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: UNION can return internal storage text instead of decoded property values. Clients receive incorrect types, and duplicate removal can either keep equal values or merge values that should differ. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 54) Found by: iteration 54 W59 frozen prediction UN2 (partial: one row held, the value did not); [cypher_clauses](models/cypher_clauses/NOTES.md) `theorem_union_answers_marked_text` (every value, any other branches), `theorem_union_dedup_by_raw`, neighbors `theorem_single_query_decodes`, `theorem_all_bool_union_stays_bool`; controls `union-keeps-decoders`, `typed-read-plain`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-observed-20261117T053516Z.json) `UN2_*`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-observed2-20261117T053826Z.json) `U_*`; [binding](results/cypher_clauses/20261117T060402Z-binding/receipt.json) `C_*`). `MATCH (n {name: 'a1'}) RETURN n.v AS x UNION RETURN 0 AS x` answers `'\x01N1'` for the stored integer 1 (and `UNION ALL` the same), `n.f` answers `'\x01D2.5'`, a stored boolean `'true'`, a stored list `'[1, 2]'`, a relationship's `r.w` `'1'`; without the UNION the same `RETURN n.v` answers 1. `RETURN n.v AS x UNION RETURN 1 AS x` answers two rows; `RETURN 1 AS x UNION RETURN true AS x` answers one row, 1; `UNION` of `1`, `2.5`, `true`, `[1]` answers 1, 2.5 and `'[1]'`, losing `true`. Passing neighbors: a `UNION` of literal numbers, of booleans in every branch, of strings, and row counts with Cypher-written data. Expected: openCypher `UNION` returns each branch's values with their types and removes duplicate rows by equivalence (TCK Union1-3, all over literals); [query.values](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values) (a node property read preserves its stored type). Observed: `_tts_union_branches` translates each branch alone and returns `SQLQuery(sql=combined, parameters=..., bool_expr_columns=...)` (`translator.py:4714`): only the boolean marks common to every branch survive; the typed-value, JSON, relationship-text, numeric and node marks of the branches are dropped, so the reader leaves `CY_TYPED`'s marked text as it is. IRIS `UNION` then removes duplicates by those raw values. Consequence: any `UNION` over stored data answers wrong-typed values, some of them control-character text, to `execute_cypher`, REST and Bolt clients; duplicate removal keeps equal values apart and merges `1` with `true`. No error is raised. Repair proposal (not implemented): carry each column's decoder through the union when every branch agrees on it, and type-mark literal branches the same way. Preserve: column checks, the refusal of mixed `UNION`/`UNION ALL`, boolean columns. The control `union-keeps-decoders` checks the direction in the model only. Iteration 58 (W62 C4, partial): a relationship returned in a `UNION ALL` branch also reaches the reader as JSON text (`'{"type":"K","props":{}}'`), while the same `RETURN r` alone answers a map; a stored double and a stored list behaved as already recorded ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/clauses/probe1.out), driver 5.3.2). Observed only, not modeled. Iteration 59 (review 56-58 evidence): literal lists in a `UNION` also come back as JSON text: `RETURN [1,2] AS x UNION RETURN [3] AS x` answers `'[1, 2]'` and `'[3]'`, and `UNION ALL` of `[1,2]` twice answers `'[1, 2]'` twice, on both engines, while `RETURN [1,2]` alone answers the list `[1, 2]` and a `UNION` of scalars answers integers ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-59/review-repairs/minor-observed-20261117T090528Z.json), keys `U_*`). Found by: independent review 56-58; reproduced by: this run's probe.

issues.title: SKIP and LIMIT use a string, boolean or whole-float parameter as a count, and call a null parameter "not provided"
issues.block: ### SKIP and LIMIT use a string, boolean or whole-float parameter as a count, and call a null parameter "not provided" Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Pagination accepts some strings, booleans and whole-number floats as counts instead of rejecting invalid types. A null count is reported as missing, making argument errors inconsistent and harder to diagnose. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 54) Found by: iteration 54 W59 (WS3 held for `-1` and 1.5; the other kinds were found after the first observation); [cypher_clauses](models/cypher_clauses/NOTES.md) `theorem_non_integer_parameter_used`, neighbor `theorem_integer_and_fraction_follow_rule`; controls `page-int-only`, `page-no-negative-check`, `page-no-fraction-check`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-observed2-20261117T053826Z.json) `L_*`; [binding](results/cypher_clauses/20261117T060402Z-binding/receipt.json) `D_*`). `LIMIT $l` with `l` = `'2'` answers two rows, with `true` one row, with `false` none, with 2.0 two rows; `'-1'` gives NegativeIntegerArgument, `'x'` a raw Python `ValueError` ("invalid literal for int()"), and `null` "Parameter '$l' used in SKIP/LIMIT but not provided in params dict" although it was provided. `SKIP` behaves the same. Passing neighbors: integer literals and parameters, negative ones (NegativeIntegerArgument), 1.5 (InvalidArgumentType), a missing parameter. Expected: openCypher (TCK ReturnSkipLimit1-2: a floating point parameter fails with InvalidArgumentType; a negative one with NegativeIntegerArgument): `SKIP` and `LIMIT` take a non-negative integer, and a value of another type is an InvalidArgumentType. Observed: `_resolve_pagination_value` refuses only a missing or null value and a float with a fraction, then uses `int(resolved)` (`translator.py:8106-8116`). Consequence: a client that passes the page size as text or a boolean gets rows instead of an error, and a null page size is reported as a missing parameter. No data is changed.

issues.title: A UNION whose branch is a whole-label count fails with SQLCODE -1
issues.block: ### A UNION whose branch is a whole-label count fails with SQLCODE -1 Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: A UNION branch using the whole-label count shortcut generates invalid SQL. An otherwise valid combined query fails instead of returning its counts. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 54) Found by: iteration 54 W59 follow-up (`U_count`); [cypher_clauses](models/cypher_clauses/NOTES.md) `theorem_label_count_branch_fails`, neighbor `theorem_count_alone_and_other_branches_prepare`; controls `count-guard-sees-union`, `shortcut-newline-from`, `ensure-from-always`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-observed2-20261117T053826Z.json) `U_count`; [binding](results/cypher_clauses/20261117T060402Z-binding/receipt.json) `E_*`). `MATCH (n:L) RETURN count(n) AS x UNION ALL RETURN 0 AS x` and `MATCH (n:L) RETURN count(*) AS x UNION RETURN 7 AS x` fail at Prepare (`SQLCODE -1`, "`)` expected, FROM found", the statement holding `... FROM Graph_KG.rdf_labels WHERE label = ? FROM (SELECT 1) __dual`). Passing neighbors: the count alone, and a `UNION ALL` whose branch returns `n.name`. Expected: openCypher allows any branch that returns the same columns (TCK Union1-3). Observed: `_tts_union_branches` translates each branch from a copy whose `union_queries` it empties (`translator.py:4690`), so `_lone_label_count`'s guard against a UNION passes (7424-7426) and the branch becomes a one-line `SELECT ... FROM rdf_labels WHERE ...` (7458); `_ensure_from` (4701-4704) looks for `"\nFROM "`, finds none and appends a second `FROM`. Consequence: a valid query is refused with a raw SQL error. Workaround: add `WHERE true` or a property to the branch's pattern, which skips the shortcut.
