issues.block: ### startNode() and endNode() of a relationship taken from relationships(p) fail with SQLCODE -29 Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Extracting the start or end node from a relationship obtained through a path fails. The intermediate relationship representation lacks the endpoint information needed to answer the query. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 54) Found by: iteration 54 W59 (`PA4_rels`, after the frozen PA4 row, which asked only for `type()`); [cypher_clauses](models/cypher_clauses/NOTES.md) `theorem_path_element_endpoints_fail`, neighbor `theorem_type_and_matched_endpoints_work`; controls `endpoint-reads-json`, `type-reads-alias`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-observed-20261117T053516Z.json) `PA4_rels`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/clauses-observed2-20261117T053826Z.json) `R_*`; [binding](results/cypher_clauses/20261117T060402Z-binding/receipt.json) `F_*`). `MATCH p = (a)-[:K*1..2]->(c) RETURN [r IN relationships(p) | startNode(r).name]` fails at Prepare ("Field 'LC5.S' not found"), for fixed-length paths too, and so does `endNode(r)`; `type(r)`, `r.w` and `r` itself answer. `startNode(r)` of a matched relationship answers. Expected: openCypher: `startNode(r)` of any relationship value is its start node; USER_GUIDE shows path functions with comprehensions (`[n IN nodes(p) | n.name]`). Observed: `_expr_fn_node_funcs` translates `startNode(v)` to `{alias}.s` and `endNode(v)` to `{alias}.o_id` for any bound variable (`translator.py:28993-29005`); for a `relationships(p)` element the alias is a `JSON_TABLE` row holding `{"type", "props"}`, with no such column. `type()` has a branch for that element (28989-28990). issues.title: A WHERE inside OPTIONAL MATCH that combines an earlier variable's property with arithmetic or OR fails the query with SQLCODE -94
issues.block: ### A WHERE inside OPTIONAL MATCH that combines an earlier variable's property with arithmetic or OR fails the query with SQLCODE -94 Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: An OPTIONAL MATCH filter can fail when it combines an earlier variable's property with arithmetic or OR. A valid read is rejected with an internal SQL error. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 54) Found by: iteration 54 W59, after the source read of the OPTIONAL MATCH WHERE placement (its prediction, from the owner [query.optional](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.optional), was written in the probe before it ran: one row per node, null where no match passes); [cypher_clauses](models/cypher_clauses/NOTES.md) `theorem_outer_arith_or_refused` (conditional on the provider premise P-OUTER-ON), neighbors `theorem_opt_neighbors_follow_rule`; controls `iris-accepts-outer-on`, `opt-cond-in-where`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/optional-mixed-observed-20261117T060018Z.json) `*_opt_plus`, `*_opt_or_mixed`, `*_opt_count`; [binding](results/cypher_clauses/20261117T060402Z-binding/receipt.json) `H_OuterArith_*`, `H_OuterOrOpt_*`). `MATCH (a:L) OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[:K]->(b) WHERE b.v = a.v + 1 RETURN a.name, b.name`, `... WHERE a.v = 1 OR b.v = 5` and the same with `RETURN count(*)` answer no rows and the result's error "SQLCODE -94 Unsupported usage of OUTER JOIN", for API- and Cypher-written data. Passing neighbors: the same condition under a plain `MATCH` and as a `WITH a, b WHERE ...` after the OPTIONAL MATCH; conditions on the optional side only; `b.v > a.v` and `b.name <> a.name`. The first run of the probe read only the rows and saw an empty answer; it is kept under `iteration-54/failed-runs/`. Expected: [query.optional](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.optional): the WHERE filters the optional matches and the row stays; openCypher allows any predicate there (TCK `Match`/`OptionalMatch` scenarios use predicates on one side). Observed: `translate_where_clause` pushes a condition that reads both the clause's new variables and earlier ones into the first optional join's ON when it names no later join alias (`translator.py:17128-17175`). The ON then holds IVG's arithmetic (`CASE WHEN ISNUMERIC(p4.val) ... CY_ARITH`) or an OR of an earlier left-joined property read with a correlated `(SELECT val ...)`, which IRIS 2026.1 refuses at Prepare. The pure-optional branch has a fallback for property subqueries (17095-17107); the mixed branch has none. The comment at 17038 names the same IRIS limit for `CY_CMP`. Consequence: a valid OPTIONAL MATCH filter fails the whole read with a raw SQL error; `execute_cypher` answers no rows with the error set. Workaround: move the test into a `WITH ... WHERE` after the OPTIONAL MATCH when dropping the null rows is intended, or compute `a.v + 1` in a `WITH` before it. Iteration 58 (W62 C3, held): the refusal follows negation polarity. A WHERE reading only the new alias runs and keeps every row whatever its AND, OR, NOT and arithmetic (`b.v = 2 OR b.v = 3`, `b.v - 1 = 2`); `NOT (b.v = a.v OR b.v = 10)` runs, while `NOT (b.v = a.v + 1)` and `NOT (b.v = 10 AND b.v = a.v)` are refused. Modeled by [clause_combos](models/clause_combos/NOTES.md) `theorem_negation_polarity`, `theorem_new_alias_only_keeps_row` (15 shapes, [binding](results/clause_combos/20261117T082514Z-binding/receipt.json) `C_*`, [probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/clauses/probe3.out)); still outside the modeled domain: `NOT ((b.v = 10) OR (a.v = 1))` is refused.

issues.title: A comparison on an earlier variable's property inside an OPTIONAL MATCH WHERE drops the rows of nodes that lack the property
issues.block: ### A comparison on an earlier variable's property inside an OPTIONAL MATCH WHERE drops the rows of nodes that lack the property Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: An OPTIONAL MATCH filter can discard the original row when a property is missing. The query loses rows that should remain with an unmatched optional result. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 54) Found by: iteration 54 W59, after the source read (same probe and prediction as [bug-cyp-142](#bug-cyp-142)); [cypher_clauses](models/cypher_clauses/NOTES.md) `theorem_outer_guard_drops_row`, neighbors `theorem_opt_neighbors_follow_rule`; controls `opt-guard-in-on`, `range-guarded`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-54/optional-mixed-observed-20261117T060018Z.json) `*_opt_eq_props`, `*_opt_and_split`; [binding](results/cypher_clauses/20261117T060402Z-binding/receipt.json) `H_EqProps_*`, `H_NeProps_*`, `H_OuterLitAndOpt_*`). Over `a1 {v: 1} → a2 {v: 2} → a3 {}`, `OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[:K]->(b) WHERE b.v = a.v` answers `a1` and `a2` with null `b` and no row for `a3`; `WHERE a.v = 1 AND b.v = 2` answers `[a1, a2], [a2, null]`, again without `a3`; `b.v <> a.v` the same. API- and Cypher-written data alike. Passing neighbors: a node that has the property keeps its null row; `b.v > a.v` (the CY_CMP range) and conditions on the optional side keep every row. Expected: [query.optional](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.optional) and openCypher: a WHERE inside OPTIONAL MATCH never removes the row; `a3` comes back with `b` null. Observed: the WHERE's read of `a.v` goes through `_expr_property_reference`, which for a variable bound before the OPTIONAL MATCH adds the structural guard `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rdf_props ... "key" = 'v')` to the query's own WHERE (`translator.py:23111-23115`) whenever `_null_rejecting_refs` marks it as an operand of a comparison in the AND chain (18603-18619); the condition itself goes into the optional join's ON. The guard is right for a MATCH's WHERE (a missing property fails the row anyway) and wrong here. Consequence: rows of the outer `MATCH` disappear from an OPTIONAL MATCH report whenever the node lacks a property the optional filter compares, with no error. Repair proposal (not implemented): do not add the guard while translating a WHERE that an OPTIONAL MATCH pushes into its join, or put it into the same ON. Preserve: the guard in a plain MATCH's WHERE (OPT-3 performance), the null row for nodes with the property. The control `opt-guard-in-on` checks the direction in the model only.

issues.title: A slice of a list parameter by parameters answers the empty list with IRIS driver 5.4.1 (and fails with 5.3.2)
issues.block: ### A slice of a list parameter by parameters answers the empty list with IRIS driver 5.4.1 (and fails with 5.3.2) Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Slicing a list parameter using parameterized bounds returns an empty list with the tested 5.4.1 driver and fails with 5.3.2. Applications cannot reliably page through a supplied list this way. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 55) Found by: frozen W60 prediction PA4 missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-PAIRS.md)); the iteration-50 source note on [bug-cyp-125](#bug-cyp-125) (markers out of order) now observed; [bolt_answers](models/bolt_answers/NOTES.md) `theorem_param_slice_answers_empty`; controls `slice-markers-in-order`, `driver-532-binds`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, under intersystems-irispython [5.3.2](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-params-5.3.2-observed-20261117T061226Z.json) and [5.4.1](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-params-5.4.1-observed-20261117T061233Z.json) (an isolated venv outside the repository) ([binding](results/bolt_answers/20261117T062350Z-binding/receipt.json) `F_slice_*`). `RETURN $l[$s..$e]` with `l = [1, 2, 3, 4]`, `s = 1`, `e = 3` answers `[]` on 5.4.1 and fails "Incorrect number of parameters" on 5.3.2. Passing neighbor: `WITH $l AS l RETURN l[$s..$e]` answers `[2, 3]` on both. Expected: [query.parameters](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.parameters); openCypher list slicing: `[2, 3]`. Observed: the translated SQL is `CASE WHEN (?) IS NULL OR (?) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE (... JSON_TABLE(?, ...) ... WHERE rn > (?) AND rn <= (?)) END` with parameters `[list, s, e, s, e]`: `_expr_slice` appends the guard values after the slice's own (`translator.py:23778-23789`), so the guards read the list and `s`, and JSON_TABLE reads `e`'s text, which yields no row. Consequence: a parameterized page of a list parameter answers nothing, with no error, on the driver the TCK uses. Medium. Repair proposal (not implemented; checked in the model only): append the guard values first, in the SQL's order. Preserve the WITH-held list path. Distinguishing case: the probe query on 5.4.1. Governing statement: [query.parameters](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.parameters).

issues.title: A string literal or string parameter equals a stored node number that it spells
issues.block: ### A string literal or string parameter equals a stored node number that it spells Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: A filter comparing a string with a stored node property can also match a number with the same spelling. Text IDs or codes can therefore select unintended numeric values. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 55) Found by: frozen W60 prediction PA2 missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-PAIRS.md)); post-read T4; [bolt_answers](models/bolt_answers/NOTES.md) `theorem_string_operand_matches_number`, general `theorem_int_operands_and_string_values_follow_rule`; controls `string-compare-typed`, `int-param-raw`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, on `execute_cypher`, Bolt and HTTP ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-observed-20261117T061246Z.json) `PA2_str`; [post-read probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-observed2-20261117T061633Z.json) `T4_*`; [binding](results/bolt_answers/20261117T062350Z-binding/receipt.json) `G_*`). Over a node with the integer `v: 1` (written by `create_node`) and one with the string `v: "1"`: `WHERE n.v = '1'` and `WHERE n.v = $x` with `$x = "1"` match both. Passing neighbors: `n.v = 1` and `n.v = $x` with `$x = 1` match only the integer. Expected: KNOWN_ISSUES ("A property cannot tell a number from a string that spells it", 4.7.0): a node filter reads the stored type; openCypher: a string never equals a number. [query.values.equality](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values.equality). Observed: an integer literal gets the typed guard (`CAST(p.val AS DOUBLE) = ...` behind the N-mark test); a string literal or any parameter becomes the raw comparison `p.val = '1'` / `p.val = ?`, which IRIS evaluates as text against the stored number's text (translated SQL recorded in the predictions file). Consequence: a filter by a string id or code also returns nodes whose number has the same digits. Medium. Repair proposal (not implemented; checked in the model only): give string operands the same typed guard (stored strings only). Preserve the integer-literal and integer-parameter behavior. Distinguishing case: `n.v = '1'` over a stored 1. Governing statement: [query.values.equality](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values.equality).

issues.title: length(p) of a path an OPTIONAL MATCH did not bind answers the pattern's length instead of null
issues.block: ### length(p) of a path an OPTIONAL MATCH did not bind answers the pattern's length instead of null Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: The length of an unmatched optional path is reported as the pattern's length instead of null. Reports can count a path that does not exist or keep rows that should fail a path-length filter. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 56) Found by: independent review round 3 (review 53-55 F2, reviewer session `c68a5c59`, probe `rv55b … len_*`); [cypher_clauses](models/cypher_clauses/NOTES.md) section I `theorem_unmatched_fixed_path_length_is_hops`, general `theorem_path_fn_departs_exactly_on_unmatched_fixed_length`, neighbor `theorem_bound_or_varlen_path_follows_rule`; controls `fixed-length-from-row`, `varlen-length-from-pattern`, `anchor-null-ignored`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, on an engine with the native executor off and one with it on ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-56/cypher/cypher-observed-20261117T065840Z.json) `fix1_un`, `fix2_un`; [binding](results/cypher_clauses/20261117T065639Z-binding/receipt.json) `I_fix1_unmatched_len`, `I_fix2_unmatched_len`, `I_fix1_unmatched_len_native_on`). Over `a1 → a2 → a3` written by `create_edge`, `MATCH (a {name: 'a3'}) OPTIONAL MATCH p = (a)-[:K]->(b) RETURN length(p), p IS NULL, nodes(p), relationships(p)` answers `1, true, null, null`; the two-hop pattern from `a2` answers `length(p)` = 2 with `p IS NULL` true. Passing neighbors: a bound path answers its own length (1, 2); a variable-length `OPTIONAL MATCH p = (a)-[:K*1..2]->(b)` with no match answers null and with matches 1 and 2; a null anchor (`OPTIONAL MATCH (a {name: 'none'}) OPTIONAL MATCH p = ...`) answers null; `length(null)` answers null. OPTIONAL MATCH never runs native, so both engines answer the same. Expected: [query.optional](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.optional) ("later expressions read them as null") and openCypher: a path the OPTIONAL MATCH did not bind is null, and `length(null)` is null. Observed: the translator's path-function branch answers `length()` of a fixed pattern with the constant `len(pattern.relationships)` (`translator.py:28797-28802`), never reading the row; `nodes()` and `relationships()` read the row's aliases and so are null, and a variable-length path reads its row value (`_vlp_path_sql`). Only a null anchor (`optional_null_row_unconditional`, 28788-28790) answers NULL. Consequence: a report that counts or filters on `length(p)` after an OPTIONAL MATCH treats rows with no path as paths of full length (for example `WHERE length(p) > 0` keeps every unmatched row, and `sum(length(p))` counts them), silently. Repair proposal (not implemented): for a path bound by an OPTIONAL MATCH, emit `CASE WHEN IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE h END`, as `nodes(p)` already yields null. Preserve: the constant for a path bound by a plain MATCH (always bound), the variable-length branch, the null-anchor branch. Distinguishing case: the binding's `I_fix1_unmatched_len` against `I_fix1_matched_len`; the control `fixed-length-from-row` checks the direction in the model only.

issues.title: percentileDisc over integers answers a float
issues.block: ### percentileDisc over integers answers a float Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: The discrete-percentile function returns a floating-point value even when it selects from integers. Callers that require an integer, such as a list index, can reject or misinterpret the result. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 56) Found by: owned as built in iteration 53 ("Today both answer a float"); registered after independent review round 3 (review 53-55 minor "percentile result type"); [percentile](models/percentile/NOTES.md) `theorem_disc_over_ints_answers_float`, neighbor `theorem_float_and_cont_kinds_follow_rule`; control `disc-keeps-input-kind`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-56/cypher/cypher-observed-20261117T065840Z.json) `pct_int`, `pct_flt`, `min_int`; [binding](results/percentile/20261117T065550Z-binding/receipt.json) `kind:unwind:int`, `kind:match:int`). `UNWIND [10, 20, 30, 40] AS x RETURN percentileDisc(x, 0.5)` answers `20.0` (a Python float), also over stored integers. Passing neighbors: `percentileCont` answers `25.0` (a float, as it should); over floats `percentileDisc` answers `1.5`; `min(x)` and `max(x)` over the same integers answer `10` and `20` as integers, on both engines. Expected: [query.functions.percentile](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.percentile): `percentileDisc` answers one of the values, so it keeps their type; Neo4j answers `20` over integers (openCypher TCK `Aggregation6` compares percentileDisc results over integers as integers). Observed: `_scalar_statistical` emits `Percentile_PDISC(JSON_ARRAYAGG(CAST(x AS DOUBLE)), p)` and the translator types the column FLOAT, so `_float_expr_value` (`_engine/query.py:1243-1260`) turns every answer into a float. Consequence: a client comparing the answer with a stored integer, or using it as a list index or a `LIMIT`, gets a float. Repair proposal (not implemented): type the percentileDisc column from its argument's static type (int for an integer property), leaving percentileCont FLOAT. Preserve: percentileCont's float, the `NumberOutOfRange` refusal, null for no values; the iteration-55 text-spelling read under driver 5.4.1.

issues.title: A percentile p that is not a number: null raises a raw Python TypeError, text and booleans are converted, a literal null answers p = 0
issues.block: ### A percentile p that is not a number: null raises a raw Python TypeError, text and booleans are converted, a literal null answers p = 0 Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Invalid percentile arguments are handled inconsistently: some are converted, while null can produce an internal Python error. A caller can receive the wrong percentile or an unclear failure instead of a type error. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 56) Found by: independent review round 3 (review 53-55 minor "null percentile parameter", probe `pct_param_null`, `pct_param_str`); the other kinds by the iteration-56 probe; [percentile](models/percentile/NOTES.md) `theorem_non_number_p_not_refused`, general `theorem_p_departs_exactly_on_non_numbers`; controls `null-param-refused`, `literal-null-refused`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-56/cypher/cypher-observed-20261117T065840Z.json) `pct_p_*`, `pct_lit_null`; [binding](results/percentile/20261117T065550Z-binding/receipt.json) `p:*`). Over `UNWIND [10, 20, 30] AS x RETURN percentileDisc(x, $p)`: `$p` = null raises `TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'NoneType'` out of `execute_cypher` (percentileCont the same); `$p` = `'x'` raises `ValueError: could not convert string to float`; `$p` = `'0.5'` answers 20.0; `$p` = true answers 30.0 (p = 1); a literal `percentileDisc(x, null)` answers 10.0 (p = 0). Passing neighbors: `$p` = 0.5 and a literal 0.5 answer 20.0; a missing `$p` is "Undefined variable: p". Expected: [query.functions.percentile](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.functions.percentile): `p` is a number from 0 to 1; anything else fails as a Cypher argument error (openCypher does not say whether a null p fails or answers null; both readings reject a raw Python exception and the p = 0 answer). Observed: `_scalar_statistical` passes a `$p` parameter through Python `float(context.input_params[name])` (`translator.py:28595-28603`) during translation, outside the error handling that turns translation errors into Cypher errors; a literal null is pasted as SQL `NULL`, which `IVG.Percentile.PDISC` reads as `""` and so as 0 in its range check and index (provider premise P-OS-EMPTY-ZERO, observed). Consequence: a client passing a null or text percentile gets an untyped Python exception instead of a Cypher error, or a silent answer for a different percentile. Repair proposal (not implemented): accept only an int or float (not bool) parameter and raise `InvalidArgumentType` otherwise; refuse a literal null the same way (or answer null, by the decision on intent). Preserve: numeric parameters and literals, `NumberOutOfRange` for numbers outside 0 to 1, the missing-parameter error.

issues.title: Over a list the query holds, a grouping key and count(DISTINCT) merge 1 with true and a list with the string spelling it, while RETURN DISTINCT keeps them apart
issues.block: ### Over a list the query holds, a grouping key and count(DISTINCT) merge 1 with true and a list with the string spelling it, while RETURN DISTINCT keeps them apart Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Grouping an inline list can merge booleans with numbers and lists with their text representation. Grouped counts can undercount distinct values and disagree with RETURN DISTINCT. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 58) Found by: iteration 58 W62 frozen prediction C2 (missed, [PAIRS](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/w62-PAIRS.md)); [clause_combos](models/clause_combos/NOTES.md) `theorem_group_iff_bound_text`, `theorem_group_merges_kinds`, `theorem_group_and_distinct_disagree`, neighbors `theorem_group_neighbors_follow_rule`, `theorem_distinct_json_route_follows_rule`; controls `group-by-kind-column`, `bool-bound-as-word`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, driver 5.3.2 ([probe](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/clauses/probe1.out); [run-time list](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/clauses/probe2.out); [binding](results/clause_combos/20261117T082514Z-binding/receipt.json) `B_int_true_*`, `B_zero_false_*`, `B_list_spelled_*`). `UNWIND [1, true] AS x RETURN x, count(*)` answers `[[1, 2]]` and `count(DISTINCT x)` 1, while `RETURN DISTINCT x` answers `[[1], [True]]`; `[0, false]` the same; `UNWIND [[1], '[1]']` gives one group and count(DISTINCT) 1 but two DISTINCT rows; `WITH [1, true] AS l UNWIND l AS x RETURN x, count(*)` answers `[[1, 2]]`. Passing neighbors: `['true', true]` (two groups), `[1,2]`, `[2,2]`, `[true,false]`, `[1,'x']`, `[[1],1]`. Expected: [query.aggregation.keys](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.aggregation.keys) and [query.aggregation](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.aggregation) ("a nested list or map is different from text spelling it"); openCypher: values of different types are never equivalent. Observed: `translate_return_clause` selects the row through the boolean-flag CASE (`translator.py:30665-30671`, `_unwind_bool_flag` 21457) or CY_LIST_KINDS' JSON column (30660-30664, `_unwind_json_text` 21533), keeping the kind, but adds the plain `sql` (`u0.x`) to GROUP BY (30777); `_expr_aggregation` writes `COUNT(DISTINCT u0.x)` (24431). IRIS binds true as 1 and a list row as its JSON text; the kind column (`x__b` / `x__t` / `x__k`) is never a key. Consequence: grouped counts over lists mixing booleans with 0/1, or lists with their spellings, merge groups with no error; count(DISTINCT) undercounts and disagrees with RETURN DISTINCT. Low: such lists are uncommon; the stored-value root is the Medium bug-cyp-135. Repair proposal (not implemented): add the UNWIND row's kind column to GROUP BY and to the COUNT(DISTINCT) argument whenever the translator emits one. Preserve: single-kind lists, `'true'` vs true apart, the null group. Control `group-by-kind-column` checks the direction in the model only.

issues.title: WITH * drops a relationship variable: a later type(r) fails with SQLCODE -29 "Field 'STAGE1.R' not found"
issues.block: ### WITH * drops a relationship variable: a later type(r) fails with SQLCODE -29 "Field 'STAGE1.R' not found" Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: WITH * fails to carry a relationship variable into the next query stage. Using that relationship afterward produces an internal SQL error. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 58) Found by: iteration 58 W62 frozen prediction C8 (missed, [PAIRS](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/w62-PAIRS.md)). Not modeled. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the same fixture and pin, driver 5.3.2 ([probe](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/clauses/probe1.out), [neighbors](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/clauses/probe2.out)). `MATCH (a:L)-[r:K]->(b) WITH * RETURN a.name, type(r), b.name` fails at Prepare with -29. Passing neighbors: the same without `WITH *`, `WITH a, r, b ... type(r)`, and `WITH * RETURN a.name, b.name`. Expected: openCypher: `WITH *` projects every variable in scope unchanged. Observed: the star branch of `translate_with_clause` (`translator.py:30857-30872`) projects a relationship as `{var}_s`, `{var}_p`, `{var}_o_id` only, so nothing named `r` reaches the next stage. Consequence: the query fails with an error naming an internal stage; no wrong answer. Workaround: list the variables. Repair proposal (not implemented): project each variable as the explicit `WITH a, r, b` does, or rewrite `*` to that list. Preserve: node variables, `WITH * WHERE`, the `CALL ... YIELD` use (2215). Governing statement (iteration 59, review 56-58 m4: moved from query.conformance, which lists documented TCK deviations): [query.with](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.with).

issues.title: WITH *, a.v AS av does not parse: "Expected EOF, got ,"
issues.block: ### WITH *, a.v AS av does not parse: "Expected EOF, got ," Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: A WITH clause combining * with an additional calculated column does not parse. The query is refused even though the projection is valid Cypher. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 58) Found by: iteration 58 W62 C8 neighbor (missed, [PAIRS](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/w62-PAIRS.md)). Not modeled. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the same fixture and pin, driver 5.3.2 ([probe](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/clauses/probe1.out)): `MATCH (a:L) WITH *, a.v AS av RETURN av` raises `CypherParseError ... col 29: Expected EOF, got ,`; `WITH a, a.v AS av` passes. Expected: the openCypher grammar allows `WITH *, items`. Observed: `Parser.parse_with_clause` (`parser.py:333-345`) returns a star WithClause with no items right after `*`. Consequence: a valid query is refused; no wrong answer. Repair proposal (not implemented): accept `, item [AS alias]` after `*` and have the star branch add them. Preserve: `WITH *` alone and `WITH * WHERE`. Governing statement (iteration 59, review 56-58 m4: moved from query.conformance, which lists documented TCK deviations): [query.with](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.with).

issues.title: FOREACH over a literal list with a SET body that reads the loop variable fails "UndefinedVariable: x" and writes nothing
issues.block: ### FOREACH over a literal list with a SET body that reads the loop variable fails "UndefinedVariable: x" and writes nothing Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: A FOREACH update over a literal list cannot resolve its loop variable in SET. The intended per-element updates are refused and nothing is written. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 58) Found by: iteration 58 W62 frozen prediction C6 (partial, [PAIRS](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/w62-PAIRS.md)). Not modeled. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the same fixture and pin, driver 5.3.2 ([probe](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/clauses/probe1.out), [neighbor](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/clauses/probe2.out)): `FOREACH (x IN [1,2] | SET n.f = x)` raises `SyntaxError: UndefinedVariable` and `get_node` still reads `f: 0`. Passing neighbors: `SET n.f = 5` in the body, a `CREATE (:M {v: x})` body (creates 1 and 2), and the empty list. Expected: openCypher runs the body per element (n.f = 2); owner [query.writes](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.writes). Observed: `_to_sql_handle_foreach` (`translator.py:3949-3966`) binds the variable only as `"__foreach_literal__"` plus `foreach_literals`, which the CREATE property path reads; the SET value's translation does not resolve it. This is a different trigger from F-0808 (parameter list, CREATE body). Consequence: the common "set from each element" FOREACH is refused and nothing is written. Repair proposal (not implemented): resolve `foreach_literals` in the SET value translation, applying the SETs in list order. Preserve: the CREATE body, the empty list, literal SET values.

issues.title: A WITH column of coalesce() answers a stored number as its text: WITH coalesce(n.v, n.s) AS x RETURN x gives '3' for 3 and '2.5' for 2.5
issues.block: ### A WITH column of coalesce() answers a stored number as its text: WITH coalesce(n.v, n.s) AS x RETURN x gives '3' for 3 and '2.5' for 2.5 Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: A WITH column using coalesce can turn a stored number or boolean into text. Later calculations and client code receive the wrong type even though the displayed value may look correct. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 58) Found by: iteration 58 W62 frozen prediction D1 neighbor B (missed, [PAIRS](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/w62-PAIRS.md)); [result_decoders](models/result_decoders/NOTES.md) `theorem_with_coalesce_number_is_text`; valid neighbor `theorem_property_reads_roundtrip`; controls `with-coalesce-typed` (the repair), `coalesce-cast-gone`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, IRIS drivers 5.3.2 and 5.4.1, all four readers (Python `execute_cypher`, Bolt with neo4j 6.4.1, `/api/cypher`, `/db/neo4j/tx/commit`) ([5.3.2](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/decoders/decoders-observed-5.3.2-20261117T080853Z.json), [5.4.1](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/decoders/decoders-observed-5.4.1-20261117T080939Z.json) `D1_coalesce`; [binding](results/result_decoders/20261117T082201Z-binding/receipt.json) `*_WithCoalesce_*`). Stored `3`, `2.5`, `true` come back as `'3'`, `'2.5'`, `'true'`; `RETURN coalesce(...)` without the WITH returns them typed. Expected: openCypher: coalesce returns its first non-null argument unchanged. [query.values](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values): "A node property read preserves its stored numeric type". Observed: in the WITH stage, `_scalar_coalesce` (`translator.py:24455-24470`) casts the first argument to VARCHAR. The final RETURN emits `x AS x` (`translator.py:30690-30691`), because `_reads_node_value` (`7644-7678`) recognises a WITH variable only when it is bound to a bare property (`_is_node_value_var` 7592), and `_is_typed_coalesce` (7620-7641) applies only to RETURN items. No decoder touches `x`. Consequence: an ordinary `WITH coalesce(...)` silently returns numbers and booleans as strings on every reader and driver. Repair proposal (not implemented): treat a WITH variable bound to a typed coalesce as a node value (add it to `prop_text_vars`) and drop the stage CAST, so the RETURN reads it through `CY_TYPED` and `parse_prop_text`. Preserve: RETURN coalesce typing, and the CASTs in WHERE. Distinguishing case: `*_WithCoalesce_int` returns `3` after the repair.

issues.title: A CASE column answers a stored boolean as 'true', a stored list or map as its JSON text, and, with IRIS driver 5.4.1, a stored number as its text
issues.block: ### A CASE column answers a stored boolean as 'true', a stored list or map as its JSON text, and, with IRIS driver 5.4.1, a stored number as its text Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: CASE expressions can return stored booleans, lists, maps and some numbers as text. Clients receive serialized values instead of the original property types. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 58) Found by: iteration 58 W62 frozen prediction D1 A (missed, [PAIRS](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/w62-PAIRS.md)); [result_decoders](models/result_decoders/NOTES.md) `theorem_case_bool_is_text`, `theorem_case_container_is_text`, `theorem_case_number_by_driver`; neighbor `theorem_strings_held_everywhere`; controls `case-typed`, `case-prop-text`, `driver-541-native`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced**, both drivers, all four readers plus the native-default engine (`D1_case`, `D1_case_noid`, `D1_ret_case`; [binding](results/result_decoders/20261117T082201Z-binding/receipt.json) `*_RetCase_*`, `*_WithCase_*`). Under 5.3.2: `3`, `2.5`, `'txt'`, `'true'`. Under 5.4.1: `'3'`, `'2.5'`, `'txt'`, `'true'`. A stored `[1, 2]` comes back as `'[1, 2]'`. Expected: openCypher: CASE returns the chosen branch's value with its type. [query.values](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values): `CY_TYPED` decides the type rather than the driver's column type. Observed: `_reads_node_value` (`translator.py:7644-7678`) has no case for CASE expressions, so the raw `p.val` is emitted (`30690-30691`) and is in no decoder list (`query.py:332-349`). Driver 5.4.1 hands raw IRIS numbers to Python as text (`prop_values.py:204-212`). Consequence: silently wrong types on every reader; numbers are wrong on the current IRIS driver. Repair proposal (not implemented): type a CASE whose branches are all node values or scalar literals/parameters through `CY_TYPED(CASE ... END)` plus `prop_text_expr_columns`, including through a WITH. Preserve: string literal branches.

issues.title: A CALL { } subquery that imports an UNWIND variable fails, as does one that imports a node and has no MATCH of its own
issues.block: ### A CALL { } subquery that imports an UNWIND variable fails, as does one that imports a node and has no MATCH of its own Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: A CALL subquery cannot handle some variables imported from the outer query. Valid subqueries using an UNWIND value or a node without their own MATCH fail with an internal SQL error. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 59) Found by: independent review 56-58 item G2 ([review](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-59/REVIEW-56-58.md)). Not modeled. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, both engines (native executor off and on) ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-59/review-repairs/minor-observed-20261117T090528Z.json), keys `G2_*`). `UNWIND [1,2] AS i CALL { WITH i RETURN i*2 AS d } RETURN i, d` fails at Prepare with SQLCODE -29 (`Field 'U0.NODE_ID' not found`); so does `UNWIND [..] AS k CALL { WITH k MATCH (m {id: k}) RETURN count(m) AS c } RETURN k, c`; `CALL { WITH i UNWIND range(1,i) AS j RETURN count(j) AS c }` raises `SyntaxError: Undefined variable: j`. Wider than the review: `MATCH (n:L) CALL { WITH n RETURN n.v * 2 AS d } RETURN d` fails with SQLCODE -23 (`Label 'P2' is not listed`). Passing neighbors: a subquery that imports nothing (`CALL { RETURN 5 AS d }` after UNWIND, two rows) and a MATCH-anchored import whose subquery matches from the imported node (count 0 for a node without edges; iteration 58 W62 C5). Expected: openCypher: a `CALL { }` subquery's importing `WITH` may name any variable in scope, whatever clause bound it; the subquery runs once per incoming row ([query.with](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.with)). Observed: `translate_subquery_call` (`translator.py:14697`, with the `CROSS JOIN LATERAL` at 14607) reads an imported variable as a node id; the cause was not traced further in this iteration. Consequence: the query fails with an internal SQL error; no wrong answer. Workaround: move the UNWIND or the expression outside the subquery. Low: loud. Repair proposal (not implemented): bind an imported scalar (an UNWIND or WITH value) by its value column, and a node by its id, in the lateral subquery; or refuse the import with a clear message. Preserve: the MATCH-anchored import (C5) and its null-row aggregates. Governing statement: [query.with](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.with).

issues.title: ORDER BY over a list the query holds sorts booleans among the numbers
issues.block: ### ORDER BY over a list the query holds sorts booleans among the numbers Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Sorting an inline list treats booleans as numbers when both types are present. The returned order differs from the intended ordering between value types. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 59) Found by: independent review 56-58 item G3 ([review](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-59/REVIEW-56-58.md)). Not modeled. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the same fixture and pin, both engines ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-59/review-repairs/minor-observed-20261117T090528Z.json), keys `G3_*`). `UNWIND [2,'a',null,1.5,true] AS x RETURN x ORDER BY x` answers `1.5, true, 2, 'a', null`; `[2,true,0.5,false]` answers `0.5, false, true, 2`; `DESC` reverses the first. Passing neighbors: numbers alone sort by value; the same list sorted by `WITH x ORDER BY x RETURN x` answers `'a', true, 1.5, 2, null` (iteration 58 C9 held); stored property values follow the kind-first key. Expected: [query.values.sorting](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values.sorting): strings, then booleans, then numbers, then null last; openCypher orderability. Observed: a `RETURN ... ORDER BY` over an UNWIND value sorts a boolean as the number it is bound as (`true` 1, `false` 0) rather than through the kind-first key (`CY_SORT_KEY`, `translator.py:7765-7769`) the `WITH` route uses; the cause was not traced further in this iteration. Consequence: a silent wrong order, only for a list that mixes booleans with numbers; Low. Repair proposal (not implemented): sort UNWIND values through the same kind-first key as the `WITH` route and property values. Preserve: the numeric order of numbers and the C9 order after `WITH`. Governing statement: [query.values.sorting](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.values.sorting).

issues.title: An engine whose schema name differs only in case from the record re-declares empty vector columns unasked and loads the schema classes under its own spelling
issues.block: ### An engine whose schema name differs only in case from the record re-declares empty vector columns unasked and loads the schema classes under its own spelling Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: A schema name differing only in letter case can trigger unintended schema changes. An engine can redeclare empty vector columns and leave their definitions inconsistent with the recorded configuration. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 56); first recorded 2026-11-13 (the audit of 2026-11-15 found it inconclusive: [review record](audits/register-20261115/bugs-review.md#bug-plt-015)) Found by: install.schema.name metadata ("suspected divergence: the deploy rewrites class sources with the engine's spelling"); iteration 56 frozen pair A6 and the post-read source (`_vector_column_action` reads the width with `GraphSchema.get_embedding_dimension` under the engine's spelling; `rewrite_sources` renames the schema classes to it); [install_lifecycle](models/install_lifecycle/NOTES.md) `theorem_unknown_width_altered_unasked`, control `unknown-width-counted`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin (fresh namespaces; [probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-56/install/case_probe.py) → [observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-56/install/case-observed-20261117T070557Z.json); binding cases `D:*`, `B:x_lower_*`, `B:fingerprint_after_lower`, `B:x_setup_after_lower`). (1) I56SD: setup with `schema_prefix="I56W"` at width 8, one 8-wide vector stored. An engine `I56W` at width 16: setup raises `EmbeddingIdentityConflict` and nothing changes (passing neighbor). The same engine named `i56w`: the dry run lists all three vector tables under `alter` (the populated one included), and setup succeeds with no warning and no `needs_manual_migration`; afterwards `kg_EdgeEmbeddings` and `kg_NodeEmbeddings_optimized` are declared 16 while the registry still records 8 for them, and the populated `kg_NodeEmbeddings` stays 8 with its vector (IRIS refused that ALTER). (2) I56SB, record `I56X`: setup by an engine named `i56x` reports `objectscript_failed` for `i56x.LedgerRevision`, `i56x.LedgerStats`, `i56x.SqlProcs` (ERROR #5092: name conflict with `I56X.…` differing only in case), re-creates all 58 routines, and clears the deploy fingerprint; the next setup by the `I56X` engine compiles every class and re-creates 58 routines again. The projected procedure and Cypher kept answering (neighbors). Engines named in either case are accepted, as documented. Expected: names that differ only in letter case are the same schema ([install.schema.name](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.schema.name)), so setup behaves as with the recorded spelling: an empty column at another width is refused without `rewidth=True` (4.7.0, [search.embedding.width](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.embedding.width)), the registry width follows the column, and an unchanged class set is not recompiled. Consequence: a deployment whose configuration spells the schema in another case (`IVG_SCHEMA_PREFIX=rag` for a namespace set up as `RAG`) silently re-declares empty vector columns at its own width, the 4.7.0 hazard the refusal exists for, and leaves registry and column disagreeing, so writes to those tables are refused at either width. Every setup from it also reports three failed classes and recompiles everything. Medium: no stored vector is lost (IRIS refuses the populated ALTER), but the documented refusal is bypassed and the namespace ends inconsistent. Repair proposal (not implemented, not checked): canonicalize the engine's schema to the recorded spelling once the record is read (`same_schema` already accepts it), before any catalog lookup, rewrite or DDL; or read the declared width case-insensitively. Behavior to preserve: case-insensitive acceptance. Distinguishing case: binding `D:lower16_setup` must then raise as `D:upper16_setup` does. Writers/readers affected: `_record_and_initialize`, `_vector_column_action`, `reconcile_recorded_dimensions`, `deploy_packaged_classes`, `RoutineRecord`. Governing statements: [install.schema.name](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.schema.name), [search.embedding.width](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.embedding.width).

issues.title: Setup records an explicitly named schema while IVG's tables sit in one other schema
issues.block: ### Setup records an explicitly named schema while IVG's tables sit in one other schema Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Setup can record a newly specified schema name while the existing graph tables remain in another schema. Engines using the existing data can then be refused until an operator reconciles the configuration. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 56); first recorded 2026-11-13 by code reading (review round 3 R3-reader H3); the 2026-11-15 audit found it inconclusive ([review record](audits/register-20261115/bugs-review.md#bug-plt-026)). Found by: install.schema.existing metadata; iteration 56 frozen pair A3 (missed: the frozen owner reading predicted a refusal); [install_lifecycle](models/install_lifecycle/NOTES.md) `theorem_other_schema_needs_a_name` (as built), control `explicit-refused` (the FR-009 repair). Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin (namespace I56SB; binding cases `B:default_*`, `B:y_explicit_dry`, `B:y_env_dry`, `B:y_explicit_setup`, `B:record_after_explicit`, `B:x_call_after_explicit`). IVG's tables in `I56X` only, the record removed. Passing neighbor: a default engine's dry run and setup raise `IVGSchemaError` naming `I56X` and record nothing. An engine with `schema_prefix="I56Y"` (or `IVG_SCHEMA_PREFIX=I56Y`): the dry run plans `explicit` with `other_schemas` `I56X`; setup records `I56Y` and creates its 18 tables, and from then on an engine for `I56X` is refused (mismatch). Expected: spec 262 FR-009: "when it is another [schema], the engine MUST be refused with an error naming that schema ... and MUST record nothing"; an explicit name settles only the several-schema case. ADMIN_GUIDE's reply table (`explicit`: "named with `schema_prefix=` beside another schema's IVG tables") and the error's own advice ("to start a new IVG Schema beside it, name it explicitly") describe the as-built path: a doc conflict, kept with the spec as the owner does. Consequence: one setup call with an explicit name abandons the existing tables' schema; the application's engine for it is refused until an operator moves data by hand. Low: deliberate, documented in the guide, reversible only manually. Repair proposal (not implemented, not checked): refuse an explicit name when IVG's tables are in exactly one other schema (as FR-009), or amend FR-009 and the owner to the guide's reading; a decision either way. Governing statement: [install.schema.existing](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.schema.existing).

issues.title: kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH lists almost none of the edges among its answered nodes and can answer more nodes than its cap
issues.block: ### kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH lists almost none of the edges among its answered nodes and can answer more nodes than its cap Severity: High · Decision: Open Description: The PageRank-guided subgraph API can return its chosen nodes with most of their connecting relationships missing. It can also exceed its node limit when many seed nodes are supplied, making the result incomplete or larger than requested. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 49) Found by: W56 prediction P1 ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-49/retrieval-PAIRS.md), missed), traced through `kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH` and `Graph.KG.Subgraph.SubgraphJson`; corrected after [review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) item 1, which found that the iteration-49 entry treated the documented cap as the defect and proposed the wrong repair, and found the seeds-over-the-cap case. [retrieval_compose](models/retrieval_compose/NOTES.md) `theorem_filled_cap_expands_only_first_node` and `theorem_admitted_seeds_ignore_cap` (every input), witnesses `theorem_guided_subgraph_drops_edges_among_top_nodes` and `theorem_guided_seeds_exceed_cap`, neighbor `theorem_guided_uncapped_lists_all_edges`; controls `edges-among-answered`, `seeds-capped`, `expand-whole-frontier-at-cap`, `guided-cap-top-k-only` ([prove](results/retrieval_compose/20261117T032018Z-prove/receipt.json), 15 of 15 controls EXPECTED_FAIL). The iteration-49 control `guided-cap-max-nodes` encoded the wrong repair and is withdrawn (its receipts are kept). Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, ObjectScript `SubgraphJson` path (no Arno reader on the fixture): iteration-50 [fixture reproduction](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/review-repro-20261117T031150Z.json) and [binding](results/retrieval_compose/20261117T032153Z-binding/receipt.json) `guided[*]`, `guided_more[*]` (AGREES 45 cases); earlier [observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-49/retrieval-observed3-20261117T024208Z.json) `PG_star_top3`, `PG_star_top7`, `PG_star_top50`. Default graph, star s → a1..a6 plus a1 → a2. `kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH([s], ppr_top_k=7)` answers all seven nodes with the single edge a1 → a2; `ppr_top_k=3` answers s, a1, a2 with only a1 → a2. Seeds s, a3, a4 with `ppr_top_k=1` answer three nodes (the cap is 1) and no edge, although s → a3 and s → a4 join them; [s] with `ppr_top_k=50` and `max_nodes=3` answers seven nodes and only a1 → a2. Passing neighbor: [s] with `ppr_top_k=50` and the default `max_nodes` answers all seven edges. Expected: the docstring (`algorithms.py:956-957`): the subgraph of the seeds and the top nodes within `k_hops`, "capped at `min(max_nodes, ppr_top_k)` nodes"; the [design note](../../docs/dev/notes/enhancements/001-ppr-guided-subgraph.md) (`top_k` a "hard node cap"; acceptance "`len(result.nodes) <= top_k` always"); [algorithms.op.subgraph](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.subgraph): the edges among the answered nodes. The cap itself is intended. Observed: `kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH` calls `kg_SUBGRAPH(seeds + top_ids, k_hops, max_nodes=min(max_nodes, ppr_top_k))` (`algorithms.py:971-973`). `SubgraphJson` admits every seed that has an edge with no cap test (`Subgraph.cls:36-48`), so the seeds alone can exceed the cap; once the count has reached the cap it expands only the first frontier node in ID order, recording that node's out-edges, and stops (`Subgraph.cls:51-99`). With Arno loaded and no `edge_types`, `IRISGraphStore.execute_subgraph` asks `ArnoAccel.SubgraphNativeJson` first (`iris_sql_store.py:2526-2541`); that path was not checked. Consequence: whenever the walk reaches at least `ppr_top_k` nodes (with the default 50, any ordinary graph), the answer is the top nodes with only the out-edges of the alphabetically first one, which may also point outside the answer; with more seeds than the cap the answer is larger than the documented cap. A retrieval caller gets a node list with its relationships missing and no sign of it. High is kept: the method's main output is wrong under its defaults, silently; the cap being intended does not change the edge loss. The over-cap node count alone would be Medium. Repair proposal (not implemented): keep the cap; admit seeds and top nodes only up to the cap (best PPR score first), then list every edge whose two ends are answered (the same repair as bug-plt-114's). Preserve: the cap `min(max_nodes, ppr_top_k)`, the PPR ranking and `ppr_top_k`, argument checks before any read, `k_hops`, and the uncapped answer (all seven edges when the cap exceeds the reachable nodes). Writers and readers: `SubgraphJson` (seed loop, frontier loop, edge list), `kg_SUBGRAPH` and `kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH` (reshape), `IRISGraphOperators.kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH`; the Arno reader must give the same answer. Distinguishing cases: [s] with `ppr_top_k=3` lists s → a1 and s → a2; seeds s, a3, a4 with `ppr_top_k=1` answer one node. Checked in the model only (controls `edges-among-answered` and `seeds-capped` make the departures fail while the uncapped neighbor verifies); not run on the product. Governing statement: [algorithms.op.subgraph.guided](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.subgraph.guided).

issues.title: kg_SUBGRAPH misses edges among the outermost nodes and lists an edge to a node it left out when capped
issues.block: ### kg_SUBGRAPH misses edges among the outermost nodes and lists an edge to a node it left out when capped Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: The subgraph reader omits relationships among its outermost nodes and can include relationships to nodes excluded by its limit. Callers receive an incomplete or internally inconsistent subgraph. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 49) Found by: the source of `Graph.KG.Subgraph.SubgraphJson` while tracing bug-plt-113; [retrieval_compose](models/retrieval_compose/NOTES.md) `theorem_last_hop_edges_missing`, `theorem_capped_subgraph_lists_edge_to_unlisted_node`; control `edge-recorded-after-cap-test`. Iteration 50: `theorem_capped_subgraph_lists_edge_to_unlisted_node` now holds for every node, adjacency and state at the cap ([review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) m9); the repair is checked in the model by the control `edges-among-answered`, which also repairs bug-plt-113's edge loss. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-49/retrieval-observed3-20261117T024208Z.json) `S_star_1hop`, `S_star_cap3`, `S_isolated_seed`; [follow-up](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-49/retrieval-observed2-20261117T024059Z.json) `S_cap*`; [binding](results/retrieval_compose/20261117T024807Z-binding/receipt.json) `subgraph[*]`). Star s → a1..a6 plus a1 → a2: `kg_SUBGRAPH([s], k_hops=1)` answers a1 and a2 but not the edge a1 → a2; with `max_nodes=3` it answers s, a1, a2 and the edge s → a3; a seed with no edges is not answered. Passing neighbor: `k_hops=2` lists a1 → a2. Expected: [algorithms.op.subgraph](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.subgraph): the nodes within `k_hops`, at most `max_nodes`, and the edges among them. Observed: `SubgraphJson` records only edges leaving a frontier node, records the edge before the cap test and quits, and admits a seed only when it has an edge either way (`Subgraph.cls:38-99`). Consequence: callers that read the edge list (context building, `kg_PPR_GUIDED_SUBGRAPH`) miss relationships among returned nodes and can meet an edge whose end is not in the node list. Medium: visible wrong structure, no stored data changed. Repair proposal (not implemented): after the walk, list every edge whose two ends are answered (and drop a crossing edge at the cap); answer an isolated seed as a node. Preserve the hop limit, the cap and the edge-type filter. Governing statement: [algorithms.op.subgraph](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.subgraph).

issues.title: The status report never counts vectors in routed tables, so a namespace whose vectors are all routed reads "absent" and not ready for vector search
issues.block: ### The status report never counts vectors in routed tables, so a namespace whose vectors are all routed reads "absent" and not ready for vector search Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: The status report misses vectors stored in routed tables. It can report that embeddings are absent and vector search is unavailable even while searches over those vectors work. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 52) Found by: iteration 52 W58 frozen predictions R7 and R8 ([pairs](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-52/reports-PAIRS.md)). R8 predicted that the count includes routed rows; the probe answered 0. The registry rows were then read directly. [operator_reports](models/operator_reports/NOTES.md) `lemma_upper_never_route` and `theorem_routed_never_counted` prove it for every name and registry; `theorem_routed_only_not_ready_but_searchable` covers the reader; control `registry-keeps-case`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, in the fresh namespaces `I52` ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-52/reports-observed-20261117T041241Z.json) `s7_routed_vectors`) and `I52B` ([binding](results/operator_reports/20261117T042408Z-binding/receipt.json) `s9_routed_vectors`, `provider:distinct_text`): - After `store_embeddings(..., graph="i52bg")`, the registry holds `kg_emb_b7583a473e7f1826`, and `SELECT DISTINCT table_name` answers `KG_EMB_B7583A473E7F1826`. - `status().tables.node_embeddings` is 0, `vector_index_state` is `absent`, `ready_for_vector_search` is False, and the report says "Vector index: absent". `/server` and `/metrics` say 0 embeddings. - `search_nodes_by_vector(v, graph="i52bg")` answers the node, and `embedding_count(graph="i52bg")` is 1. - The snapshot of the same namespace lists the routed table with its row. - Edge vectors (iteration 53, review round 2 item m7; the iteration-52 attempt used a wrong item key): after `store_edge_embeddings([{"s", "p", "o_id", "embedding"}], graph=g)` the registry holds `kg_eemb_…` (kind `edge`) and `DISTINCT` answers `KG_EEMB_…`. `tables.edge_embeddings` is 0 and `ready_for_edge_search` is False, while `edge_vector_search(v, graph=g)` answers the edge. One legacy edge vector then makes it 1 and True. Reproduced in `I53` ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-53/reports/failed-probe-20261117T044921Z.json) `edge_routed_status`, `edge_routed_search`) and `I53B` ([binding](results/operator_reports/20261117T045659Z-binding/receipt.json) `s17_edge_routed`, `s17:edge_search_g`, `s17_edge_legacy`); `theorem_routed_edges_never_counted`, `theorem_routed_edges_only_not_ready_but_searchable`, control `edge-registry-keeps-case`. Expected: Spec 230 FR-006 and the `_embedding_row_count` docstring: "Counting one table name reported zero for an install whose vectors are all routed — a number an operator reads as 'the embeddings are gone' while a search over the same rows answers fine." The owner [install.status](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.status) says the totals count each registered table of that kind. Doc conflict (review round 2 item m3): ADMIN_GUIDE's field table (`docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:940`) says `ready_for_vector_search` means "the default embedding table holds vectors", which reads as the legacy table only and so would describe today's answer. It was written before routing; spec 230 FR-006 and the code's own docstring are later and say the total counts every table of the kind, so this entry keeps FR-006 as Expected and the owner records the conflict. The same table (`:942`) says `adjacency.kg_edge_count` "equals the edges in `rdf_edges`"; the code caps it (`KGEdgeCount` stops at 10000 and sets `kg_edge_count_capped`), which the model takes as a premise (below the cap). Observed: `_embedding_tables` (`_engine/admin.py:336-354`) reads `SELECT DISTINCT table_name, COALESCE(kind, 'node')` from the registry. It keeps a row only when `is_routed_embedding_table(name)` matches `^kg_emb_[0-9a-f]{16}$` (`security.py:47`), case-sensitive. On IRIS, `DISTINCT` over the default-collation column answers the SQLUPPER form, so no routed name ever matches. This leaves out: - every routed node table (and, by the same test, every routed edge table: `kg_eemb_`); - every HNSW index on a routed table (`hnsw_built` uses the same list). The iteration-13 `routine_reporting` binding replayed this reader on local SQL, whose `DISTINCT` keeps the stored case, so it could not see this. Its correspondence for routed tables is withdrawn at the IRIS reader. Consequence: an operator reads "the embeddings are gone" and not ready, which is the misreport FR-006 was meant to end, while searches on those graphs answer. A deployment that routes every graph (spec 227) always reads `absent`, and a re-embed or restore decided from this report is wasted work. A probe error is never raised, so nothing says the count is partial. Repair proposal (not implemented): compare case-insensitively (`is_route(name.lower())`), or select without `DISTINCT` and deduplicate in Python, or use `%EXACT(table_name)`. Preserve: - the legacy table first; - a kind taken from the registry row; - a row with no kind read as a node route; - a lost table reported, with the other counts kept. Writers and readers: `store_embeddings` and `embed_nodes` (registry rows), then `_embedding_tables` → `_embedding_row_count` and `_hnsw_built` → `status()`, `report()`, `/server` and `/metrics`. Distinguishing case: routed vectors only → `node_embeddings` 1 and ready. Control `registry-keeps-case` checks the direction in the model only; the proposal was not run on the product. Governing statement: [install.status.readiness](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.status.readiness).

issues.title: verify_sync reports drift forever once two graphs hold the same edge; heal=True reports it healed and the next check reports drift again
issues.block: ### verify_sync reports drift forever once two graphs hold the same edge; heal=True reports it healed and the next check reports drift again Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: When two graphs contain the same relationship, the sync check repeatedly reports drift even after a successful rebuild. Monitoring or repair scripts can keep rebuilding an already consistent index. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 52) Found by: reading `BuildNKG` after the iteration 52 W58 freeze (the frozen rows S1-S3 did not cover two graphs); [operator_reports](models/operator_reports/NOTES.md) `theorem_shared_triple_never_in_sync`, `theorem_heal_claims_in_sync_then_drift`; neighbor `theorem_unique_triples_in_sync_after_sync`; controls `verify-counts-distinct-rows`, `nkg-per-graph`, `heal-rereads`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-52/reports-observed-20261117T041241Z.json) `s4_*`, `s5_g_only_edge`; [binding](results/operator_reports/20261117T042408Z-binding/receipt.json) `s4_shared_triple` to `s6_sync_again`): - With `a -R-> b` in the default graph and in graph `i52bg`, `verify_sync()` answers `in_sync` False (3 SQL edges against 2 indexed edges), on the writing engine and on another engine. - `verify_sync(heal=True)` answers `in_sync` True and `healed` True. - The next `verify_sync()` answers False again, and so does the check after another explicit `sync()`. - Every later edge keeps the gap of one. Expected: the `verify_sync` docstring: "`bool(report)` mirrors `in_sync` for `if not engine.verify_sync(): engine.sync()` usage". After a sync on a quiet namespace the check should report in sync. Observed: - `verify_sync` (`_engine/admin.py:813-815`) flags drift when the rows of `rdf_edges` outnumber `^NKG("$meta","edgeCount")`. - `BuildNKG`/`RewritePass` (`TraversalBuild.cls:250-373`) build `^NKG` with no graph dimension and count each (s, p, o) once. `Adjacency.Put` likewise counts a triple only when `^NKG` does not hold it. - So every row whose triple another graph also holds counts once more in SQL than in `^NKG`, permanently. - The heal stamps `in_sync = True` without reading again (`admin.py:839-843`). A multigraph's parallel edges should do the same; the source predicts it, but it was not run. Consequence: the documented `if not verify_sync(): sync()` runs a full rebuild on every check once any two graphs share an edge, which is ordinary for named graphs: 422 s for LDBC SF10 per ADMIN_GUIDE. A monitor alerting on drift never clears, and the heal's own report says the opposite of the next check. Repair proposal (not implemented): compare `^NKG`'s count with `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT s, p, o_id)` (or the count `RewritePass` records), and have the heal read the counts again after its sync. Preserve: - the one-directional rule (`^NKG` over-counts after deletes); - the pending-sync flag; - `indeterminate` on a failed read. Writers and readers: `create_edge`, the bulk paths, `sync()`, `BuildNKG`, `Adjacency.Put`, then `verify_sync` and `SyncReport.__bool__`. Distinguishing case: a shared triple after `sync()` → in sync. Controls `verify-counts-distinct-rows` and `heal-rereads` check the direction in the model only; the proposal was not run on the product. Governing statement: [install.status.verify_sync](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.status.verify_sync). Continuation iteration 57 (strengthened): the shared-triple mechanism is modeled in [adjacency_maint](models/adjacency_maint/NOTES.md) `theorem_nkg_held_elsewhere`: `Adjacency.Remove` keeps the merged `^NKG` edge while another graph holds the triple and removes it otherwise ([binding](results/adjacency_maint/20261117T075252Z-binding/receipt.json) `nkg_n1n2_after_ga` true, `nkg_xa_after` false).

issues.title: engine.capabilities says ^KG and ^NKG are not built on a namespace set up before it held edges, whatever sync() does, until setup runs again
issues.block: ### engine.capabilities says ^KG and ^NKG are not built on a namespace set up before it held edges, whatever sync() does, until setup runs again Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Capability reporting can keep saying traversal indexes are absent after data is loaded and the indexes are rebuilt. Until setup runs again, callers receive a misleading status and some algorithms use a slower path. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 52) Found by: iteration 52 W58 frozen prediction C1 (missed: predicted that the first engine stays stale and a fresh engine is current; both are stale) and the source read after the freeze; [operator_reports](models/operator_reports/NOTES.md) `theorem_markers_never_set_after_empty_setup`; neighbors `theorem_setup_again_sets_markers` and `theorem_setup_with_edges_sets_markers`; controls `sync-sets-markers`, `setup-marks-empty`, `engine-cache-unchanged`, `setup-skips-bootstrap`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-52/reports-observed-20261117T041241Z.json) `s0` to `s2_sync`; [binding](results/operator_reports/20261117T042408Z-binding/receipt.json) `caps_fresh`, `s2:caps_e1`, `s15:*`): - After setup on the empty `I52B`, then edges, then `sync()`, every newly created engine reads `kg_built` False and `nkg_built` False. - The syncing engine reads `kg_built` True and `nkg_built` False. - After `initialize_schema()` runs again, from any engine, new engines read both True. Expected: API reference and docstring: "What the namespace has deployed: the Graph.KG classes, `^KG`, `^NKG`." Observed: - The flags are the `Graph.KG.Meta` markers (`schema.py:2843-2848`). Only `bootstrap_kg_global` writes them, during setup and only when `rdf_edges` has rows (`schema.py:3309-3358`). - `_sync_kg` sets `kg_built` in the calling engine's memory only (`_engine/schema.py:2892`). Nothing sets `nkg_built` except that bootstrap. - `kg_PERSONALIZED_PAGERANK` takes its `Graph.KG.PageRank.RunJson` path only when `kg_built` (`_engine/algorithms.py:342`). Every new engine, the HTTP server's included, therefore takes its other path. The scores observed were the same. Consequence: a report of what is built that is wrong in the common flow (set up first, load afterwards), plus a slower path for personalized PageRank in every new process until setup is re-run. Low: the answers observed were the same, and the documented re-run of setup after an upgrade clears it. Repair proposal (not implemented): have `sync()` record both markers, or derive `kg_built`/`nkg_built` from `KGEdgeCount`/`NKGPopulated` as `status()` does. Preserve: detection once per engine, and refusal (`ClassesUnreadable`) when the classes cannot be read. Writers and readers: `bootstrap_kg_global`, `sync()`, `_detect_capabilities`, `kg_PERSONALIZED_PAGERANK`. Distinguishing case: empty setup, load, sync → a fresh engine reads both True. Control `sync-sets-markers` checks the direction in the model only; the proposal was not run on the product. Governing statement: [install.status.capabilities](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.status.capabilities).

issues.title: The schema diagram draws a relationship whose end has no label as starting or ending at the first label
issues.block: ### The schema diagram draws a relationship whose end has no label as starting or ending at the first label Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: The schema diagram attaches an unlabeled relationship endpoint to the first available label. The visualization can imply a relationship between labels that the data does not contain. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 52) Found by: reading `get_schema_visualization` after the iteration 52 W58 freeze (frozen row H7 held); [operator_reports](models/operator_reports/NOTES.md) `theorem_unlabeled_endpoint_is_first_label`; control `viz-none-distinct`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-52/reports-observed-20261117T041241Z.json) `s16_schema_viz`; [binding](results/operator_reports/20261117T042408Z-binding/receipt.json) `s14:viz`). With labels `A, B, D, Y` (ids 0 to 3): - `UNLAB` between two unlabeled nodes is drawn `0 → 0`, A to A. - `BL` from an unlabeled node to a `Y` node is drawn `0 → 3`, A to Y. Expected: the docstring says a predicate's ends are "those of one edge's endpoints (0 if none)". A diagram reader cannot tell "none" from the first label, because ids start at 0. Observed: `start_label_id = 0` and `end_label_id = 0` are kept when the sampled endpoint has no label, and `label_to_id` numbers the sorted labels from 0 (`_engine/schema.py:2804-2853`). Consequence: Neo4j Browser-style schema views (`/schema` consumers, `db.schema.visualization`) show a relationship attached to an unrelated label. Low: documented in the docstring, and the diagram is sampled anyway. Repair proposal (not implemented): number labels from 1, or give an unlabeled end its own placeholder node. Preserve: one node per label and one relationship per predicate. Control `viz-none-distinct` checks the direction in the model only. Governing statement: [install.status.diagram](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.status.diagram).

issues.title: A status count that fails reads as zero on /server, /metrics and the readiness flags; only the text report says "unknown"
issues.block: ### A status count that fails reads as zero on /server, /metrics and the readiness flags; only the text report says "unknown" Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: When a status query fails, the API and metrics can report zero instead of unknown. Operators may mistake a monitoring failure for missing data or incorrectly decide that an operation is unavailable. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 53) Found by: independent review round 2 (session `d548b72a`, item M2), source reading (`cypher_api.py:498-554`, `status.py:192-214`, `_engine/admin.py:449-476`); [operator_reports](models/operator_reports/NOTES.md) `theorem_failed_census_unknown_only_in_report`, `theorem_failed_vector_count_reads_zero`, `theorem_failed_side_counts_silent`; controls `metrics-marks-unknown`, `readiness-unknown-not-false`, `failed-count-not-zero`, `side-count-marks-unknown`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** in iteration 53 on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, in the fresh namespaces `I53` ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-53/reports/failed-probe-20261117T044921Z.json) users `i53_native`, `i53_part`) and `I53B` ([binding](results/operator_reports/20261117T045659Z-binding/receipt.json) `s19_i53_bnative`, `s19_i53_bpart`). A monitoring user that may read the namespace's database and use the Native API but holds no SELECT on the IVG tables reads a namespace with 6 nodes, 2 edges and 1 node vector: - `status().unknown` names `graph` and `vector_index`, and the report prints "unknown (see Probe errors)" for them. This part works as documented. - `/metrics` prints `ivg_nodes_total 0`, `ivg_edges_total 0` and `ivg_embeddings_total 0` beside `ivg_kg_populated 1`, with no error or unknown sample. `/server` answers `nodes 0, edges 0, embeddings 0` (it lists the errors but drops `unknown`). `ivg status` prints that answer and exits 0. - `ready_for_bfs` and `ready_for_multihop_bfs` are False while `adjacency.kg_populated` is True and the adjacency serves traversals; `ready_for_vector_search` is False. - A user with SELECT on the node, edge and node-vector tables only reads `labels 0`, `props 0` and `edge_embeddings 0` (truth 2, 6 and 1). Each failure is in `errors`, but `unknown` names nothing, and `ready_for_edge_search` is False. - Passing neighbor: with every privilege the same moment reads the true counts, nothing unknown, and every flag True. Expected: ADMIN_GUIDE (`docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:950-958`, 4.6.0 R050): where a probe failed the report must say "unknown" instead of a value; before 4.6.0 "it printed `0 nodes` and `in sync` there", which R050 calls the defect. ADMIN_API says `/server` is "part of `engine.status()`" and `/metrics` is "from `engine.status()`"; the owner [install.status](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.status) says failed counts must not read as invented zeros. A readiness flag "should say whether the operation it names would answer" ([install.status.readiness](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.status.readiness)). Observed: `_count` answers 0 after a failed SELECT and names a part only for the nodes and edges counts (`_engine/admin.py:449-457`); the labels, props and edge-vector counts name none (472-476). `/server` (`cypher_api.py:498-524`) copies the counts and `errors` but not `unknown`; `/metrics` (527-554) prints the counts as gauge numbers with neither. The readiness properties (`status.py:192-214`) compare the counts with 0. Consequence: a Prometheus alert or dashboard reading `ivg_nodes_total 0` sees an emptied graph when only the scraper's role lost a privilege, the pre-4.6.0 misreport R050 removed from the text report. An operator script that gates on `ready_for_bfs` or `ready_for_edge_search` refuses work the namespace can do. A narrow monitoring role is the normal way to give a dashboard read access. Repair proposal (not implemented): carry `unknown` into `/server`; in `/metrics` leave out a gauge whose part is unknown (or add an `ivg_status_unknown{part=…}` gauge); name a part for a failed labels, props or edge-vector count; make a readiness flag unknown (None) when its count is unknown. Preserve: completed counts and the errors list; the text report's behavior. Writers and readers: `_status_probes` → `EngineStatus` → `report()`, readiness properties, `/server`, `/metrics`, `ivg status`. Distinguishing case: the native-only user above. Controls `metrics-marks-unknown` and `readiness-unknown-not-false` check the direction in the model only. Governing statements: [install.status.readers](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.status.readers), [install.status.readiness](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.status.readiness).

issues.title: The ledger line shows "0 commits · 0 rejections" when the ledger counters cannot be read, and reports no error
issues.block: ### The ledger line shows "0 commits · 0 rejections" when the ledger counters cannot be read, and reports no error Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: When ledger counters cannot be read, the status line reports zero commits and zero rejections without an error. Operators can mistake inaccessible audit metrics for an absence of activity. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 53) Found by: independent review round 2 (session `d548b72a`, item M3), source reading (`ledger/client.py:543-575`, `_engine/ledger.py:39-67`); [operator_reports](models/operator_reports/NOTES.md) `theorem_ledger_stats_failure_reads_zero`, `theorem_enable_two_commits_one_reject`; control `ledger-read-reported`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** in iteration 53 on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, in `I53` ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-53/reports/failed-probe-20261117T044921Z.json) users `i53_native`, `i53_part`, `i53_noledger`) and `I53B` ([binding](results/operator_reports/20261117T045659Z-binding/receipt.json) `s18_ledger`, `s19_i53_bnoledger`). After `ledger.enable()`, two commits and one commit refused for a stale head: - `_SYSTEM` reads "Ledger: enabled · head seq 3 · 3 commits · 1 rejections", and `ledger.stats()` agrees. - A user with SELECT on every IVG table except `ledger_stats` reads "enabled · head seq 3 · 0 commits · 0 rejections"; `unknown` is empty and `errors` says nothing about the ledger. Its `engine.ledger.stats()` returns `commits_ok 0` without raising. - Passing neighbor: a user without the Native API resources fails the Meta read, and the report says "Ledger: unknown (see Probe errors)", as documented. Expected: `_ledger_status`'s docstring (`_engine/ledger.py:41-42`): "a read that fails is reported to `errors` … (4.6.0 R160: both reads were silent)", and ADMIN_GUIDE's unknown rule for the ledger (`docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:950-958`). Observed: `GraphLedger.stats()` catches any exception from the `ledger_stats` SELECT and returns the zero counters (`ledger/client.py:549-563`), so `_ledger_status`'s own `except` (60-66) never runs. Consequence: an operator auditing the ledger reads no rejections where there were some, from a role that may not read the counters. Low: it needs a role split at one table, the head sequence still shows, and the ledger's own history is unaffected. Repair proposal (not implemented): let `stats()` raise (or return a flag) when the read fails, so `_ledger_status` reports it and names `ledger`. Preserve: `stats()` on a never-enabled ledger; the Prometheus ledger hook. Control `ledger-read-reported` checks the direction in the model only. Governing statement: [install.status.ledger](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.status.ledger).

issues.title: A node returned whole over Bolt carries each property longer than 200 characters cut to 200 characters and "...", and a long list or map as that cut text
issues.block: ### A node returned whole over Bolt carries each property longer than 200 characters cut to 200 characters and "...", and a long list or map as that cut text Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Reading a whole node over Bolt truncates long property values and can convert lists or maps into shortened text. Clients silently receive different data from a direct read of the same property. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 55) Found by: source reading after the W60 freeze ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-PAIRS.md), post-read T1, prediction written before the probe ran); [bolt_answers](models/bolt_answers/NOTES.md) `theorem_long_property_truncated`, neighbor `theorem_short_property_kept`; controls `no-truncation`, `truncate-at-200`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, the product's own TCP Bolt listener (`start_tcp_bolt_server`, real engine) and the neo4j Python driver 6.4.1 ([post-read probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-observed2-20261117T061633Z.json) `T1_node`, `T1_scalar`; [binding](results/bolt_answers/20261117T062350Z-binding/receipt.json) `D3_wire_*`, `D3_unit_*`). A node with `s201` of 201 characters, `s300` of 300 and `lst` = `[0, ..., 99]`: `MATCH (n) RETURN n` over Bolt answers a Node whose `s201` is its first 200 characters plus `...`, and whose `lst` is the string `"[0, 1, 2, ..., 51, 5..."`. Passing neighbors: a 200-character value comes whole; `RETURN n.s201`, `n.lst` and `properties(n)` answer the stored values over Bolt, `execute_cypher` and HTTP.
