Expected: [access.bolt.graph_values](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.graph_values): a Node carries its stored properties (Bolt structure semantics); USER_GUIDE: a list comes back as the list "through `execute_cypher`, REST and Bolt alike". Observed: `BoltSession._parse_props_field` cuts any value whose `str()` is longer than 200 characters to `str(val)[:200] + "..."` (`bolt_server.py:887-898`); `_recompose_graph_row` builds every whole node from it (`:745-756`). Consequence: a driver application (or a tool such as LangChain or Neo4j Browser) that reads a node's text or list property gets a silently shortened string of another type; the same value read as `n.p` is whole. Medium: silent wrong values at a documented reader. Repair proposal (not implemented; checked in the model only): send the parsed value whole. Preserve the decoding of booleans and JSON values. Distinguishing case: a 201-character string and a 100-element list in `RETURN n`. Governing statement: [access.bolt.graph_values](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.graph_values).

issues.title: Bolt identifies a node by 31 bits of Python's string hash, so two nodes can reach the driver as one, with the second node's properties in both rows
issues.block: ### Bolt identifies a node by 31 bits of Python's string hash, so two nodes can reach the driver as one, with the second node's properties in both rows Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Bolt uses a short, process-dependent hash as a node's identity. Different nodes can appear as one node to a client, and the identity can change when the server restarts. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 55) Found by: source reading after the W60 freeze (post-read T3, [predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-PAIRS.md)); [bolt_answers](models/bolt_answers/NOTES.md) `theorem_hash_collision_loses_first_node` (provider premise P-DRIVER-ID), neighbor `theorem_distinct_ids_keep_both`; controls `id-from-node-id`, `driver-no-id-cache`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, the product's own TCP Bolt listener (`start_tcp_bolt_server`, real engine) and the neo4j Python driver 6.4.1 ([post-read probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-observed2-20261117T061633Z.json) `T3_collide`, `collision`; [binding](results/bolt_answers/20261117T062350Z-binding/receipt.json) `D1_wire_collision`). The probe searched node IDs in the listener's own process until two collided (`i55b_061633_h6045`, `i55b_061633_h27318` → 1939752146), created both with `n: 1` and `n: 2`, and read `MATCH (n:L) RETURN n ORDER BY n.n`: two records, both the second node (`n: 2`, its `id`), `result.graph()` one node. `execute_cypher` answers both nodes. Passing neighbor: two nodes whose ids differ arrive as themselves. Expected: [access.bolt.graph_values](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.graph_values): each node in a result has its own identity (Bolt: a Node's id and element_id identify it within a transaction). Observed: `_node_int_id` is `hash(node_id) & 0x7FFFFFFF` (`bolt_server.py:351-352`); Python salts string hashes per process, and the driver keeps one Node object per id within a result (observed, neo4j 6.4.1). Consequence: with n nodes in one answer the chance of a merge is about n²/2³²: about 1% at 10,000 nodes. The client then shows one node's labels and properties for another and loses the first; graph views merge them. Ids also change on every server restart. Medium. Repair proposal (not implemented; checked in the model only): derive the id from a unique key (and send the node id as `element_id` on Bolt 5). Preserve one id per node within a result. Distinguishing case: the colliding pair above. Governing statement: [access.bolt.graph_values](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.graph_values).

issues.title: Bolt reports a relationship's start and end from the order of the columns around it, not from the stored direction
issues.block: ### Bolt reports a relationship's start and end from the order of the columns around it, not from the stored direction Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Bolt derives a relationship's endpoints from nearby result columns rather than its stored direction. Clients can display or traverse the relationship backward, or receive no endpoints at all. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 55) Found by: source reading after the W60 freeze (post-read T2, [predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-PAIRS.md)); [bolt_answers](models/bolt_answers/NOTES.md) `theorem_endpoints_follow_columns`, general `theorem_one_hop_right_iff_source_first`, `theorem_rel_alone_or_last`; controls `swap-columns`, `no-prev-node`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, the product's own TCP Bolt listener (`start_tcp_bolt_server`, real engine) and the neo4j Python driver 6.4.1 ([post-read probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-observed2-20261117T061633Z.json) `T2_*`; [binding](results/bolt_answers/20261117T062350Z-binding/receipt.json) `D2_wire_*`, `D2_unit_*`). Stored `a→b`: `RETURN a, r, b` reports start a, end b (passing neighbor); `RETURN b, r, a` and `MATCH (b)<-[r]-(a) RETURN b, r, a` report start b, end a; `RETURN a, b, r` reports start b and no end; `RETURN r` alone has no endpoints. Expected: [access.bolt.graph_values](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.graph_values): a Relationship carries its own start and end node (Bolt structure semantics; openCypher `startNode(r)`). Observed: `_recompose_graph_row` takes `prev_node_id` (the node triplet before the column) as start and the triplet after it as end, else 0 (`bolt_server.py:787-799`); the engine's relationship value `{"type", "props"}` has no endpoints. Consequence: a driver application that walks relationships by `start_node`/`end_node`, or draws them, gets the direction wrong whenever the query names the end node first, and no endpoint otherwise. Medium. Repair proposal (not implemented; checked in the model only): carry the stored source and target with the relationship value. Distinguishing case: `RETURN b, r, a` against `RETURN a, r, b`. Governing statement: [access.bolt.graph_values](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.graph_values).

issues.title: Bolt reports every failed query as Neo.ClientError.Statement.SyntaxError, including IRIS errors and driver parameter errors
issues.block: ### Bolt reports every failed query as Neo.ClientError.Statement.SyntaxError, including IRIS errors and driver parameter errors Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Bolt labels every query failure as a syntax error, including database and driver failures. Clients cannot distinguish a bad query from a transient problem that may be safe to retry. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 55) Found by: frozen W60 prediction ER2 (the failure held; its code was not predicted); source `_handle_run`; [bolt_answers](models/bolt_answers/NOTES.md) `theorem_runtime_failure_reported_as_syntax`, neighbor `theorem_gate_codes_follow_rule`; controls `code-by-cause`, `gates-folded`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, the product's own TCP Bolt listener (`start_tcp_bolt_server`, real engine) and the neo4j Python driver 6.4.1 ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-observed-20261117T061246Z.json) `ER2_union_count`, `PA3_*`, `PA6_missing`; [binding](results/bolt_answers/20261117T062350Z-binding/receipt.json) `C_*`). An SQLCODE -1 failure ([bug-cyp-140](#bug-cyp-140)), a driver "Invalid number of parameters" and an undefined parameter each raise `CypherSyntaxError` with code `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SyntaxError`; `/db/neo4j/tx/commit` answers the same code. Passing neighbors: a parse error is a SyntaxError; `IVG_READ_ONLY` gives AccessMode; a wrong key gives Unauthorized. Expected: [access.bolt.errors](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.errors): Neo4j status codes classify a failure by cause (a database failure is a DatabaseError or TransientError; a missing parameter is ParameterMissing). Observed: `_handle_run` sends `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SyntaxError` for every exception, including `result.error` re-raised (`bolt_server.py:612-618`). Consequence: a driver's managed transaction never retries a transient database error, and a client cannot tell a bad query from a failed database. Low. Governing statement: [access.bolt.errors](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.errors).

issues.title: An integer result past 64 bits ends the Bolt session instead of failing the query, and the engine answers it
issues.block: ### An integer result past 64 bits ends the Bolt session instead of failing the query, and the engine answers it Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: A result containing an integer outside Bolt's supported range terminates the connection. The client loses its session instead of receiving a query-level error explaining the unsupported value. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 55) Found by: post-read T5 ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-PAIRS.md)); [bolt_answers](models/bolt_answers/NOTES.md) `theorem_overflow_breaks_connection`, neighbors `theorem_int64_values_arrive`, `theorem_marker_is_smallest`; control `nofit-is-failure`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, the product's own TCP Bolt listener (`start_tcp_bolt_server`, real engine) and the neo4j Python driver 6.4.1 ([post-read probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-observed2-20261117T061633Z.json) `T5_*`; [binding](results/bolt_answers/20261117T062350Z-binding/receipt.json) `B_wire_overflow`). `RETURN 9223372036854775807 + 1 AS x`: `execute_cypher` answers 9223372036854775810; over Bolt the driver raises `ServiceUnavailable` ("defunct connection"), and a raw client sees the socket closed. Passing neighbors: 2⁶³−1 and −2⁶³ arrive; the literal 9223372036854775808 is refused as IntegerOverflow on every reader. Expected: openCypher: integer arithmetic overflows with an error; [access.bolt.results](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.results): a failed RUN or PULL is a FAILURE. Observed: `PackStream._pack_int` falls through to `struct.pack('>q')`, which raises for a value outside int64 (`bolt_server.py:95-105`); `_handle_pull` sends records outside RUN's try (`:640-650`). Consequence: the client loses its connection and any open transaction; `execute_cypher` returns an approximate number. Low. Governing statement: [access.bolt.results](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.results).

issues.title: The Neo4j HTTP transaction route answers a whole node as three text columns, not a node
issues.block: ### The Neo4j HTTP transaction route answers a whole node as three text columns, not a node Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: The Neo4j-compatible HTTP route returns a whole node as separate text columns. Clients expecting a structured node must instead interpret the serialized pieces themselves. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 55) Found by: frozen W60 prediction RT8 (TX) missed ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-PAIRS.md)). Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** in-process (FastAPI `TestClient`) against the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-55/pipeline-observed-20261117T061246Z.json) `RT8_node`, `RT9_*`, `RT10_rel`). `MATCH (n) RETURN n` on `POST /db/neo4j/tx/commit` answers columns `n_id`, `n_labels`, `n_props` with JSON text, as `execute_cypher` does; Bolt answers one Node. Passing neighbor: `RETURN properties(n)` answers the map with node `meta`. Expected: the Neo4j HTTP API answers a node as its property map with node `meta`; [access.surfaces](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.surfaces) (each call does what the engine method does) does not settle which shape a Neo4j route owes. Observed: the route returns the engine's columns unchanged; only Bolt recomposes node triplets. Consequence: a Neo4j HTTP client gets three columns per node and must parse JSON text. Low. Governing statement: [access.surfaces](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.surfaces).

issues.title: A Bolt rollback keeps the transaction's writes: BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK do nothing and every statement commits at once
issues.block: ### A Bolt rollback keeps the transaction's writes: BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK do nothing and every statement commits at once Severity: High · Decision: Open Description: Bolt accepts transaction and rollback commands, but each statement is committed immediately. An application can be told that rollback succeeded while its writes remain in the database. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 56; promoted from F-1601, playbook audit 2026-11-13/14) Found by: playbook arm, F-1601 ([review record](audits/register-20261115/bugs-review.md#F-1601); live `c16-s1-cypher-http`), then "inconclusive, not reproduced" in the 2026-11-15 register audit; reopened by independent review 53-55 item F1 ([review](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-56/REVIEW-53-55.md), probe `rv55b … bolt_tx`, [observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-56/review-probes/rv55b-observed-20261117T064330Z.json)). Model: [bolt_tx](models/bolt_tx/NOTES.md) `theorem_rollback_keeps_writes`, `theorem_rollback_departs_iff_writes`, `theorem_failed_tx_keeps_earlier_writes`, `theorem_reset_or_close_keeps_writes`; neighbors `theorem_commit_agrees`, `theorem_autocommit_agrees`; controls `atomic-tx`, `begin-refused` (the two repairs), `rollback-answers-failure`, `failure-not-sticky`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, the product's own TCP Bolt listener (`start_tcp_bolt_server`, real engine) read by an independent raw Bolt 4.4 client and by the neo4j Python driver 6.4.1 ([binding](results/bolt_tx/20261117T065936Z-binding/receipt.json), AGREES 17; [cells](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-56/bolt/tx-observed-20261117T065936Z.json), prefix `i56b_065931_`). Raw client: `BEGIN, RUN CREATE, PULL, ROLLBACK` answers SUCCESS to all four and a second connection counts 1 node (2 for two CREATEs); after a failing statement, PULL and ROLLBACK are IGNORED and RESET succeeds, and the earlier CREATE stays; RESET or a closed connection inside a transaction keeps it too. Driver: `tx.rollback()`, a failure then `tx.rollback()` (the driver raises only the statement's `CypherSyntaxError`), an aborted `execute_write` (only the application's `RuntimeError`) and a session closed with an open transaction all leave the node. Passing neighbors: `tx.commit()`, a successful `execute_write` and auto-commit `session.run` keep one node, as they should; an empty transaction rolled back leaves none; a failing statement writes nothing. Expected: [access.bolt.transactions](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.transactions): an explicit transaction keeps its writes only if it commits; ROLLBACK, a failed statement, RESET or a closed connection must leave none of them, or the server must refuse BEGIN so the client knows each statement commits on its own (Bolt message specification: BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK; README: "a neo4j-driver compatible server"; the engine's own contract, USER_GUIDE: a caller's rollback removes IVG's writes). Which of the two repairs IVG adopts is the open question [access.transactions](open_questions.md#access.transactions); both make this outcome impossible. Observed: `BoltSession._dispatch` answers BEGIN and COMMIT with SUCCESS and ROLLBACK with SUCCESS after clearing only the pending rows (`bolt_server.py:500-510`); `_handle_run` runs each statement through `engine.execute_cypher` on a connection with no open transaction, so each write commits when the statement finishes (`:567-622`); RESET clears pending rows only (`:662-667`). Consequence: a Neo4j application that relies on a transaction to undo its work keeps partial or unwanted writes, and every signal it gets says the rollback succeeded: a unit of work that fails halfway leaves its first half, and a retry of that unit (the driver's own `execute_write` pattern, or the application's) writes it again. The damage is silent, persisted and on the driver's standard API. High: the same class as [bug-tmp-003](#bug-tmp-003) (a rolled-back write leaves effects), here for every write a Bolt transaction makes. Repair proposal (not implemented, checked in the model only): either hold a transaction's statements in one engine transaction on the session's connection and end it on COMMIT, ROLLBACK, RESET, failure or disconnect (control `atomic-tx`), or answer BEGIN with a FAILURE saying explicit transactions are not supported (control `begin-refused`, design `Refuse`, `theorem_refusal_matches_rule`). Preserve: auto-commit statements (`theorem_autocommit_agrees`) and committed transactions (`theorem_commit_agrees`). Writers affected: `_dispatch`, `_handle_run`, `_handle_reset`, the TCP and WebSocket run loops (connection close). Distinguishing case: the binding's `R_rollback` (count 1 today, 0 after either repair) beside `R_commit` (1 on both). The read-only gate inside a transaction and isolation from other sessions are not checked. Governing statement: [access.bolt.transactions](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.transactions).

issues.title: An unrecorded namespace whose IVG Schema holds this release's SQL objects admits engines
issues.block: ### An unrecorded namespace whose IVG Schema holds this release's SQL objects admits engines Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: An engine can accept a namespace whose setup record is missing if some SQL objects already exist. Incomplete installation steps may go unnoticed until an operation later fails. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 56) Found by: iteration 56 frozen pair A5 (missed: the owner predicts a refusal); `check_first_access` (`schema_name.py:220-242`: with no record, the class `.funcCYCMP` admits the engine; with a record, nothing is probed); [install_lifecycle](models/install_lifecycle/NOTES.md) `theorem_unrecorded_with_marker_admitted`, `theorem_record_admits_without_objects`, control `unrecorded-marker-refused`. Documented in KNOWN_ISSUES ("After an interrupted setup the engine accepts the namespace, and its edge writes fail"), with no register entry before. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin (namespace I56SA; binding cases `A:norecord_marker_call`, `A:record_nomarker_call`, `A:norecord_nomarker_call`). After a complete setup, `^IVG.Deploy("schema")` killed: a new engine's first call answers (0). With the record present and `Graph_KG.CY_CMP` dropped: a new engine answers. Passing neighbor: with both the record and the marker function gone (IVG's classes and globals still there), the first call raises "setup has not finished here"; the next setup records `inferred` and recreates the one routine. Expected: [install.schema.not_ready](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.schema.not_ready): an engine on a namespace with no schema record, or without the current release's SQL objects, raises one error on first access. ADMIN_GUIDE describes the as-built rule ("no record and lacks 4.6.0's SQL objects"). Consequence: an engine runs on a namespace whose last setup stopped after its DDL (grants, Arno revocation, ledger history and the record not yet done), or whose objects were partly dropped; failures surface later as SQL errors (KNOWN_ISSUES: edge writes fail where `Graph.KG.EdgeScan` is missing). Low: documented, and the next setup repairs it. Repair proposal (not implemented, not checked): refuse with no record regardless of the marker (the control `unrecorded-marker-refused`), keeping setup, status and legacy removal exempt; optionally probe the marker when a record exists. Distinguishing case: `A:norecord_marker_call` must then raise "setup has not finished here". Governing statements: [install.schema.not_ready](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.schema.not_ready), [install.setup.resume](../ontology/concepts/install.g5.md#install.setup.resume).

issues.title: A populated vector table at another width beside empty ones blocks setup both ways, and the manual-migration reply never comes
issues.block: ### A populated vector table at another width beside empty ones blocks setup both ways, and the manual-migration reply never comes Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Changing vector width can leave setup blocked when some vector tables are empty and others contain data. The expected migration guidance is not shown, leaving the operator without the documented recovery path. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 56) Found by: iteration 56 frozen pair D2 (partly missed); `_refuse_width_change` (`_engine/schema.py:1564-1599`) checks every vector table: an empty one at another width refuses without `rewidth`, a populated one refuses with it; [install_lifecycle](models/install_lifecycle/NOTES.md) `col_action`, `width_refused`, `theorem_populated_never_rewidened`, `theorem_empty_other_width_needs_rewidth`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin (namespace I56SA; binding cases `W:e8_dry_populated`, `W:e8_setup_populated`, `W:e8_rewidth_populated`, `W:col_after_populated`, `W:rows_after_populated`). All three vector tables declared 16, one 16-wide vector in `kg_NodeEmbeddings`, the others empty. An engine at width 8: the dry run lists `kg_NodeEmbeddings` under `needs_manual_migration` and the other two under `needs_rewidth`; `initialize_schema()` raises `EmbeddingIdentityConflict` (the empty tables); `initialize_schema(rewidth=True)` raises too (the populated one). Nothing changes; the vector stays. Passing neighbor: with all tables empty, `rewidth=True` re-declares them (`W:e16_rewidth`). Expected: ADMIN_GUIDE §11: "plain `initialize_schema()` names the table in `status["needs_manual_migration"]`, with a matching entry in `status["warnings"]`"; the dry run's own lists predict that reply. Consequence: the documented reply and warning never appear for the usual layout (node vectors stored, edge table empty); the operator gets a refusal naming the empty tables and, after `rewidth=True`, one naming the populated table. The documented remedy (delete the vectors, then `rewidth=True`) still works. Low: safe, misleading. Repair proposal (not implemented, not checked): either list a populated table under `needs_manual_migration` and re-declare only the empty ones when `rewidth=True`, or document that a populated table blocks setup at another width until it is emptied. Governing statement: [search.embedding.width](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.embedding.width).

issues.title: An OPTIONAL MATCH node with no match answers labels '[]' and properties '[]' at execute_cypher, /api/cypher and tx/commit
issues.block: ### An OPTIONAL MATCH node with no match answers labels '[]' and properties '[]' at execute_cypher, /api/cypher and tx/commit Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: An unmatched optional node is returned with serialized empty labels and properties instead of null values. Clients inspecting those fields can mistake a missing match for an existing empty node. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 58) Found by: iteration 58 W62 frozen prediction D2 (partial, [PAIRS](uplift/consolidated/iteration-58/w62-PAIRS.md)); [result_decoders](models/result_decoders/NOTES.md) `theorem_optional_node_labels`; control `labels-null`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced**, both drivers (`D2_opt`, `D2_with`; [binding](results/result_decoders/20261117T082201Z-binding/receipt.json) `*_Opt_labels`). The row is `[i, null, '[]', '[]', null]`; Bolt returns `b` as null. Expected: [query.optional](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.optional): the pattern's new variables are null. Observed: `labels_subquery` (`translator.py:1282-1289`) uses `COALESCE(JSON_ARRAYAGG(label), CAST('[]' ...))`, and the properties column also comes back `'[]'`. Consequence: a caller that tests `b_labels` or `b_props` instead of `b_id` sees a node with no labels where there is no match. Repair proposal (not implemented): return NULL for those columns when the node id is NULL. Preserve: a bound node with no labels still returns `'[]'`.

issues.title: A Neo4j HTTP `tx/commit` request keeps the writes of its successful statements when another statement fails, and runs the statements after the failure
issues.block: ### A Neo4j HTTP `tx/commit` request keeps the writes of its successful statements when another statement fails, and runs the statements after the failure Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: A multi-statement HTTP transaction request commits successful statements even when another statement fails, and continues running later statements. Retrying the failed request can repeat writes that already took effect. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 59) Found by: independent review 56-58 item G1 ([review](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-59/REVIEW-56-58.md), probe `rv58 … B`: CREATE, a failing UNION, CREATE in one request answered 400 and kept both nodes). The open question [access.transactions](open_questions.md#access.transactions) had recorded the fact in one bullet since the uplift began, without an owner or register entry. Model: [bolt_tx](models/bolt_tx/NOTES.md) HTTP section: `theorem_http_batch_keeps_writes_around_failure`, `theorem_http_batch_departs_iff`, the rule `theorem_http_rule_is_bolt_rule`; neighbors `theorem_http_all_succeed_agrees`, `theorem_http_read_only_runs_none`; witness `theorem_http_witness_failing_middle`; controls `http-batch-atomic` (the repair), `http-stop-at-failure`, `http-failure-writes`, `http-status-ok-on-error`, `http-read-only-runs-reads`, `read-only-first-only`, `rule-http-keeps-earlier`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** (iteration 59) on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin: the product's FastAPI app (`iris_vector_graph.cypher_api`) in-process through `TestClient`, real engine on USER, counted by a second engine connection ([binding](results/bolt_tx/20261117T090118Z-binding/receipt.json) section H, AGREES; prefix `i56b_090113_`). CREATE, failing, CREATE: status 400, 2 results, 1 error, **2 nodes**; failing then CREATE: 1 node; CREATE then failing: 1 node; two failures among two CREATEs: 2 nodes, 2 errors. Every error carries `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SyntaxError`, whatever failed. Passing neighbors: two CREATEs commit both (200); reads around a failure write nothing; under `IVG_READ_ONLY=true` a request with one CREATE (first or last) answers 403 `Neo.ClientError.Statement.AccessMode` and runs none of its statements (0 results), as ADMIN_API says; two reads under read-only answer 200. Expected: [access.http_transactions](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.http_transactions): one `tx/commit` request is one transaction that keeps its writes only if every statement succeeds; a server that cannot do this must refuse a request it could commit only in part. Sources: the route's own name (`/db/neo4j/tx/commit`, Neo4j's HTTP route that opens and commits a transaction in one request); ADMIN_API's Neo4j HTTP routes and its read-only rule, which already treats the request as one unit ("runs none of its statements"); the same rule the product's Bolt surface owns ([access.bolt.transactions](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.bolt.transactions)), which `theorem_http_rule_is_bolt_rule` derives the batch rule from (BEGIN, the statements, COMMIT). Neo4j's HTTP API documentation is not quoted: fetching it was denied in this session, as in the review's (limitation); the rule above rests on the product's own documents and its Bolt rule. Which repair (one transaction, or refusing multi-statement requests) is the open question [access.transactions](open_questions.md#access.transactions). Observed: `neo4j_tx_commit` (`cypher_api.py:386-404`) runs each statement through `_run_cypher` (`:239-265`, `engine.execute_cypher` on the cached engine with no caller transaction, so a write commits when the call returns), appends one error for an exception and continues with the next statement; the status is 400 when any statement failed. The read-only gate (`:379-384`, `_cypher_writes_under_read_only` `:230-236`) is the only all-or-nothing decision. Consequence: a client that sends a multi-statement request as one unit of work and gets 400 back cannot tell that the statements before and after the failure were committed; a retry of the request writes them again. Medium rather than High (unlike [bug-plt-127](#bug-plt-127)): the persisted partial write is the same class, but the client is told that the request failed (status 400 and an `errors` entry), so it is not silent; the departure needs a request that mixes a failing statement with writes. Repair proposal (not implemented, checked in the model only): run the request's statements on one engine transaction on the cached engine's connection, stop at the first failure and roll back (control `http-batch-atomic`; Neo4j also stops at the failure: `http-stop-at-failure`), or refuse a request with more than one statement that writes. Preserve: a request whose statements all succeed commits all (`theorem_http_all_succeed_agrees`), and the read-only refusal (`theorem_http_read_only_runs_none`). Writers and readers affected: `neo4j_tx_commit`, `_run_cypher` (its one retry, HD-1603, must not re-run a statement inside the transaction). Distinguishing case: the binding's `H_fail_middle` (count 2 today, 0 after the repair) beside `H_all_ok` (2 on both). `/db/{db}/query/v2` (one statement) and a statement that fails after writing part of its own effect are not checked. Governing statement: [access.http_transactions](../ontology/concepts/access.g5.md#access.http_transactions).

issues.title: An IVF index built with metric "cosine" ranks by the raw dot product, so a long vector outranks a perfectly aligned one
issues.block: ### An IVF index built with metric "cosine" ranks by the raw dot product, so a long vector outranks a perfectly aligned one Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: IVF cosine search ranks unnormalized vectors by their raw dot product. A longer vector can outrank a better-aligned vector, giving a different ranking from other cosine-search paths. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 47) Found by: source reading of `IVFIndex.Search` while checking W53's SQL reader ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/sqlprocs-PAIRS.md); not a frozen prediction); [ivf_entries](models/ivf_entries/NOTES.md) `theorem_cosine_ranks_as_dot` (every query and vector pair) and `theorem_cosine_metric_misranks` (witness), controls `cosine-normalized` (the repaired order; the equal-length neighbor `theorem_equal_lengths_agree`, general since iteration 50, still verifies) and `cosine-takes-l2-branch` (which also fails `theorem_cosine_metric_misranks`, named since iteration 50). Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-47/ivf-cosine-observed-20261117T014744Z.json); [binding](results/ivf_entries/20261117T014907Z-binding/receipt.json) `cosine_ivf_search`, `cosine_kg_IVF`). One graph holds `long_off` = (10,0,0,0), `unit_on` = (0.6,0.8,0,0) and `other` = (0,0,1,0); `ivf_build(..., metric="cosine")`, then the query (0.6,0.8,0,0). `ivf_search` and `SELECT kg_IVF(...)` both answer `long_off` 6.0, `unit_on` 1.0, `other` 0.0. Passing neighbor on the same vectors: the route search `search_nodes_by_vector` answers `unit_on` 1.0, `long_off` 0.6, `other` 0.0. Not exercised: `vector_search`'s IVF fallback and `kg_RRF_FUSE`'s IVF leg (the fixture supports `VECTOR_COSINE`, so the fallback is not taken). Expected: the metric's name and default (`ivf_build(metric="cosine")`, reported back by `ivf_info`); `_IVF_METRICS` accepts "cosine" and "dot" as different choices; the route search ranks by cosine, and `VecIndex` was changed in 4.7.0 so that a cosine index scores the cosine. Observed: every branch that scores under "cosine" computes `$vectorop("sum", $vectorop("v*", q, v))`, the same as "dot": centroid choice and entry scoring in `Search` (`IVFIndex.cls:75-78`, `112-115`) and the cell choice in `Insert` (`:200-201`). `ivf_build` clusters the raw vectors with Euclidean k-means whatever the metric and stores them in those cells (`vector.py:1985-2017`, `AddBatch`); nothing divides by a length. So under "cosine" the build's cells follow distance while `Search` and `Insert` follow the dot product ([review 47-49](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-50/REVIEW-47-49.md) m8; see [bug-srch-107](#bug-srch-107)). Consequence: with stored vectors that are not unit length (`store_embedding` accepts any), a cosine IVF index returns a different top k from the route search on the same data, through both the Python and the SQL reader. Unit-length embeddings, which most providers return, are unaffected. Medium: wrong ranking under a confirmed but data-dependent trigger. Repair proposal (not implemented): normalize vectors and centroids at build and insert time for metric "cosine" (or divide by the stored length at search time). Preserve: "dot" and "l2"/"euclidean" scores unchanged; equal-length vectors keep their order. Writers: `ivf_build`, `AddBatch`, `Insert`; readers: `Search` (via `ivf_search`, `kg_IVF`, `ivg.ivf.search`, `vector_search`'s fallback, `kg_RRF_FUSE`). The control `cosine-normalized` checks the repaired order in the model only; the repair was not run on the product. Governing statement: [search.ivf.metric](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.ivf.metric).

issues.title: The engine's fusion reads a cosine IVF index only in the process that built it, so the same call ranks differently elsewhere
issues.block: ### The engine's fusion reads a cosine IVF index only in the process that built it, so the same call ranks differently elsewhere Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Combined search uses the cosine IVF index only in the process that built it. A restart or another worker can silently switch search paths and produce a different ranking for the same request. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 49) Found by: W56 prediction F7 ([predictions](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-49/retrieval-PAIRS.md); held for the building engine, missed for a fresh engine and the operators) and the source of `_fusion_leg_index` / `_index_graph`; [retrieval_compose](models/retrieval_compose/NOTES.md) `theorem_fused_leg_depends_on_building_engine` with neighbor `theorem_other_graph_ivf_not_read`; controls `ivf-scope-persisted`, `hnsw-before-own-ivf`, `ivf-cosine-normalized`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-49/retrieval-observed-20261117T023944Z.json) `leg_index_choice_*`, `F7_engine_building`, `F7_engine_fresh`, `F7_ops_fresh`; [binding](results/retrieval_compose/20261117T024807Z-binding/receipt.json) `choice_building`, `choice_fresh`, `engine_fuse_building`, `engine_fuse_fresh`, `ops_fuse_fresh`). One graph with 62 vectors including L = (10,10,0,0); `ivf_build(..., metric="cosine")` in engine e1. The same `kg_RRF_FUSE(100, 200, 200, 60, [1,0,0,0], "zeta", graph=g)` answers L 31st in e1 (it reads the IVF index, which scores L's dot product 10 first) and 62nd in a fresh engine and in `IRISGraphOperators` (they cannot tell the index's graph and read the server-side cosine search). Passing neighbor: before the IVF build, e1 answers exactly as the fresh engine does. Expected: one answer per call and data; [search.ivf.metric](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.ivf.metric) (a cosine index scores the cosine). Observed: `ivf_build` records the index's graph only in the building engine's `_index_graph_scopes` (`vector.py:2023-2025`); `_index_graph` answers None for an IVF index in any other engine (`:164-176`), and `_fusion_leg_index` prefers an index recorded for the graph over `hnsw` (`:187-225`). The IVF leg (`ivf_search`) also ignores `graph`. Consequence: a service that builds its IVF index in one process and searches in another (or restarts) silently changes the vector leg and the fused ranking; with non-unit vectors, the building process ranks by bug-srch-109's dot product. Medium: wrong ranking, data- and process-dependent. Repair proposal (not implemented): record an IVF index's graph with the index (as BM25 does) and choose the leg by that, and repair bug-srch-109; preserve the BM25 leg's choice and the hnsw leg's graph scope. Governing statement: [search.fusion.leg_index](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.fusion.leg_index).

issues.title: `/vectorSearch` and `/hybridSearch` refuse a query of another width for a graph with no vectors
issues.block: ### `/vectorSearch` and `/hybridSearch` refuse a query of another width for a graph with no vectors Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Vector and hybrid REST searches can reject a query for its width even when the graph contains no vectors. An empty graph produces a misleading compatibility error instead of an empty result. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 49) Found by: W56 prediction Y1 (held for a 768-wide query, missed for a 4-wide one) and the source of `PyOps.vectorToJson` / `getExpectedDimension`; [retrieval_compose](models/retrieval_compose/NOTES.md) `theorem_unrouted_rest_search_refuses_width`; control `unrouted-no-width-check`. Reproduced by: **Partially reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-49/retrieval-observed-20261117T023944Z.json) `Y1_*`; [binding](results/retrieval_compose/20261117T024807Z-binding/receipt.json) `pyops_unrouted_4`, `pyops_unrouted_768`, `engine_unrouted_4`). `Graph.KG.PyOps.VectorSearch` (the `/vectorSearch` body) for a named graph with no route and a 4-wide query raises "Query embedding dimension 4 does not match expected 768"; with a 768-wide query it answers []; the engine's `kg_KNN_VEC` answers [] for the 4-wide query. The REST application itself was not deployed, so the HTTP response is the missing step. Expected: [search.routes.no_fallback](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.routes.no_fallback): an unrouted pair answers nothing, never a width error. Observed: `vectorToJson` checks the width against `getExpectedDimension`, which answers `getDefaultDimension()` = 768 for a pair with no route (`PyOps.cls:136-141`), before the route is looked up. Consequence: a REST search of a graph that has no vectors yet fails with a misleading width error instead of an empty answer. Low. Repair proposal (not implemented): look the route up first and answer [] for an unrouted named graph. Governing statement: [search.fusion.rest](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.fusion.rest).

issues.title: `/hybridSearch` replaces a fusion constant of 0 with 60
issues.block: ### `/hybridSearch` replaces a fusion constant of 0 with 60 Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: Hybrid search replaces an explicitly supplied fusion constant of zero with the default value. Callers receive a different ranking configuration from the one they requested. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 49) Found by: the source of `PyOps.HybridSearch` (`c = int(c) if c else 60`, `PyOps.cls:374`) after W56 F8; [retrieval_compose](models/retrieval_compose/NOTES.md) `theorem_hybrid_c_zero_becomes_60`; control `hybrid-c-kept`. Reproduced by: **Partially reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-49/retrieval-observed-20261117T023944Z.json) `F8_pyops_hybrid_G_c0`; [binding](results/retrieval_compose/20261117T024807Z-binding/receipt.json) `pyops_hybrid_c0`): `HybridSearch(q, "zeta", 100, 0, g)` answers exactly the scores of `c = 60`. The REST route's own argument handling was not exercised. Expected: the caller's constant (the SQL procedure and the engine accept 0 and score 1/rank). Consequence: a caller asking for c = 0 silently gets c = 60. Low (an unusual value). Repair proposal (not implemented): default only a missing `c`. Governing statement: [search.fusion.surfaces](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.fusion.surfaces).

issues.title: The SQL function kg_BM25 answers an empty list for k of 0 or less, while bm25_search and ivg.bm25.search refuse it
issues.block: ### The SQL function kg_BM25 answers an empty list for k of 0 or less, while bm25_search and ivg.bm25.search refuse it Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: The SQL BM25 function accepts a zero or negative result limit by returning an empty list. Other entry points reject that argument, so SQL callers can mistake an invalid request for a search with no matches. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 56) Found by: independent review round 3 (session c68a5c59, minor "kg_BM25 vs bm25_search"). Formal: [bm25_scoring](models/bm25_scoring/NOTES.md) `taken`, `entry_k`, `theorem_sql_k_nonpositive_empty_others_refuse` (general over k and the ranked count); controls `sql-entry-validates-k` (the repair) and `nonpositive-k-takes-all`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, iteration 56 ([binding](results/bm25_scoring/20261117T070040Z-binding/receipt.json) cases `k:*`). Over one built index and the query `graph`: `SELECT Graph_KG.kg_BM25(name, 'graph', 0)` and `(…, -1)` answer `[]`; `bm25_search(name, 'graph', 0)` and `-1` raise a pydantic `ValidationError` (k ≥ 1); `CALL ivg.bm25.search(name, 'graph', 0)` and `-1` raise `ValueError`. Neighbor: k 1 answers the same single top document on all three. Expected: the three readers apply one argument rule. The translator (`_translate_bm25_search`, translator.py 3161-3166) says the procedure validates "the model bm25_search runs: a name and a query that are not blank, and k of 1 or more (4.6.5)"; ADMIN_GUIDE 256 and 433 list `kg_BM25` as the SQL form of the same search. Observed: `SqlProcs.kgBM25` (131-135) checks the SELECT privilege and calls `BM25Index.SearchProc` → `Search` → `SearchCore`, which quits its result walk when `count >= k` before taking a document (336-345), so any k ≤ 0 gives `[]` with no error. k is not validated on the SQL path. Consequence: a direct SQL caller that passes 0 or a negative k (for example a computed limit) silently gets no documents, where the Python and Cypher entries report the bad argument. Low: the caller passes an invalid argument and the answer is empty, not wrong documents. Repair proposal (not implemented): refuse k < 1 in `SqlProcs.kgBM25` (or `SearchProc`) with an SQL error naming k, as the other two readers do. Preserve: every k ≥ 1 answer (the binding's `sql:*`, `tie:sql` and `k:sql@1` cases). Distinguishing case: `k:sql@0` refused instead of `[]` (control `sql-entry-validates-k` is this repair in the model; not run against a patched product). Governing statement: [search.bm25](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.bm25).

issues.title: No quarantined vector can be placed through the IRIS DB-API driver
issues.block: ### No quarantined vector can be placed through the IRIS DB-API driver Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: The documented recovery operation for quarantined vectors fails through the normal IRIS DB-API connection. An operator cannot make those vectors searchable through that client path. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 56) Found by: iteration 56 frozen pair F1 (missed: neither the placement nor a named refusal occurs); `_quarantined_row` (`_engine/schema.py:2072-2095`) returns `row[0]`, `row[1]`, `row[2]` after `cursor.close()`, which `get_embedding_identity` (1050-1053) explicitly avoids ("The IRIS driver's DataRow is a live view onto the cursor: reading it after close() raises Cursor closed"); [install_lifecycle](models/install_lifecycle/NOTES.md) `theorem_unreadable_row_never_placed`, premise P-DATAROW-CLOSED, control `row-read-materialized`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin (namespace I56SA, intersystems-irispython 5.3.2; binding cases `Q:place_*`). Six quarantined rows (q1 and q2, widths 4 and 3, dtypes DOUBLE and FLOAT), a route (`g1`, `qm`) of width 4 and node q1 in `g1`: every `place_quarantined(q_rowid, graph=..., model_key="qm")` raises `ProgrammingError: Cursor closed; Details: DataRow is inaccessible and/or Cursor is closed`, whatever the route, width, dtype or node; the quarantine keeps six rows and the route none. Passing neighbors: a q_rowid with no row raises the documented `ValueError`; `list_quarantine()` lists six and refuses an unknown reason. With `_quarantined_row` materializing the row first (the proposed repair, substituted in the harness only), every documented outcome holds (`QR:*`): no route, width and dtype conflicts, node not in the graph refused with the row kept; the valid row placed (quarantine −1, route +1); a second vector for the same node refused by the route's key (SQLCODE -119) with the row kept; totals conserved; no route created. Expected: [search.quarantine.placement](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.quarantine.placement) and ADMIN_GUIDE §9: an operator places each quarantined vector, naming its graph; placement succeeds when the route and node fit, and refuses naming the reason otherwise. Consequence: the only documented way out of quarantine does not work over the DB-API driver (the ordinary client connection), so vectors the 4.0.0 migration quarantined stay unsearchable; the error names a communication failure rather than a reason. Medium: an operator recovery path is unusable; no data is lost (the row stays). Embedded Python (irispython inside IRIS) was not tried; the unit tests use a mocked cursor. Repair proposal (not implemented; checked only as a harness substitution, `QR:*`): materialize the row before closing the cursor (`values = None if row is None else tuple(row)`), as `get_embedding_identity` does. Behavior to preserve: refusal order and the insert-then-delete transaction. Governing statement: [search.quarantine.placement](../ontology/features/search.g5.md#search.quarantine.placement).

issues.title: DijkstraPath with two empty endpoints answers a zero-length path through the NUL character
issues.block: ### DijkstraPath with two empty endpoints answers a zero-length path through the NUL character Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: A shortest-path call with two empty endpoints returns a zero-length path through a nonexistent node. Invalid input produces a plausible success result instead of no path or an error. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 53) Found by: iteration 53 Part B, after reading `DijkstraJson`'s endpoint tests (not a frozen prediction; DJ10 covered equal ids only); [sql_procs](models/sql_procs/NOTES.md) `theorem_sql_empty_endpoints_zero_path`, neighbors `theorem_dijkstra_endpoint_neighbors`; control `nul-read-as-empty`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-53/sqlprocs/sqlprocs-observed-20261117T050743Z.json) `dijkstra.empty_both`; [binding](results/sql_procs/20261117T051429Z-binding/receipt.json) `dj_empty_both`). `SELECT Graph_KG.DijkstraPath('', '', '', 9999, 10, 'out', '', 'g')` answers `{"nodes":["\u0000"],"rels":[],"costs":[],"length":0,"totalCost":0.0}`. Neighbors: `DijkstraPath('', 'd', …)` answers `{}`; the Cypher CALL with `''` raises "from parameter not supplied". Expected: an empty source or target answers no path; "direct native empty endpoints answer no path" ([algorithms.op.paths.weighted](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.paths.weighted); the parent path-search rule says the same). Observed: an SQL `''` reaches the procedure body as `$Char(0)`; `DijkstraJson` (`TraversalPaths.cls:262-275`) tests `srcId = ""`, which `$Char(0)` fails, then `srcId = dstId`, which it passes, and answers the empty path of that node. `EdgeScan.MatchEdges` and `GraphKey` already map `$Char(0)` to "" (R269). Consequence: a SQL caller that passes empty parameters gets a path of length 0 and cost 0 with a node id no graph holds, instead of no path. Repair proposal (not implemented): translate `$Char(0)` to "" for both endpoints at the top of `DijkstraJson` (or in `DijkstraPath`), as `MatchEdges` does. Preserve: equal non-empty endpoints answer the empty path. Distinguishing case: the call above answers `{}` (control `nul-read-as-empty`). Governing statement: [algorithms.op.paths.weighted](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.paths.weighted).

issues.title: shortest_path_length(a, b, ..., 'in') answers the outgoing length from a to b, not execute_shortest_path's incoming one
issues.block: ### shortest_path_length(a, b, ..., 'in') answers the outgoing length from a to b, not execute_shortest_path's incoming one Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: The length-only shortest-path API ignores an incoming-direction request and measures the outgoing path. Direct callers can receive the wrong distance or be told that a valid incoming path does not exist. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 57) Found by: iteration 57 W61 frozen prediction S2 (held: the owner working assumption of [algorithms.op.paths.direction](open_questions.md#HD-1003) names the gap); [traversal_strategy](models/traversal_strategy/NOTES.md) `theorem_in_length_differs`, neighbor `theorem_lengths_agree_out_both`; controls `length-in-reversed` (the repair), `esp-no-reversal`, `length-both-as-out`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([binding](results/traversal_strategy/20261117T074632Z-binding/receipt.json) `sp_in_p3_p1`, `sp_in_p1_p3`; neighbors `sp_out_p1_p3`, `sp_both_p3_p1`). On the default-graph chain p1-R->p2-R->p3: `execute_shortest_path(p3, p1, [], 5, 'in')` answers length 2 and `shortest_path_length(p3, p1, [], 5, 'in')` answers -1; the reverse pair `(p1, p3, 'in')` answers -1 and **2**. Neighbors: 'out' and 'both' answer the same length on both readers. Expected: `IRISGraphStore.shortest_path_length`'s docstring: "what execute_shortest_path's paths' length is, without them"; [algorithms.op.paths](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.paths) "The search can follow the edges, go against them, or do both"; the working assumption "Require IRISGraphStore.shortest_path_length to reverse 'in' as execute_shortest_path does". Observed: `shortest_path_length` (`iris_sql_store.py:2162-2181`) passes the direction unchanged to `TraversalPaths.ShortestLength` (`TraversalPaths.cls:117-175`), which sets `tBoth = (direction = "both")` and otherwise searches the source's out entries and the target's in entries, i.e. 'in' is walked as 'out'. `execute_shortest_path` (`:2197-2207`) reverses 'in' itself. Consequence: a direct store caller asking the incoming distance gets the outgoing one: a false "no path" where an incoming path exists, and a positive length where only an outgoing path exists. Cypher is not affected: its length-only route (`query.py:3620-3626`) is taken only for 'out' and 'both'. Severity Low because the only affected entry point is the public store method (no Cypher, SQL or HTTP caller reaches it with 'in'), though the wrong answer is silent and can be positive. Repair proposal (not implemented): in `shortest_path_length`, for 'in' call `ShortestLength(target, source, ..., 'out', graph)` as `execute_shortest_path` reverses; and make `ShortestLength` refuse any direction outside {out, both} (`CheckDirection`). Preserve: 'out'/'both' lengths unchanged (`theorem_lengths_agree_out_both`). Distinguishing case: `sp_in_p1_p3` answers -1 after the repair (control `length-in-reversed`). Governing statement: [algorithms.op.paths](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.paths).

issues.title: execute_bfs with a direction other than exactly "out", "in" or "both" answers an undirected walk from the edge table ("OUT", "sideways") or a walk of the edge table instead of the adjacency index ("outbound", "inbound")
issues.block: ### execute_bfs with a direction other than exactly "out", "in" or "both" answers an undirected walk from the edge table ("OUT", "sideways") or a walk of the edge table instead of the adjacency index ("outbound", "inbound") Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: The breadth-first search API accepts unknown direction strings and falls back to a different traversal. A typo can return plausible but unintended neighbors instead of being rejected. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 57) Found by: iteration 57 W1 source read after the W61 freeze (not a frozen prediction; B5 covered the three exact directions); [traversal_strategy](models/traversal_strategy/NOTES.md) `theorem_unknown_direction_walks_both`; controls `sql-unknown-dir-as-out`, `types-ignore-case`, `bfsfast-case-insensitive`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([binding](results/traversal_strategy/20261117T074632Z-binding/receipt.json) `os_dirtext_OUT`, `os_dirtext_sideways`, `os_dirtext_outbound`, `os_dirtext_inbound`; neighbors `os_out_any_2`, `os_both_any_2`). From `s` on the mix graph, hops 2: `execute_bfs(s, [], 2, "OUT", 0)` answers `a 1 R, b 1 Q, c 1 "", d 2 Q, x 2 R` — the undirected rows (`os_both_any_2`) with an empty type for `c`, reached only against an edge; `"sideways"` answers the undirected rows with no error; `"outbound"` / `"inbound"` answer the out / in rows. Each of the four calls the SQL fallback (`fallback_calls` 1); the three exact directions do not. Expected: `execute_bfs`'s docstring: the rows "walked in `direction`"; the path routines' policy for directions ([algorithms.op.paths.direction](open_questions.md#HD-1003): refuse a direction outside {out, in, both}, as `DijkstraJson`'s `CheckDirection` does). `_select_bfs_strategy` already reads `"outbound"` and case-insensitively. Observed: `BFSFast` (`TraversalBFS.cls:107-208`) compares `direction = "out"` / `"in"` / `"both"` exactly, so any other text walks no edge and `BFSFastJsonSorted` answers `SORTED:0`; `_run_objectscript_bfs` (`iris_sql_store.py:2059-2065`) then calls `_sql_bfs_fallback`, whose else branch (`:2132-2149`) reads both columns for every text but out/outbound/in/inbound; `_bfs_rows` (`:1897-1898`) lowercases the text for `ReachTypes`, so "OUT"'s types are read as outgoing while its depths are undirected. Consequence: a caller (or a protocol client passing a user-supplied direction) gets plausible rows for a direction the store does not know: an undirected neighbourhood for "OUT", with blank types; and "outbound"/"inbound" are answered from `rdf_edges` rather than `^KG`, so they can differ from "out"/"in" wherever the two disagree (an undeclared index, W2's domain). Low: the in-tree Cypher caller passes only out/in/both. Repair proposal (not implemented): normalise once at `execute_bfs` (lowercase; outbound -> out, inbound -> in) and refuse anything else with `ValueError`, before choosing a strategy. Preserve: the three exact directions' rows (`theorem_os_rows_eq_sql_rows`). Distinguishing case: `os_dirtext_OUT` answers the `os_out_any_2` rows (control `sql-unknown-dir-as-out` shows the model decision). Governing statement: `execute_bfs` docstring; [query.paths.varlength](../ontology/features/cypher.g5.md#query.paths.varlength).

issues.title: While sync() rebuilds the adjacency index, traversal reads in other sessions see it purged: khop answers the seed alone, a path length answers no path, and BFS answers with blank types
issues.block: ### While sync() rebuilds the adjacency index, traversal reads in other sessions see it purged: khop answers the seed alone, a path length answers no path, and BFS answers with blank types Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Traversal readers can see an empty or partially rebuilt adjacency index while another session runs sync. They return incomplete paths and neighborhoods instead of waiting or reporting that a rebuild is in progress. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 57) Found by: accident, then on purpose: the builder's re-run of the `traversal_strategy` binding overlapped worker W2's binding, which ran `sync()` ([DISAGREES receipt](results/traversal_strategy/20261117T075247Z-binding/receipt.json), 12 cases answered by the SQL fallback with blank types); W61 workflow 3 asked about a rebuild during other work, but no frozen prediction covered reads during a rebuild. Formal: [rebuild_reads](models/rebuild_reads/NOTES.md) `theorem_reader_sees_seed_alone` (general), neighbor `theorem_quiet_reader_sees_rows`; controls `rebuild-swaps` (the repair), `refill-keeps-old`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin: [race probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-57/rebuild_race/race_probe.py) ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-57/rebuild_race/race-observed-20261117T075352Z.json): 897 of 15,944 reads during four `sync()` calls departed) and the [binding](results/rebuild_reads/20261117T075627Z-binding/receipt.json) (AGREES with the as-built model: 4,481 of 58,520 reads during `sync()` saw the seed alone). Default graph `s-R->a, a-Q->b, s-R->c`, declared (functional) index: quiet, `khop(s, 2)` answers s, a, b, c and `shortest_path_length(s, b)` answers 2 (every quiet read); during another process's `sync()`, `khop` answers `[s]`, the length answers -1, and `execute_bfs(s)` answers the right nodes with every type blank (its ObjectScript walk found no edge, the SQL fallback answered the nodes from the rows, and `ReachTypes` read the purged index). Expected: [structure.rebuild](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.rebuild) "running it again is safe", and with a declared index "the adjacency never needs it"; [structure.drift](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.drift); [algorithms.op.khop](../ontology/features/algorithms.g5.md#algorithms.op.khop) "A walk that fails raises an error rather than answer empty". BuildKG's own comment: "destroyed adjacency looks to every reader like a graph with no edges". The live `^NKG` rewrite is held to "no reader sees an empty or invented ^NKG during the rebuild" (`tests/e2e/test_nkg_live_rewrite_e2e.py`). Observed: `TraversalBuild.BuildKG` (lines 30-140) takes the writers' lock `^IVG.AdjW` shared (`Adjacency.BeginRebuild`, 814-822), which readers never take, and with a declared index runs `rdfedges.%BuildIndices($lb("idxedgesadj"), 1, …)` after its transaction: the purge empties `^KG("out"/"in")` and the callbacks refill it row by row (up to 8 jobs). `BFSFast` and `TraversalPaths.ShortestLength` read `^KG` directly. Consequence: a silent wrong answer, not an error, for every adjacency reader in every other session for the length of a rebuild (about three seconds per `sync()` on this small fixture; proportional to the edge count): k-hop, BFS types, unweighted path lengths, and by the same mechanism degree, PPR and the native Cypher reads over `^KG` (not exercised). `sync()` is the documented step after bulk loads and erasures, and it rebuilds a declared index that needs no rebuild. Medium: silent and reachable in ordinary operation, but transient and repaired when the rebuild ends. Repair proposal (not implemented): with a declared index skip the edge-index rebuild in `sync()` (structure.rebuild already says it is not needed), or build into a shadow tree and swap once, as `RewriteNKG` does for `^NKG`. Preserve: the end state equals the rows (`theorem_end_is_rows`, `adjacency_maint::theorem_incremental_equals_rebuild`). Distinguishing case: no seed-alone read during `sync()` (control `rebuild-swaps`; proved for the repair: `theorem_swap_shows_old_or_rows`). Governing statement: [structure.rebuild](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.rebuild). Iteration 59 (review 56-58 evidence): the native Cypher reader is now exercised and departs too, and the writers' side is the passing neighbor. The reviewer's race probe ([copy](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-59/review-repairs/race_repro.py), fresh prefix `i59r_`) reproduced it afresh ([observation](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-59/review-repairs/race-observed-090546.json)): of 6,238 reads during three `sync()` calls, 462 answered `MATCH (s)-[*1..2]->(b) RETURN count(DISTINCT b)` = 0 on a `native_cypher=True` engine together with k-hop = the seed alone and path length −1 (4 more mixed reads departed), where every quiet read answers 3; all 40 `create_edge` calls made during `sync()` were still in `^KG("out")` and answered by k-hop afterwards. So the race loses reads, not writes. Found by: independent review 56-58 (its own probe `race-084644`: 467 of 6,413); reproduced by: this run.

issues.title: khop2_count_fast answers the sum of the middle nodes' out-degrees right after sync(), counting the source and repeated targets, and the walked count after any unrelated write
issues.block: ### khop2_count_fast answers the sum of the middle nodes' out-degrees right after sync(), counting the source and repeated targets, and the walked count after any unrelated write Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: The fast two-hop count can count repeated targets and the starting node immediately after a rebuild. An unrelated write changes which counting path runs, so the answer can change without the neighborhood changing. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 57) Severity reasoning: read-only, no data changed; but the documented meaning ("How many nodes are first reached at the second outbound hop from `node_id`", API_REFERENCE; docstring: "neither `node_id` nor a direct neighbour is counted") holds only while the stats are stale, and the same call on the same data answers differently depending on whether any write anywhere in the namespace happened since the last sync(); a caller cannot tell which answer it got. Found by: iteration 57 W61 R2 (frozen prediction expected the upper bound from test_460_r284; the departure is against the method's own documentation); [adjacency_maint](models/adjacency_maint/NOTES.md) `witness_fast_overcounts` (diamond 2 vs 1; back edge 1 vs 0), `theorem_two_hop`; controls `fresh-ignores-stamp`, `walk-counts-source-and-first-hop`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([binding](results/adjacency_maint/20261117T075252Z-binding/receipt.json) and the builder's [re-run](results/adjacency_maint/20261117T075646Z-binding/receipt.json), cases `two_hop_after_sync`, `two_hop_after_write`). Default graph, edges on Q57: s2→m1, s2→m2, m1→y, m1→s2, m2→y. Right after sync() (stamps `^IVG.BuiltFrom("deg2p"/"deg2p_exact")` = `^KG("__version")`): `khop2_count_fast(s2,"Q57")` = 3, `khop2_count_exact` = 1. After `create_edge(z1, R57, z2)` (unrelated): both 1. Expected: fast answers the number first reached at hop 2 (1), like exact, fresh or stale; or its documentation says "an upper bound while the stats are current". Observed: `KHop2CountFast` (TraversalKHop.cls:214-225) returns `^KG("deg2p",0,src,pred)` while `Fresh("deg2p")`; `Build2HopStats` (TraversalBuild.cls:939-994) stores the sum over middle nodes of their out-degree on the predicate ("an upper bound"), counting the source reached back, first-hop nodes and a target once per middle node. Stale, it walks (`KHop2Count`, 67-133), excluding source and first hop, each target once. Consequence: callers reading the fast count as a count over-count right after a sync and get a different value after any write. Repair proposal (not implemented): document fast as an upper bound while current, or have it read `deg2p_exact` (BuildNKG already builds it) when fresh. Preserve: stale stats never read (R284). Distinguishing case: `two_hop_after_sync` [3, 1] becomes [1, 1] (or the doc names 3). Governing statement: structure.rebuilt (two-hop statistics are a rebuilt store); docs/API_REFERENCE.md §khop2_count_fast. Affected owner: [structure.rebuilt.stamp](../ontology/features/graph-structure.g5.md#structure.rebuilt.stamp) (the reader rule holds; the value it gates departs), algorithms.op.khop.

issues.title: A distinct-target count answers at least 11 for any window that holds a target, so one target reads as 11
issues.block: ### A distinct-target count answers at least 11 for any window that holds a target, so one target reads as 11 Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: The approximate distinct-target counter reports at least eleven for any nonempty window. Small groups are substantially overcounted, so a dashboard cannot reliably distinguish one target from several. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 51) Found by: iteration 51 W57 frozen prediction D1 (missed; [pairs](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-51/stats-PAIRS.md)) and the source read after the freeze; [temporal_stats](models/temporal_stats/NOTES.md) `theorem_distinct_nonempty_at_least_eleven`, `theorem_distinct_one_target_is_eleven`; controls `small-range-correction`, `no-empty-guard`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-51/stats-observed-20261117T034349Z.json) `D_d1`, `D_d3`, `D_dbig`, `A4_rbc_distinct`; [binding](results/temporal_stats/20261117T040000Z-binding/receipt.json) `distinct_d_*`, `distinct_a_*`). Three edges to one target answer 11; three distinct targets answer 11, 12 or 13 depending on their names; 100 distinct targets answered 69, 91, 88 and 69 in four runs with different names; a committed single edge answers 11. Passing neighbors: a window with nothing answers 0, and a delete rebuilds the sketch (12 to 11 after deleting one of two targets). Expected: "An approximate count from the HyperLogLog sketches ... (about 26% error)" (`_engine/temporal.py:1088-1093`, `TemporalIndex.cls:628-631`, `docs/API_REFERENCE.md` `get_distinct_count`). Observed: `GetDistinctCount` answers `$Number(0.673 * 16 * 16 / Z, 0)` with Z the sum of 2^-register over 16 registers, and 0 only when every register is zero (`TemporalIndex.cls:671-681`). With one register set Z is at most 15.5, so the answer is at least 11 (11.1 rounded); there is no small-range (linear counting) correction. The model proves the bound for every sketch. Consequence: a dashboard asking how many distinct peers a source reached reads 11 for one peer and cannot tell 1 from 10; below about 40 targets the error is far above a quarter. With 16 registers the error is also about 26% at one standard deviation for large counts, so single answers near 100 can be 30% off. Repair proposal (not implemented): apply HyperLogLog's small-range correction (when the estimate is below 2.5 × 16 and some register is zero, answer 16 × ln(16 / zero registers)), or count exactly below a threshold. Preserve: 0 for an empty window, the merge over touched buckets, the rebuild on delete. Distinguishing case: one target answers 1 (control `small-range-correction` checks the model's direction only; the proposal itself was not run on the product). Governing statement: [temporal.stats.distinct](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.stats.distinct).

issues.title: Two different attribute sets can intern to the same label-set hash, and resolving it returns the other set
issues.block: ### Two different attribute sets can intern to the same label-set hash, and resolving it returns the other set Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Different sets of event attributes can receive the same stored identifier. Looking up that identifier can return the first set's attributes instead of the attributes the caller saved. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 51) Found by: iteration 51 W57 case S3 (added after reading `InternLabelSet`; not a frozen prediction); [temporal_stats](models/temporal_stats/NOTES.md) `theorem_label_sets_collide` (for all keys and values); control `escape-values`. Related: [F-0509](#F-0509) (the same missing escaping makes some canonical texts non-JSON). Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-51/stats-observed-20261117T034349Z.json) `S3_quote`, `S4_fraction`; [binding](results/temporal_stats/20261117T040000Z-binding/receipt.json) `labels`). `intern_label_set({"a": 'x","b":"y'})` and `intern_label_set({"a": "x", "b": "y"})` both return `7725e82f…`, and resolving it answers `{"a":"x","b":"y"}`. `{"x": 0.5}` resolves to `{"x":.5}`, which `json.loads` refuses. Passing neighbors: the same keys in another order give one hash; an unknown hash resolves to `''`; a purge leaves interned sets. Expected: "Canonicalize, hash, and intern an attribute dict" (`_engine/temporal.py:835-846`); spec 204 FR-012 (the canonical form is JSON). A canonical form identifies its set: different sets must not share it. Observed: `InternLabelSet` writes each string value as `"` + value + `"` and each key as `"` + key + `"` without escaping (`TemporalIndex.cls:1365-1376`), so a quote inside a value can close the string and add keys; numbers are written in IRIS's canonical text. Consequence: two distinct attribute sets stored for retention share one hash, and the first one interned decides the resolved text; a caller that resolves the hash of the injected set gets the other set's attributes. Attribute values from users or upstream systems can trigger it. Repair proposal (not implemented): build the canonical text with JSON escaping and JSON number text (for example from the `%DynamicObject` with sorted keys), keeping existing hashes for texts that need no escaping. Preserve: key-order independence, type fidelity, append-only storage. Distinguishing case: the two sets above get different hashes. Governing statement: [temporal.labelset](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.labelset).

issues.title: A label set holding a nested object or list gets a new hash on every call, and different nested values can share one
issues.block: ### A label set holding a nested object or list gets a new hash on every call, and different nested values can share one Severity: Medium · Decision: Open Description: Attributes containing nested objects or lists are not given stable identifiers. Repeating the same input can create extra entries, while different inputs can lose their distinction when read back. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 53) Found by: independent review round 2 (session d548b72a, review of commit 8d8d9ae4, probe p51b; item M1). Formal: [temporal_stats](models/temporal_stats/NOTES.md) `theorem_nested_value_hash_per_call`, `theorem_nested_content_ignored` (general), valid neighbor `theorem_scalar_sets_idempotent`; control `nested-serialized-as-json`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, iteration 53 ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-53/temporal/temporal-observed-20261117T044748Z.json) `M1`; [binding](results/temporal_stats/20261117T045124Z-binding/receipt.json) `nested`). `intern_label_set({"k": {"b": 1}})` twice returns two hashes, resolving to `{"k":"10@%Library.DynamicObject"}` and `{"k":"12@%Library.DynamicObject"}`; a list (`[1, 2]`) and a mixed set (`{"a": "v", "z": [1]}`) behave the same with `%Library.DynamicArray`. `{"k": {}}` and `{"k": {"b": 1}}`, each interned first in its call, share one hash. Passing neighbors: a string, number, boolean or null value interns to one hash on every call and resolves to its JSON value. Not JSON: `InternLabelSet("{not json")` throws a parsing error rather than returning `""`. Expected: "Idempotent" and "Type fidelity" (`TemporalIndex.cls:1336-1338`); "Canonicalize, hash, and intern an attribute dict" (`_engine/temporal.py:835-846`); spec 204 FR-012 (the canonical form is JSON). Equal sets share one hash; different sets get different hashes. Observed: the value branch for anything other than a number, boolean or null concatenates `val` (`TemporalIndex.cls:1376-1378`). For an object or array `%Get` returns an object reference, whose text (`NN@%Library.DynamicObject`) depends on the call, not on the value. The stored text therefore has neither the nested content nor a stable form. Consequence: re-interning the same attributes yields a new hash each time, so callers that compare or group by hash split one set into many; each call appends another entry to the append-only `^KG("labelset")`, which no purge removes; and two different nested values can resolve to the same text, so the stored attributes are lost. Repair proposal (not implemented): write an object or array value as its canonical JSON (`val.%ToJSON()`, with sorted keys for objects), or refuse nested values with a clear error. Preserve: the hashes of sets with scalar values, key-order independence, append-only storage. Distinguishing case: `{"k": {"b": 1}}` twice gives one hash and resolves to `{"k":{"b":1}}`, and `{"k": {}}` gets a different hash (control `nested-serialized-as-json` checks the model's direction only; the proposal was not run on the product). Governing statement: [temporal.labelset](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.labelset).

issues.title: A millisecond-class edge is counted by the seconds readers' whole buckets although its time is outside the window
issues.block: ### A millisecond-class edge is counted by the seconds readers' whole buckets although its time is outside the window Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: The seconds-based and milliseconds-based temporal stores can contribute to the same aggregate buckets. When both are used in one graph, reports can count events outside the requested time window. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 53) Found by: independent review round 2 (session d548b72a, probe p51; item m1). Formal: [temporal_stats](models/temporal_stats/NOTES.md) `theorem_ms_edge_in_seconds_whole_bucket` (general, with the seconds-class neighbor); control `ms-buckets-apart`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, iteration 53 ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-53/temporal/temporal-observed-20261117T044748Z.json) `m1_*`; [binding](results/temporal_stats/20261117T045124Z-binding/receipt.json) `ms_in_sec_*`). `TemporalIndexMS.InsertEdge` at (T+50)·1000 ms, then the seconds readers over [T, T+299]: `get_temporal_aggregate` count 1, sum 2.0, one `get_bucket_groups` row, `get_edge_velocity` 1, `get_distinct_count` 11; while `get_edges_in_window` and `get_bucket_group_targets` over the same window answer nothing and the cut window [T, T+298] counts 0. The converse holds: the millisecond class's whole-bucket `GetAggregate` counts a seconds edge (1; cut window 0). Expected: aggregate and group reads answer exactly the requested window, and velocity counts whole buckets of the reader's own unit ([temporal.stats.window](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.stats.window)); the millisecond class is a "supported" separate unit (`TemporalIndexMS.cls:1-3`). Observed: both classes write the same `^KG("tagg")` and `^KG("bucket")` nodes keyed by bucket number, and x·1000 / 300000 equals x / 300 for every x, so a millisecond event lands in the seconds bucket of its seconds value. The raw store keeps the millisecond timestamp, so exact readers miss it. Consequence: in a graph written through both classes, whole-bucket statistics, groups, velocity and bursts mix units and disagree with the raw window. The Python engine calls only the seconds class, so this needs a direct ObjectScript caller of `TemporalIndexMS` on the same graph. Repair proposal (not implemented): keep the millisecond class's statistics under their own subscript (or refuse mixed units per graph). Preserve: each class's own whole/cut agreement. Distinguishing case: the event above counts 0 in the seconds whole bucket (control `ms-buckets-apart` checks the model's direction only). Governing statement: [temporal.stats.window](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.stats.window).

issues.title: backfill_temporal_rows answers the temporal triples it walked, not the rows it wrote, and setup reports that as edges given rows
issues.block: ### backfill_temporal_rows answers the temporal triples it walked, not the rows it wrote, and setup reports that as edges given rows Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: The temporal backfill reports how many relationships it visited rather than how many rows it created. Setup can claim that existing relationships were newly repaired, and a repeat run still reports work. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 53) Found by: iteration 53 Part B, frozen predictions BF1/BF2 (missed: the count), after reading `BackfillWalk`; [sql_procs](models/sql_procs/NOTES.md) `theorem_backfill_count_overstates` (for every state where one structural triple already has a row), `theorem_backfill_idempotent_same_count`, neighbor `theorem_backfill_count_exact_when_all_missing`; control `count-written-rows`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin ([probe](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-53/sqlprocs/sqlprocs-observed-20261117T050743Z.json) `backfill`; [binding](results/sql_procs/20261117T051429Z-binding/receipt.json) `bf_*`). With three structural temporal triples that already had marked rows, `SELECT Graph_KG.backfill_temporal_rows()` answered 3 and wrote nothing; again 3; after one row was deleted by SQL, 3 (one row written, marked); after an explicit edge with a timestamp, 4 (nothing written, the explicit row stays unmarked). The temporal-only predicate got no row and was not counted. Expected: ADMIN_GUIDE:413 documents setup's `temporal_rows_backfilled` as "the temporal edges it gave rows first"; setup stores this function's answer there (`schema.py:878-884`). Observed: `BackfillStructuralRows` returns `BackfillWalk(...).asserted`, which is incremented for every distinct structural triple it passes to `AssertTemporalRow`, whose `INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS` writes nothing for a triple that already has a row (`TemporalIndex.cls:232-300`, `Adjacency.cls` AssertTemporalRow). Consequence: an operator upgrading a namespace where most temporal edges already have rows (written with `graph=` before the index, or by an earlier backfill) is told that many edges were given rows; a re-run never reports 0. No row is written wrongly. Repair proposal (not implemented): count only the triples whose edge `INSERT` wrote a row (`%ROWCOUNT`), or rename the field to the triples checked. Preserve: idempotence, the skip of temporal-only predicates, the bounded memory. Distinguishing case: the second run above answers 0 (control `count-written-rows`). Governing statement: [temporal.structural.upgrade](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.structural.upgrade).

issues.title: An aggregate read with an empty source or predicate answers 0 when the window only cuts buckets and meets no edge
issues.block: ### An aggregate read with an empty source or predicate answers 0 when the window only cuts buckets and meets no edge Severity: Low · Decision: Open Description: An aggregate query with an empty source or predicate can return zero in a quiet window but fail in a busy one. Invalid arguments can therefore produce plausible results depending on the data. Run: Uplift 2026-11-17 (continuation, iteration 56) Found by: independent review round 3 (session c68a5c59, challenge to the round-2 m2 disposition), on the as-built observation of the iteration-53 probe (`m2_*`). Formal: [temporal_stats](models/temporal_stats/NOTES.md) `get_aggregate_keys`, `theorem_empty_key_quiet_cut_window_answers_zero` (general over every state, graph, key and window), neighbor `theorem_empty_key_raises_with_whole_bucket_or_event`, witness `theorem_empty_key_witness`; controls `empty-key-refused` (the repair) and `empty-key-never-raises`. Reproduced by: **E2E reproduced** on the run-isolated IRIS 2026.1 continuation fixture with the unchanged pin, iteration 56 ([binding](results/temporal_stats/20261117T065845Z-binding/receipt.json) cases `ek_*`). One edge `ek -P-> a` at T+50 in a fresh graph (T on a 300-second bucket boundary). `get_temporal_aggregate("", "P", "count", T+100, T+200)` answers `0`; `sum` answers `0.0`; `(ek, "", count)` and `("", "", count)` answer `0`. The same empty-source read over [T+10, T+100] (the edge's timestamp in the cut part) raises `RuntimeError: GetAggregate+32 ^KG("tout",g,T+50,"")`; over the whole bucket [T, T+299], and over the empty whole bucket [T+300, T+599], it raises `GetAggregate+13 ^KG("tagg",g,b,"")`. Neighbor: `(ek, "P", count)` answers 1 over [T+10, T+100] and 0 over [T+100, T+200]. Expected: an aggregate read needs a source and a predicate ([temporal.stats.window](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.stats.window)); no document promises an empty key as a wildcard (USER_GUIDE 1011-1027, the `get_temporal_aggregate` docstring), so an invalid call is refused, the same way whatever the window. Observed: `GetAggregate` (TemporalIndex.cls 1445-1493) reads `^KG("tagg", g, b, source, predicate, ...)` for a whole bucket and walks `^KG("tout", g, ts)` for a cut one, ordering `^KG("tout", g, ts, source, predicate, o)` at each timestamp present. With an empty source or predicate the first whole bucket or the first timestamp met raises ; a window that holds no whole bucket and meets no timestamp of its graph (any source's) reads nothing and returns count 0 and sum 0. The Python layer (`get_temporal_aggregate`, `iris_sql_store.get_temporal_aggregate`) passes "" through; for min, max and avg the empty answer then raises the store's `ValueError` (bug-tmp-009) as for any empty window. Consequence: a caller that passes an empty source by mistake gets a plausible 0 in quiet windows and a server error in busy ones; whether the call is valid depends on the data. Low: it needs an invalid argument, and the Python entry point does not offer an empty source as a feature. Repair proposal (not implemented): refuse an empty source or predicate in `get_temporal_aggregate` (Python) or at the top of `GetAggregate`, before any read. Preserve: every given-key read (all existing `agg_*` binding cases), the group and target reads where an empty predicate means every predicate. Distinguishing case: `ek_src_quiet_count` refused instead of 0 (control `empty-key-refused` is this repair in the model; it was not run against a patched product). Governing statement: [temporal.stats.window](../ontology/features/temporal.g5.md#temporal.stats.window).
